--- 帖子 #1 ---
THE CHART LOVERS METHOD I am starting this thread for those of us who love charts...watching them...studying them...analyzing them and of course, making money from them. My system is simple. It is a basic trend following one using the weekly, daily and H4 charts. I have made a goodly amount of money using this system, although I cannot say that I "discovered" it. I have traded forex for approximately 4 years, have lost more than a few thousand dollars, have responded to more than one $99 special offer for the holy grail. I have followed several threads on FF, some with more success than others, have downloaded about every indicator known to man. But I did not start making real money until I deleted all the indicators (except one) and started drawing trendlines and support/resistance levels. I do not have my ego involved in this thread, as I have noticed many "thread starters" do. I have been a successful attorney for many years and have no need to prove anything to either myself or to others. I do believe in helping others though, and can think of no better way than by sharing my little knowledge with other like minded traders, hoping that we all become even more successful together. I post on two other forums on FF and have had many traders ask about my trading and charts...so many in fact, that I thought it was a good time to set the method down once and for all so that I would no longer have to individually respond to private messages and emails, regarding same. So let's get going: TRADE ANY MARKET SESSION THAT MAKES SENSE FOR YOUR LIFESTYLE. DON'T WORRY ABOUT WHICH MARKET IS OPEN, WHICH IS CLOSED. 1. The Three Tap Trade (3 Tap H4) A. Chart Set Up Save as template: H4 candlestick chart with period separators . Add to this chart a standard RSI indicator set with period (3). That's it...all there is to it! See the first chart below. It is the Almost Naked chart which is the foundation of all of the trading set-ups which I will discuss below. B. Check Trend on Weekly, Daily, and H4 Charts This is the most important part of this method. All three (3) timeframes (TFs) must be in agreement (confirmation) on direction. Perhaps, the easiest way to do this is to attach the RSI Arrow Indicator to your charts. The indicator and directions can be found here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost.php?p=4127792 It is important that you develop the ability to confirm the RSI directions without using an indicator because you should visually verify the positioning of the RSI on the H4, Daily, and Weekly charts before entering a trade. Scan through any or all pairs you wish to trade and jot down only those which have confirmation of direction on all three TFs. Do this by observing the RSI . THINK ABOUT THE FACE OF A CLOCK For LONG: RSI should be pointing between 12:00 AND 2:00 O'CLOCK . 3:00 is neutral. For SHORT: RSI should be pointing between 4:00 and 6:00 O'CLOCK . Again, 3:00 is neutral NOTICE ON THE CHART BELOW THAT THE DIRECTION IS DOWN, OR SHORT. (RSI IS BETWEEN 4:00 AND 5:00 O'CLOCK) Now look at the most recent price action (PA).on the chart below. Notice that it is also short. This will be a pair "of interest" if and only if the direction on the daily and weekly charts confirm the H4 chart direction. C. Concentrating only on those pairs with trend confirmation and one at a time: On H4 chart take a long look at what you see. You know the direction you are looking for from your previous scan of the pairs. (Marking with an arrow helps give a quick reference to direction.) Draw trendlines (TLs) connecting bottoms for LONGS and connecting tops for SHORTS. NOTICE ON RECENT CHART #2 BELOW - USDCHF D. Entry Here is where patience comes in. Enter in designated direction only after PA has tapped the trendline 3 times (Knock three times on the...oh well). This "refinement" is David's idea on Trendline Scalping thread....thanks David. NOTICE ON CHART #2 BELOW - USDCHF... THAT IT TOOK 9 CANDLES (36 HOURS) FOR THE THIRD TAP! THAT'S PATIENCE, BUDDY!...BUT LOOK AT THE PAYOFF.. E. Take Profits (TP) and Stop Losses (SL) You can place set TP and SL if you are more comfortable with that. I use support and resistence levels for both. Remember that H4 and larger TFs must have more breathing room, so do not place SL too tightly. Let me know if anything needs further explanation. F. Recently Asked Questions 10/27/2010 Q: Does one wait for the close of the 3rd tap candle before entering or enter immediately?. A: When desired trade is long and 3rd tap candle is long (green on my charts), enter immediately. When desired trade is short and 3rd tap candle is short (red on my charts), enter immediately, because both a set-up and a trigger has occurred in each of these scenarios. Q: I notice that usually when the 3rd tap occurs, the RSI is not supporting the direction of the desired trade. Is it important that the H4 RSI support the direction of the weekly and daily RSI at this point? A: It is important that the H4 RSI the daily and weekly RSIs show the same direction before entering the trade. Remember there is a difference between a trade set-up and a trade trigger. The set-up is the 3 taps, the trigger is PA in the right direction . This is consistent with the question above. Q: Do you use M30 or M15 charts on the 3 tap trades? A: Although I don't use shorter time frames (TFs) for 3 tap trades, some traders have indicated to me that they use these TFs to observe price action (PA) before entry. I do use the TFs for breakout trades (BO), discussed below. Another trade set-up for our trading arsenal-- BELOW: 2. The H1 4 Candle Breakout Trade (H1 4C BO) I have added a new trade set-up to the 3 tap trade discussed above. It works hand and hand with the 3 tap trade. Often we can see PA going in one direction and want to get in, but need a logical way to do it. Certainly 3 tap is one way, but what if you do not see a good 3 tap set-up on the H4 chart? Then move to the H1 chart and take a look . The H1 4 candle breakout set-up: A. This is a price action (PA) trade and the weekly RSI direction does not need to match the direction of the trade. Because this is considered a "fast" trade...meaning over in a few hours at the longest...only the H4 and H1 candles need to confirm direction, but they will do that if PA moves in the desired direction. B. You will be looking at the bodies of the first four H1 candles of a new trading day...disregard the tails (wicks)....whenever that is for you. That is one reason period seperators need to be placed on the chart. C. Place horizontal lines at the highest high of these four candles' bodies (not including the tails, if any) and the lowest low of these four candles' bodies , again, disregard the tails. These lines are really just R/S lines. D. Wait for a breakout in the direction of the bias. I sometimes place a pending order below/above a R/S line before I go to bed. E. Enter from the M15 chart, when at least one candle has completely cleared the R/S line in the desired direction. The entry takes discretion, as the quality of the candles is important to observe. NOTE: You can set this up several hours after the fourth candle that you are observing. For example: My first four candles are from 2:00 pm - 6:00 pm. I may not get to the set-up until 8 or 9 p.m. That is ok, in fact, that gives time to observe PA. Do verify the directional bias again, however. PLEASE SEE POSTS #1029 - 1032 ON PAGE 69 FOR COMMENTARY AND CHART EXAMPLES 3. Scrutch's Method of Finding A++ and A+++ Trades 11/24/2010 Please don't use Scrutch's screening of trades until you are totally familiar and comfortable with the 3 Tap H4 trade and the H1 4C BO trading systems. Q: Do you consider an A++ trade one in which both setups occur on the same pair? A : Yes, both setups need to be in agreement for an A++ trade. If you only have one of the two setups and the RSI's are in agreement, I consider that to be an A+ trade. When they happen together, the odds of a great trade increase dramaticaly. I don't take these just any time that both conditions are true. I , want to see the H4-3T happen first, most likely the RSI's wont be in total agreement at that time. Then , I want to see the breakout happen within a few hours, two or three at the most, with four hours maximum. After four hours I feel that the real advantage has expired. Not that it will not or could not still be a very nice trade, just that it no longer has the force of the dual confirmation behind it. The CADJPY breakout occured about two and a half hours after the H4-3T. The USDCAD breakout occured about three hours after the H4-3T. For either of these trades I'm looking at the M15 chart for the breakout confirmation, and yes price action needs to reflect the momentum as well. IF, the H4-3T setup occurs and the H1-4C-BO setup occurs in thirty minutes or less, then... , I think that would be an A+++ trade. When this happens I'm usually looking at a M5 chart for entry because I want to get in as early as I can...depending again on price action. Q : Do you limit the number of pairs you look at and trade? A : I watch the majors mostly but also keep an eye on the others as well. To keep a close watch on them all is a bit daunting but it's doable becaue of the time frame involved. I do pay close attention to the spread, which influences whether I want to take the trade or not. If the spread is large, then I'll just pass on the trade. I draw all potential H4-3T's that I see and adjust them as the market moves, regardless of the RSI's. At times I'll have two H4-3T's drawn, a bullish and a bearish. Then I adjust them as the market dictates direction. I draw all the H1-4C-BO's at the close of the fourth hourly bar from period separator to period separator. At times I will start drawing these sooner...depends on what the RSI's are showing me. 4. Indicators (Optional) RSI Arrow Indicators http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost.php?p=4127792 - to read explanation and download to chart . 5. New Daily Entry (MONEYTREE) added May 18, 2011 In commemoration of reaching 1000 pages and while waiting for the paint dryingly boring monthly chart trades, I have been working on a new entry on the daily charts that seems to be working very well. It is quite simple. 1. There must be directional confirmation on both the weekly and daily RSI . If monthly also, the better, but not necessary. 2. Enter using either the H1 4C BO entry or 3 Tap entry or other entry of your choice in the direction of the RSI within the first few hours of the beginning of your new daily candle, if possible (whatever time of day that is for you), say within the first 6 hours (although 6 is arbitrary). The point is, we are trying to capture as much of the full day as is possible. 3. Immediately place a 30 pip SL. Then forget about it. 5. Next day at around the same time check the trade. It will have done one of 3 things: a) hit the SL, b) taken off, or c) ranged around. If: a) Oh, well...go to the next trade; b) Great, decide whether to TP or add a position if direction continues; c) Wait it out, That's all there is to it. Rinse and Repeat.... --- 帖子 #140 ---
Hi Tim... It's not "check the trend on 3 TFs then check the RSI". Checking the RSI on 3 different TFs is just a quick and simple way to confirm direction of trend, or no definite trend when the TFs differ. Once we start finding trends in the direction we are looking for, because the RSI scan indicated the direction, we look for the triple taps. Notice that really until Wednesday of this week, there were few discernable trends, thus we were looking at breakout trading....one type of trading done were trends are not established.

--- 帖子 #175 ---
2 O'clock means the angle of your hour hand when looking at a clock when it strikes 2:00. In other words, the angle of 30 degrees. 1 O'clock would be 60 degrees, and 12 O'clock would be 90 degrees. Consider 3 O'clock to be 0 degrees. 4 O'clock would be -30, 5 O'clock would be -60 degrees, and 6 O'clock would be -90 degrees ... hope that is clear.

--- 帖子 #257 ---
Another pretty obvious question here: When the third tap happens, price action will always be against the trend, by definition. For example, on a long trade, the trendline is drawn from low to low, and the price has to come down to hit for the third time. It's also pretty clear from some of these examples that you will wait before jumping in, at least on some of these trades. If the price continues to march through the line, you bail on the trade. But how much does it have to move in your favor before you decide to take it? (In this regard, your approach seems different from David's. As I understand it, he jumps on a third tap at the moment it hits. And I think there are other people who may wait for the candle to close. But I don't think you are doing either of those necessarily.)

--- 帖子 #260 ---
Yes, that is correct: third tap is against the trend. You can call it a retrace, a pullback, an attempt to break through the TL.---it's all those things. If because of my schedule, I come to a potential trade at the time of the 3rd tap, I will wait to see if PA breaks through the TL or heads back into the trend direction. If I come to a potential trade after the 3rd tap, then my analysis is different: how many candles ago was the tap? is there room to travel (reasonable R/S levels above and below)? are all TF trends still in confirmation?

I still use the triple hit method as presented by lawgirl ... However, if I see a channel as well, then the more reason I think that the triple hit will hold. --- 帖子 #338 ---
JG, I do not believe that this system is really a good newbie system. I think that even though it is simple, it is really an advanced system of trading. And one reason is that there will always be vagueness, because there are no exact numbers involved..only areas i.e. areas of support, areas of resistence etc. Another reason I believe this is a better system for advanced traders is that we are really trading three different styles, based on trend and PA alone. 1. 3 tap system - the easiest. Basically find the trend. Look for taps. 2. Breakout system - when there are no discernable trends. The first three days of this week were like this on many pairs. 3. Channel Trading - knowing the trend, but trading the bounces off of trend channels. The hardest and riskiest of the three, in my opinion, because countertrend trades are involved. There are whole threads and indeed books written on each of these styles of trading. We are using them interchangably because we are "reading the charts" and can determine what type of market we are in. And we can determine what type of trade is called for. We can also determine when a pair doesn't fit into any of our trade types and move on to another pair. This is advanced trading.

I want to show you guys a trade I took last night that gave me 25 pips. This is an extension of my post # 338 above, a Breakout trade with a twist.. From my scan yesterday, I knew this pair had a short directional bias. I confirmed this bias before I set up the trade. H4 chart below I could not find a valid 3 tap entry on the H4 chart. --- 帖子 #382 ---
I'm done until Sunday afternoon. It has been an interesting week. Very different from the week before, when pairs were trending more (better?). But I met my goal and hope everyone else did too, even though I believe I had to work alot harder. If you have a chance to study charts, pick one or two of the major pairs and go back through the last week and look for patterns of 3 taps, breakouts and channel trades. Note the ones that worked out and, just as importantly, the ones which did not. Note end of month directional bias of the pairs you are studying, mark S/R levels and jot down what you believe, based on PA and trend direction, the trend will do. Will it continue? Pullback?.. Of course, we have no control over trend continuation, but it is surprising how often it does continue. Remember too, that the same analysis is used when looking at the monthly charts...i.e. trading within a range (take a look at USDCAD..trading within a range for the last 10 months!), trending, breaking out. Get some rest, spend time with your families..see you back on Sunday afternoon.

--- 帖子 #530 ---
hi ballo, just check page no 1 " 2. Check Trend on Weekly, Daily, and H4 Charts This is the most important part of this method. All three (3) timeframes (TFs) must be in agreement (confirmation) on direction. Scan through any or all pairs you wish to trade and jot down only those which have confirmation of direction on all three TFs. Do this by observing the RSI . For LONG: RSI should be pointing between 12:00 and 2:00 . 3:00 is neutral. For SHORT: RSI should be pointing between 4:00 and 6:00 . Again, 3:00 is neutral NOTICE ON THE CHART BELOW THAT THE DIRECTION IS DOWN, OR SHORT. (RSI IS BETWEEN 4:00 AND 5:00 O'CLOCK) Now look at the most recent price action (PA).on the chart below Notice that it is also short. This will be a pair "of interest" if and only if the direction on the daily and weekly charts confirm the H4 chart direction. enclosure the sample of chart ecad wktf, D1 and 4Hr and this is what i understand of this method only taken the trade if the three tf with the same direction or close above 50 level of rsi indicator cheers

hi all, i have been following this and i still do have problems regarding the RSI direction although i read thru the thread again n again.. can any helpful give advice on this? 1. regarding the RSI for the 3 tap trade, lawgirl mentioned that all RSI must be pointing the same way as the direction u trade. This means that we can trade against the trend(which is the PA forming HH/HL, in the case of uptrend), as long as the RSI is in tandem, which means we can short on an uptrend(like channel trade)??? 2. about taking the trade, for a 3 tap trade to occur, we should enter the trade on the third tap, however, on the 3rd tap on the TL, the RSI will definitely be pointing at a different direction as the daily and weekly RSI, since it is a pullback. So we do not take a trade on the 3rd tap, but wait for the RSI on the 4hr to turn to our desired direction, which is same as the daily and weekly RSi. Hence, we will never enter right on the 3rd tap on the TL. thx so much for ur help in advance.

Maybe I am confused, but it seems the "50" level is meaningless. The attached Weekly chart shows that RSI can be up or down when it is either above or below the "50" mark. And it shows that an "up" when it is above the "50" mark can be as significant as an "up" when it is below the "50" mark. And it is the same for a "down"....whether RSI is above or below the "50", a "down" can be equally significant. So it seems that the direction the Weekly RSI is pointing, up (12 o'clock to 2 o'clock) or down (4 o'clock to 6 o'clock), is more important than if this action is taking place above or below the "50" level. And this conclusion may be especially valid if we seek only direction from the Weekly RSI because we are seeking entry on H4. I mean (unless I am missing something here) a final Weekly RSI "up" above the "50" mark can still yield a good move upwards as seen from the perspective of H4. --- 帖子 #706 ---
No, no--you are making this far too difficult. TLs are the last thing to do. Try this order of doing things.. 1. have you template on the screen with the first pair that your broker has displayed on "Market Watch" ( your template should look something like the chart on p.1 of this thread.) Start off with weekly . Look at RSI direction and glance at PA (red and green candles really help) Click daily , then H4 . Say outloud (No, I'm not kidding!) as you go to each TF: "up, up, down (or whatever) 2. Go to the next pair on Market Watch by dragging the pair over to the chart on the screen. Starting at weekly again saying outloud: "down, up, down" (whatever the direction) 3. Go to the next pair by dragging over to the chart and start at weekly again: this time, let's say it: "up, up, up" Write this pair down on a piece of paper. ( I use a notebook so I don't have a million scrapes of paper around.) After doing this for all the pairs you are interested in..go back to each one and look for trends on the H4 chart and draw your TLs. I make notes for myself on the chart so that I can remember what I am looking for when I go back through for review. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #846 ---
If you want to catch a setup that someone else has reported, but your chart isn't on the same timeframe as theirs, there is an alternative. All you need to do is back up to the 1H chart, zoom out, and look for the same set-up. Every time a four hour candle opens, a one hour candle also opens. Thus, its possible to get a picture of what someone is talking about on the H1 charts, even if its not a perfect solution. There are times when it might be a better solution than missing a promising trade.

--- 帖子 #847 ---
As I understand it, the RSI simply does not matter as much for breakout trades. Here, you have a possible breakout trade, and a possible triple tap at once. The nicest thing would be for price to break south. Thus your TT and Breakout would give you two reasons for entering the same trade. In that case, your question doesn't matter. If price breaks north, your TT setup was false (and its not really part of this system since you only have two of the three TFs in your favor). But it might still be a breakout worth taking.

--- 帖子 #848 ---
The topic is "3 Taps on H4". And an alternatiave of using a condensed H1 to show same as H4 is on the table. Personally, I like it. The H1 is universal for all broker servers. I propose another consideration; time. Look at the attached H1 chart. Well, first let me say that of the W, D and H4, only the RSI on the W has not rolled over down. Ok, back to H1. The TL might seem to be the area to anticipate going short. But if you look closely you will see verical time lines in the background that bracket prime market trading hours. So what? Well, as we approach the prime hours, PA may indeed hit the TL. But prime hours traders may also pump PA up past the TL! Why? If PA is destined to drop, the PPMs could always pump it high first to improve taking on positions before the drop! So what? If PA breaks up thru TL, some might shelve the thought of going short and this method, and instead go long on a "H1 breakout" long trade. And this might not work out well if the pump is preparatory for a huge drop, which you have taken your eyes off of. And such could happen with GU. Note that between 6 and 9 hours from now there are 3 high impact releases. This is the stuff that can cause preparatory "reverse" drives and whipsaws....heck, anything could happen! In conclusion, taking "time" into account with this method might be an enhancement. Unfortunately, time lines get scrunched up on H4....another reason to consider the H1 alternative.

I much prefer S/R levels to diagonal lines. In my experience the horizontal S/R lines are honored by PA far more often than are TLs. When we look for 3 tap H4 trades with the TLs, that is exactly what we are doing with the TFs confirmation..trying to find the trend bias and using it to our advantage, or putting the trade in our favor, as you said. This week, however, PA has defied us more often than not.

--- 帖子 #865 ---
I was probably confusing in my earlier response to siam. A H1 breakout is based on the first four H1 candles of a new trading day. You can see from the charts I post where my new day is..at the dotted period separators. Yours may look somewhat different. A horizontal line is drawn at the high of the four candles and at the low of the four candles. This creates a 4 candle "ditch". After finding the directional bias, its a waiting game for a PA breakout in the anticipated direction. Sometimes the direction changes and the breakout is in the opposite direction. In that case, verify direction on other TFs and roll with it. Another horizontal ditch, which is one of my favorites is a consolidation ditch..where PA trades for hours, sometimes days withing the horizontal lines (S/R). Breakouts occur the same way.

--- 帖子 #1003 ---
I trade both live and demo, using two separate computers and three screens. Almost every live trade I make, is set up on the demo screen first. I do no trade set-ups on the "live" computer. My "live" computer is used solely to take trades, not to monitor them. I monitor from the demo screen only...place R/S levels, TLs etc. As soon as a demo trade is doing what it is "supposed" to do, I go live. A few pips may be missed, but not enough to notice.

Just works best for me, that's all. Not necessarily suggesting that it would for others.

--- 帖子 #1043 ---
Hi Cencored..the 3 tap TL does not have to be accurately tapped by the wicks, they can be poking through somewhat. The main thing is PA at the 3rd tap point. What is it doing? You are correct, if I don't see a trade on H4, I will look for one on H1. The H1 4 candle breakout set-up: *****NOW POSTED ON PAGE 1******* 1. Find the directional bias on weekly, daily, H4. All must match at the time of set-up. 2. You will be looking at the first four H1 candles of a new trading day...whenever that is for you. That is why period seperators need to be placed on the chart. 2. Place horizontal lines at the highest high of these four candles and the lowest low of these four candles. These are really just R/S lines. (see my posted chart above, blue area). 3. Wait for a breakout in the direction of the bias. I often place a pending order below/above a R/S line before I go to bed. NOTE: You can set this up several hours after the fourth candle that you are observing. For example: My first four candles are from 2:00 pm - 6:00 pm. I may not get to the set-up until 8 or 9 p.m. That is ok, in fact, that gives time to observe PA. Do verify the directional bias again, however. It is extremely simple, yet extremely profitable. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #1175 ---
Glad to have you here lookas. Of course, one can have any pair they like on the watch list. But my initial scan is to narrow down that list, in other words, I don't even look at a pair that, at the time I scan them, does not conform on all time frames. THEN I go back to each pair individually and "see what I can see" i.e. look for set-ups. Sometimes at this point, the trade has been missed, sometimes it is just starting, sometimes there is no discernable trade. I don't generally care which pair/s I trade. If you are watching a particular pair, however, yes it is possible to have H4 in a countertrend as you are watching for that 3rd tap. Hope this makes sense, it is the middle of the night for me...

--- 帖子 #1257 ---
Indeed! Precisely what they don't need, LG. At their stage, they desperately need "fundamentally simple" as their prime "indicator," at this point. Call it the FS indicator, if you will. Remember, what it was like when you were a Nube. All that minutia to wade through, all those TA missiles being launched at you faster than you can blink. That's simply too much for the Nube to consuming all at once. Not because Elliot, Gann, Gartley, Pesavento, or Millard, offered us rocket science, they not attempt to consume it all at once, but merely because one of the very first things the Nube needs is to develop at least a base level of patience and confidence. And, that is precisely what a thread like this can teach the Nube, or even the trader who feels they lost their "touch." All advanced concepts in trading (or, life for that matter) are positioned upon fundamental concepts. Which is why being forced to wait on the 3rd wave (you call them Taps), will give them training for learning more about market waves and market cycles, which is a huge topic in and of itself - unless the Nube already possesses a technical mindset/background (mathematics, engineering, physics, EECS, etc.). Having to wait on the individual cycles, helps to reduce the ego. Been the mentor before, so I can appreciate what you are doing here with these guys. I think you are doing the right thing with this thread. Keep up the good work and I may even drop back by to explain the WHY behind the H1 Four Hour Break-Out. We know it happens, but many (most) don't really know why it happens. There is a technical principle that explains this particular phase of any currency pair's "session life-cycle" which causes the range to occur. In fact, it happens in many other places other than the first four hours of the new daily session. And, here's the really cool part - the entry into and duration of, that particular phase of the pair's session life-cycle, can even be predicted before it happens. --- 帖子 #1392 ---
Thanks for your lovely greeting; this time the honour and good fortune are all mine. Guys, is it just my perception or has the quality of threads here at FF improved dramatically in recent months. It seems to me that every couple of weeks or so, someone is stepping forward with a system they are trading successfully already, rather than an idea he or she is hoping to develop with help from more experienced traders. These days, there seem to be far fewer systems requiring 14 pretty-coloured thingies to line up before a trade is triggered. Granted, not all systems suit traders but with the quality of what is on offer, most of us should be able to find something. I like David's 4H trendline scalping system. I like Lawgirl's system still more. I do not immediately see a way to automate it; I tried an automation of David's system and it works reasonably well but there was always a problem with precisely identifying appropriate taps, or legs as D calls them. Here, we have the added difficulty of the angle of ascent/descent of the Rsi. This will not stop me thinking about possible automation and would be happy to take pm's from people with ideas about how to measure it. Not here, please, as this would clutter up what is a beautifully clear thread. I attach a few goodies: Lawgirl's Trendline Buy/Sell ea's. These are not robot traders of the kind I usually write. They are for use when traders have identified the first two trendline taps and are awaiting the third. In a downtrend, you will drag the Sell ea onto the chart; it will wait until the market achieves the third tap and enter the trade for you, to save you possibly missing it through not being at the computer. The ea will attempt to send the trade and then suspend itself. There is a 'safety feature in the form of a prompt for confirmation when you drag the ea onto the chart. This prompt also appears if your platform is closed and restarted for any reason; this is to ensure the ea does not inadvertently send the trade twice before you have the chance to remove it. One significant input is TrendLineName. This defaults to 'T' and has to be the same name as that of the trendline you are using to trigger the trade; easiest is to leave the default in place and change the name of your trendline. The ea will whinge at you if it does not find an appropriately-named trendline. Another input to understand is CriminalIsECN. Set this to 'true' if your criminal insists on two-stage order-sending. Included are opportunities to use Atr to decide on a tp and trading hours limitations, should you want them. Alternatively, the ea can be told to send default tp/sl that you can adjust once the trade has triggered. Those of you familiar with Nanningbob's V5 and the robots developed to trade his system, and my development of The Beast, will be familiar with Recovery; this is what ReEntryLinePips and ReEntryLineColour are all about; when it sends a trade, the ea will draw the ReEntry line for us. I doubt I am alone in contemplating whether Recovery can be of benefit here. Here is an invaluable tool when studying the charts. Flicking from chart to chart, or from tf to tf, there can be a delay before the platform receives a tick that updates the display. Unxip mt4.ticker.exe to your desktop and run it every time you want to run through the charts to check on setups/triggers etc. It sends a tick to your platform every half-second or so and keeps the charts up to date as you look through them. It is a bit of a resource hog, so I only have it running when I need it.

--- 帖子 #1455 ---
The attached is an EA and so goes in your Expert Advisors folder. It attempts to give an at-a-glance view of the trending status of the pairs you wish to trade. The 'Trend' col will show up/down if all three tf Rsi's are heading in the same direction. If not, it will show 'flat'. There are a few things to consider: We are using Rsi in this system as a visual aid - the actual value has no significance. This cannot be coded, so a robot has to have set parameters to work within. LookBackCandles tells it how far back in time to go to compare Rsi now with Rsi then . I thought we might need to look back a few candles to get a direction, but was forgetting that Rsi(3) is highly sensitive to movement, and the default of 1 appears ok. People can experiment. Does there need to be x points separation between Rsi now and Rsi then .I originally thought that there should, hence the MinimumValueChange input. This turned out not to be especially important and the default of 1 appears to work OK. I suggest that people go to the relevant chart if both the D1 and W1 line up, even if the H4 does not. The H4 is the trigger, so going in the 'wrong' direction may simply indicate a retrace that will lead eventually to a tap of the trendline. Bearing 3) in mind, would people like me to remove the H4 from the trend-spotting decision process and use only the two higher tf's? I only came across this thread on Thursday, and will be guided by lg and the more experienced traders. So, bung the ea on a chart and see if it needs tweaking. To save hammering our processors, I have coded the bot to check in with Rsi every five minutes instead of every tick.

--- 帖子 #1464 ---
Having a hard and fast pip goal is always flawed, no matter which strategy IMO. Markets are dynamic, so simply take what the market gives you. E.g. if you see a bottom forming in the RSI indicator, take your profit. If you see reversal candles (dojis, inside bars, outside bars, long bars, etc.) or previous S/R (esp. on h4) take your profit. Or at least take half and set your SL to BE. There are no hard and fast rules in Forex. Trade what you see - as Lawgirl said it.

--- 帖子 #1465 ---
I have just been forced to work out how to send emails from within an EA, by a pal for whom I am doing some coding. It turns out to be ridiculously simple, so I have added the function here. This ea should now send you an email alert when it detects a change from a flat to a trending market. To enable this feature: leave the AlertByEmail input at its default of 'true' in your platform, go to Tools|Options|Email and set up your email thingies. A couple of curiosities are emerging with the ea. I sometimes find I have to click on the chart to achieve a display when I drag it onto a chart. I have no idea why. Changing the PairsToTrade input does not appear to work whilst the ea is running - it makes my display disappear completely. Changing the input involves 4 stages: call up the ea's Inputs window and save your existing set file make your changes re-save the set file re-drag the robot onto the chart, loading it with your new set file A bit of a faff, I know, but not as though we have to do this 15 times a day. I just had another idea and have added two new inputs: TrendRequiresAllThree and TrendRequiresOnlyHtf TrendRequiresAllThree requires all tf Rsi's to be pointing in the right direction before alerting us to a trend change TrendRequiresOnlyHtf requires only the D1 and W1 to be pointing in the right direction before alerting us to a trend change I do not know which setting is the best to use as I have not sufficient experience with the system. Any advice, lg?

I am trying to establish a relationship with the monthly direction after a certain number of trading day and the daily direction. --- 帖子 #1512 ---
I try hard not to ever let a winning trade turn into a loser. Happens sometimes, but not often. This is about the only time I have harsh words about myself, with myself...when this happens. I generally never let a trade hit my SL either. That's because my SLs are often very unrealistic. I exit from the same TF on which I took my set-up. That is, if it was a H4 set-up I will exit on an H4 candle PA change or color change. If a daily set-up, then I will exit on a daily change of PA and/or candle color change, etc. I only use a lower TF like 15M to enter a H1 4 candle BO trade...and only for entry, not for exit.

--- 帖子 #1516 ---
I will exit if PA reverses. A stall can just be a "breather" before another good move. That is one reason I do not like to move to a smaller TF for exit when I took the trade on a longer TF. What is really a breather or stall on the larger TF can look like a reversal on the shorter TF. So I view it as mixing apples and oranges. But this is where personal judgment comes in. Don't sit and watch a trade turn around thinking it will come back to you...generally it does not. I would like to hear more about how you took a larger loss than you needed to.

--- 帖子 #1568 ---
Hi Lawgirl, Following your recent posts I have seen you mention if there was any correlation between weekly and monthly charts. Having run a few extensive tests from this years data it provides interesting results: Weekly/Monthly Correlation It appears that if price is above the opening price for the month, two weeks into the month it will stay above the open price and vise versa, however this does not indicate that half way through the month it will continue in the direction of the trend for example, price might be 200 pips above the open price but fall to only being 20 pips above the open price by the end of the month. The only month where this corrolation did not apply was Janauary, which is always a odd month! Also during my testing I also found that the opening price for the week is always a nice price to take note of as often price comes to retest this area and can provide some nice entries. Todays Trading It looks like today was an interesting day for trading, im glad people managed to grab some pips, however my trading strategy usually keeps me out of trading Mondays so I am looking forward to getting stuck in tomorrow. Many Thanks, TheDell

I am ever so pleased to see the Rsi trend ea proving useful. For sure, it is a boon to me. This is just to remind everyone not to rely on it; it provides a good warning that a tradable trend might be in place but that is all. When it presents a trend signal, this still needs checking manually for accuracy. lg's use of Rsi is a visual thingy. Visual thingies cannot be coded into ea's, so it has to have certain assumptions programmed into it. There are times when these will be false. It is pretty good, but not perfect so bear this in mind.

--- 帖子 #1651 ---
whatfx...The 4 and 6 are the imaginary numerals on a clock face. The slope needs to be somewhere in between the 4 and 6 to be a strong down move, just a bit past the 3 but not yet pointing at the 4 would be considered a weak down. Just a bit on either side of the 3 or pointing right at the 3 would be considered neutral or flat. The slope is the only thing this methodology takes into consideration, the RSI values are meaningless with this method. You could have two bars reading 97.5 or 12.25...either one would reflect a neutral reading as the slope would be horizontal, towards 3 if you will. If two consecitive bars have the same RSI value then the slope will be horizontal , regarless of what the value is. Please look at the image. USD news...Treasury Sec Geithner Speaks AUD news...Monetary Policy Meeting Minutes in a couple of hours.

--- 帖子 #1709 ---
The broker time only affects the 4 hr candles, not the daily, weekly, 60 min etc. If 4 hr candle opens when London opens, in theory, it more clearly reflects what is happening right then .. if it opens 2 hours before or 2 hours after London, its shape 'could' give an erroneous impression of where price is headed. London is the major forex market so if you are watching 4h candles, it may be better to have them open when London opens. I have been told this by more experienced traders, I am not entirely sure how it works out in real time, but I have noticed over the past few days that some people see a 3-tap on their 4h chart where others do not .. and this depends on when their 4 hr candles open &amp; close. I'm still experimenting to see if having 4h candles in sync with LO makes a significant difference or not... Hope that clears it up.

--- 帖子 #1759 ---
The entry is exactly the same on a daily as on a H4 chart. But you need to know what time your daily candle starts. For example for me, it is 2:00 pm, so if I have my TL drawn and already have two taps, and assuming RSI conformation, I am going to try to be around to see what happens at the open of the next daily candle. If I don't have the third tap within a few hours, I would assume I am not going to get it that day and wait for the next day...requires lots of patience, but often worth it.

--- 帖子 #1823 ---
Glad you are getting something out of this thread, wilk. You will always have winners and losers, but you know that. When we talk about PA, yes we are talking about long and short candles..mine are red and green. If you have a 3rd tap for a short and the candle is long (green), wait for the next candle for PA to start down (turn red). If the 3rd tap for a short is short (red), generally you do not have to wait for the next candle to enter. Of course the opposite for a long trade. A lot depends on when you "arrive" at the 3 tap.

--- 帖子 #1830 ---
That is correct, the 3rd tap is really a retracement, wave, pullback, whatever you want to call it, before a continuation in the desired direction. The 3rd tap does not have to be green, it could be a tap with a long tail, but if it is green, we want to wait for the next candle to see if the 3rd tap will "hold" or if PA is going to shot through it. But yes, sometimes we get to a chart after the 3rd tap but while there is still a valid trade. That is a judgement call. I generally will not take a trade if 3rd tap occurred hours before.

--- 帖子 #1924 ---
Hi all, First, please forgive me as I must admit I hadn't enough time to read all the thread before posting. I wanted to share one way of trading I use from time to time. I'm a noob so I can make mistake and hopefully, experienced traders will help to improve the method. The advantage of the method is it works with (almost) no indicators. Just a chart and your eyes to spot about 10-15 setups per day per pair. The win ratio is impressive after a few hours of training (so you can easily spot bad setups before you enter them). The bad news is it's stressful and requires to monitor your chart every second. First, the pinbars you want to trade : Pin Bars I like to trade those on M1 chart, there's more setups and trades are usually short (a few minutes). Attached chart shows 18 possible setups in a 6-7 hours time frame. Pre-requisites : - Low spread broker (you can only trade M1 with less than 2 pips spread). - Fast execution of orders on broker's side. Below 1 second is fine. Indicators : - There's really only one helpful indicator : Better Volume ( doc here and here , indicator here ). - You can also see if the KPI attached helps. It shows the buying/selling pressure on each candle. It's far from mandatory. All other indicators are useless, they all tell you about the past. You don't care about what happened in the past, you can see it on the chart ! You want to know about the future. The pinbars are all about that. Entry rules : - Youy're looking for good shaped pinbars. The wick should be more than 2/3 of the candle. 75-90% wicks are the best setups, showing a strong rejection and so a stronger move in the opposite direction. - Previous bar wick is preferably short. Previous bar high is no more than half of the pinbar. The lower, the better. - Now, the pinbar closed and the next bar opened. Same rules apply : if the price goes too high in the pinbar direction : forget the setup. If the price continues to move in your direction, you enter the trade just at the pinbar's low. - See setup #15 on the chart as a perfect one : this is exactly what you are looking for. - For more security, you could want to play only in the trend direction. In this case, use M15 to find short term trend and confirm at H1 or H4. Exit rules : - Stop loss : at the opposite end of the pinbar. The longer the pinbar, the larger your stop. But longer pinbars give better odds to your trade, so it's fine. - In all cases, no fixed TP : you stay in the trade as long as the price is going straight in your direction ! - When you're 5 pips positive, move sl to break-even. - Option 1 : close the trade as soon the price begins to move against you, whatever the profit. This is conservative option, less risks, less pips ! - Option 2 : if applicable, you can use a down trend line that starts at the pinbar. When the price breaks the line, exit. - If you can run the trade for more than 10 minutes and 15 pips profit, jump to a higher time frame (M5) and see how it looks. You could use a trend following indicator like Heiken Ashi to try to stay in. Samples : #1 : Not a good setup. The pinbar doesn't go lower than the high of the previous bar. However, the down wick is very nice and the pinbar is beyond the close of the previous bar. Conservative people don't want to trade this. Aggressive ones will give it a try (and, in this case may lock in 30-40 pips, but this is luck). #2 : Not a good setup. Not a pinbar. #3 : Not a pinbar. #4 : Not the nicest one can find, but it's worth trying. The volume indicator also confirms you could be at a bottom. Without this last information, you could stay out, but with this yellow volume bar, you jump in. #5 : Not a pinbar. #6 : Touchy. Two pinbars and the price falls below their low only a couple of candles later. During this time, the Better Volume confirms you it's a top (two green bars). This is a risky trade : it doesn't show a clear rejection but two consecutive green bars on the volume indicator is a good sign. This one would have been a winner. #7 : A nice 10 pips winner. #8 : A very nice setup you should not miss. Volume is increasing for this bar but the reject is clear. You want to take this trade. You'll loose 10-12 pips on this one. It happens. #9 : Not as nice as #8, but still a setup you should give a chance to. Volume is increasing but the pinbar is still well formed. Risky trade, but this one would give you back the money you lost on #8. #10 : Price is moving slowly, pinbar is short. Risky setup. #11 : Price has been playing higher two bars before and volume is increasing (it should decrease) : setup is not clean. Stay away. #12 : Previous bar high is too high into the pinbar territory, pinbar is small. On the other hand, volume tells you this may be a top (red bar before the spike) and is slighty decreasing on the pinbar. You can try to enter the trade, the pinbar is small, so will be your stop in case the trade goes against you. You would probably close this one with 5 pips at most. #13 : Not perfect, but a setup to play with. #14 : The price has got high on the bar following the pinbar. But, the context is the price made a high (#13), then a small pullback and could be reverting down. The bar is small so you play with a tight sl here. It is worth the risk. #15 : PERFECT ! No doubt, this is THE setup of the day. Better volume confirms this is a top (two red bars just before the pinbar). #16 : Nice pinbar. However, previous bar went far into price territory of the pinbar. You should avoid this kind of setup, but the pinbar's shape is really good, so ... #17 : Nice shape, but the price is already playing at this level since 3 bars, so the rejection is not so clear. Some risks involved in this trade. #18 : Small bar but a setup you could give a chance to. Unfortunately, in the best case it is a break even trade, if you're not qucik enough, a looser. We saw 18 possible setups. 10-12 of them really worth the trade. You end up with 1 looser, a couple of break-even and several winners. Depending on your exit rules, you would have been making between 50 and 130 pips during this 7 hours time frame for this pair. I call this a nice day As with any trading system, knowing the S/R will be of great help. Murrey Math can help ( indicator here ) and display some levels. See on the attached chart how the price has been rejected several times from MM levels. Don't forget about other S/R levels and try to avoid taking a trade against them. My $0.02.

--- 帖子 #1957 ---
As far as I know, the three tap idea started on David's thread. There was some confusion there about the "one week" rule. David had been using it on his Neural Network, but early trades on that thread clearly did not use it. LG has been pretty consistent about observing the week rule, though I've seen some trades taken here that look back to the previous week. These usually happen pretty early in the week. I think the big question here is whether the trend is still valid. In this thread, we are using four hour, daily and weekly RSI for trend confirmation. If the first legs of the trade occur much further back than a week, then you have to start asking yourself whether the RSI readings are doing anything for the trade analysis. Personally, I think the answer is no. Thus, in my view, to take longer trades means looking to something else to confirm the trend. And that may be fine. But it's not this strategy. Just my 2 pips.

When the gap came down almost exactly to Friday's close and started the other way the odds were in favour of going long. This type of trade has nothing to do with the method that LG has layed out on this thread but she probably brought it to everyones attention because she just likes to share. Gotta love her for that, there aren't many people like that around. There are multiple ways to do a gap trade and it's a very popular trading method that a lot of traders use. There are traders that trade nothing but the gaps, from the daily charts down to tic charts. A lot of traders will sell the gap up open and reverse to long when it fills the gap with a close stop below...a dual trade so to speak. This is probably not the type of trade that a NuB trader would want to take on as they can be very tricky and it's easy to get on the wrong side of them. I haven't looked for anything but I would think that there are a lot of gap trading discussions on FF if you would like further insight into them. You can smack me hands if I'm overstepping here LG... Edit: Should have read the thread before posting...see I've arrived after the discussion has been taken care of...

--- 帖子 #2271 ---
It's currently at support on the H4 chart from 10/18, and the dip on 10/22 is pretty close. That may be too far back for you, but the support areas are pretty much in the same range. As for what you should do, there are probably as many answers as there are traders. You could 1) take your pips (never a bad idea) 2) move the stop up to where you will get something on the trade, but still let it ride; 3) split the trade, closing part of the position and letting the rest go (perhaps with a stop); 4) set a trail stop; 5) set a jumping stop; etc., etc. Just keep in mind, there are two things that mess with almost every trader's mind: fear and greed. Whatever you do, just ask yourself if you are doing it for a reason, or whether you are just letting one of those two demons get to you. For me, what that means is that I should be confident that my decision was right at the time I make it, no matter what the market decides to do to (or for) me. And for me that's alot harder to do than it is to say.

--- 帖子 #2382 ---
1. When trade is long and 3rd tap candle is long (green), I enter immediately. When trade is short and 3rd tap candle is short (red), I enter immediately, because there has been both a set-up and a trigger in both of these scenarios. 2. It is important that RSI on H4 and RSI on daily and weekly be in same direction before entering the trade. Remember there is a difference between a trade set-up and a trade trigger. The set-up is the 3 taps, the trigger is PA in the right direction . And yes, this is consistent with no. 1 above. 3. I don't trade shorter TFs for the 3 taps, but use shorter TFs for BO entries.

--- 帖子 #2399 ---
Ok folks...a nice big round of applause for gspe if you will. I've been communicating with gspe the last few days and he has been kind enough to almost completely redo his indicator for us. This is an indicator so it needs to be placed in the indicator folder and MT4 will have to be rebooted for this file to compile so you can use it. Experienced users can open it with MetaEditor and compile it and be done. Default location is the upper right hand corner with enough room left for an Expert to show up. The indicator can be moved on screen by using the X and Y locations in the user dialog. The user can use any time frame they wish but there is a limit of five time frames allowed. Just use the standard M?, H?, D1, W1 or MN separated by a comma. There's a true/false statement if you only want to see the name of current pair listed. You don't need to enter a pair name, just set this to true and the current pair will be listed. Font size and color may be changed in the user dialog. There's a true/false statement if you want to see the indicator placed in your RSI window (upper right) and a user choice to enter the name of the RSI that they are using, if it's different that the standard RSI(3)...so, if you have your RSI value set to 7 or something other than 3 you will need to change this in the user dialog. You must have a RSI window for this option to work. The value of the arrows are set to reflect the strength of the RSI movement: Sideways arrow reflects a neutral value a bit above and below the 3:00 position. Angled arrow reflects a weak move in the direction of the arrow, aproximately 3:00+ to 2:00 and 3:00- to 4:00. Straight up or straight down arrow reflects a strong move form the 2:00 to 12:00 or from the 4:00 to 6:00 positions. We have tried to come up with colors for the arrows that show well on both light and dark chart backgrounds. The arrow colors can not be changed via the user dialog, they can only be changed inside the code. Thank You Very Much gspe... ... Enjoy

--- 帖子 #2400 ---
The H1, D and W RSIs don't agree. The trade you are taking is off the H1 chart. Triple Tap trades are generally off the H4. I know some people do it off other time frames. LG has done them off of longer timeframes, but I can't think of an example where she took a third tap on a shorter timeframe. From what I've observed, when working off the H1 chart, she generally waits for confirmation by price action, usually be waiting for a M15 close in the direction she wants to trade. There are other reasons why your trade might be a good one, but they don't have much to do with any of the strategies used on this thread. (I'm actually thinking of shorting as well, because it looks like a decent short according to another strategy I've been looking at.) Hope it works out for you.

--- 帖子 #2423 ---
I have only traded H1 3taps a few times, so I haven't tested it out, but I would confirm with that TF and the 2 next higher TFs on any TF I was trading i.e. if trading H4..confirm with daily and weekly. If trading daily, confirm with weekly and monthly...so if trading H1, confirm with H4 and daily. The reason for this is you are not expecting as many pips from an H1 trade as you might from an H4 or daily trade so longer term trade may not be as important.

--- 帖子 #2554 ---
Correlations are important on short timeframes such as the m5. However on long tfs, e.g. h1, h4 or daily, correlations are unimportant. http://www.mataf.net/en/tools/01-01-correlation Take a look at EJ, UJ and GJ and see the correlation on m5 vs h1. Whilst at the moment UJ and EJ are highly correlated on m5 (98%), on h1 their correlation is just 18%.

--- 帖子 #2603 ---
It's really time to wind-up trades for the week/month. I have had a very good week and hope everyone else has also. Next week should be even better. Be prepared to open the week with 1 or 2 gap trades, should gaps occur at the open of market. If anyone does not know about gap trades, they are pretty simple. Basically, the market opens with PA disconnected (gapping)from the previous bar either up or down. PA looks suspended or hanging out there all alone . Gaps are almost/always filled. So if the gap is up above the last PA, we would sell (we want PA to come down to meet the last PA). IF the gap is down, we buy ( we want PA to go up to meet the last PA). Remember the prior PA cannot move, so it is the gap PA that has to adjust. Gaps are fun, almost sure money and as Scrutch said earlier in the thread, there are traders who only trade them for a living. So why shouldn't we trade them also. I shall be looking for them and hope you will join me at market open to do the same. Have a wonderful weekend everyone.

--- 帖子 #2621 ---
Steve Hopwood has developed an EA for trade management called the Multi Purpose Trade Manager. It has a pretty strong functionality, and can let you be a bit more precise about how to exit a trade (or a group of trades) when you aren't at the computer. The link to it is on his signature block. The guide for it is pretty self explanatory. For the trades you are talking about, you could, for example have had it set a stop loss at a particular point when the trade was in your favor (say set the stop at +25 when the trade hit +40), and from there you could have it do trailing stops or jumping stops, etc... It's a very nice, and flexible, piece of work. It's not a substitute for a brain (though it might be better than my brain, sometimes), but it's much better than simply using stop loss, take profit, or trailing stops.

--- 帖子 #2627 ---
vukovi21... Minimum size gap...The size of a gap is a traders preference thing. The gap range needs to be enough for you to make a profit, some tradrers are satisfied with a 5p profit, others want to see a 10p or 15p profit range before they will take the risk. Gaps happen all the time, you just don't see them on large time frame charts and the gaps that do happen are very minimual. The gap traders watch for in the 4x occurs when the market opens Sunday, after the Friday close. It's a trade that happens once a week, during the week the 4x market trades twenty four hours a day and the gaps are minimual.

I only glanced at the USD/CHF and it didn't seem to do too well but I'll go over that one and a couple of other pairs. I'll post the results when I finish. Also note that there could be variations between brokers due to their GMT offset. I think it should even out in the long run though. Here is a link that was posted in the Gap Trading forum that will give you an idea of opening prices so you can be prepared when your broker opens. http://www.oanda.com/currency/real-time-rates As far as a little background on why I chose 75% of the gap for TP and SL points, this quote should sum it up for you: "Always take your profits too soon. The bulls make money and the bears make money, but the pigs never do." That hangs on my wall in front of my desk. I don't scalp but I absolutely hate to see profits turn to break even or worse into a loss. After 12 years of trading I have given up on chasing the home run trades and instead go for a much smaller move. It fits my personal trading psychology. This will be different for everyone. Trading psychology is by far the most important aspect of trading as I have painfully learned. You can have the best system in the world but if your mindset is off you will lose. Sorry, I have a problem with rambling on and on! Anyways, good luck to everyone this evening! Trade well and prosper.

--- 帖子 #2877 ---
Just a word about putting a trade on demo before trading it live. Give yourself a big demo account..around $50,000. Don't worry about "building" this account..view it instead as a testing ground. I don't worry about what happens to it and I rarely look at the balance. I view my demo account as my trading laboratory. I spent a long time doubling my demo account, before I realized that, to me, it was stupid. I know it goes against conventional forex wisdom and advice. But it frees you up to trying different patterns, trades, etc. And yes, you may lose a few pips in the "transfer" to live, but you will stay out of many, many losing trades which more than makes it worthwhile.

--- 帖子 #2895 ---
Look to Page 1 ~ Post 1. The breakout range is set on the H1 chart, then when you switch to any other time frame chart the BOr will still show the same values as you had on the H1 chart. If you're using MetaTrader charting, you don't have to redraw the BO range, as long as you don't change charts, just change time frames. LG waits for a complete (body AND wicks) to close outside the BOr on the M15 before making her entry. On the GBPCHF chart I posted the entry (By The Book) would have been as soon as the first small bearish candle closed. Where my short line points would have been where I would have taken the trade using the M15 chart. Had a small bearish bar after price penetrated the lower BO line, followed by a small bullish bar, and the entry would have been just below these two bars. Super conservitive would be to wait for the bottom of the engulfing bearish bars lower wick to be cleared. Perhaps this would turn out much the way LG trades by using the demo first. The small bullish bar was a failure so the risk at this entry would have been very small. Yes I would have placed a trade if the break had been out the top...but only if the RSI's were pointing up. The RSI's control the direction you want to trade, with LG's methodology.

--- 帖子 #2900 ---
Yes and No . The BO lines need to be drawn on the H1 chart using the body (Open / Close) of the candle, which looks like what you've done but I can't verify that, as the prices on my chart is different than yours. If your bottom line is the same value as the open of the first bar (bullish) and the upper line is the same value as the open of the fourth bar (bearish) then that's correct. Our peridod separators are totaly different, so we show different bars ... As for the entry...you want to move to the M15 chart to wait for the first closed bar outside the BO range. You show the entry on the H1 chart and if you were on the M15 chart the entry would most likely be much better.

--- 帖子 #2915 ---
Yes my broker has another 2 candles to go until the period separator, so it's 3 candles before FXDD, that's correct. I generally prefer GMT charts but on the h1 tf all charts should look relatively similar no matter which broker. The period separator is a good guideline, but since most moves either start in Asian session or at or before London session, ppl should check which 4 candles they draw there S/R lines at. Volume increases dramatically at the opening of a new market, be it Asia, London or US. This is when most of the break outs happen. A little bit of backtesting should point out to anyone where to draw those lines. Since before the start of the Asian session (and often in the Asian session as well), we have the lowest volume of the whole day, it makes sense to draw your S/R lines at 4 candles in the Asian session. I don't know exactly how to quantify it any better, which is why I was asking you, how you learned about this h1 BO system so that I can read up on it, where this "phenomenon" comes from and thus give a better idea of where ppl should draw there S/R lines depending on their broker etc... Hope this all makes sense

--- 帖子 #2949 ---
The straddle technique is another BO method for LG's 4C technique, especially if you can't monitor your trades closely, or at night. Straddle for the 1H breakout involves drawing our lines for the 4 candles as usual. Then 2 pending orders are placed, a buy stop a certain number of pips above the upper line and a sell stop a certain number of pips below the lower line (plus spread). In LG's method, when the trend is up, the buy stop will be triggered, when it's down, the sell stop will be. SL should be at the lower or upper lines respectively. The "certain number of pips" is the buffer, for a 1HR method it's around 10-15 pips - this corresponds to the M15 confirmation of the breakout. TP should be modest, as LG stated, ca. 30 pips or so. Preferrably, when one trade is triggered, and is going well, the other should be deleted. In some cases the BO is false and turns on you, and the other order gets triggered, and usually relinquishes the pips lost on the false BO, as in this chart below: if you got triggered short on the lower line, the trade turns against you, but the buy order would have been triggered, and made up for the false-ish short breakout. Chart:

--- 帖子 #2950 ---
I know we don't do EA's here, but it seems to me that a breakout EA for a straddle order might be very useful. Since it wasn't fully explained before, a straddle order is basically two conditional orders placed at once. If the price rises a certain amount, then buy. If it falls a certain amount, then sell. That's pretty close to the Four Bar H1 Breakout strategy here. An EA could do the following: 1) From the H1 chart, find the high open or close, and the low open or close, for the last four hours. These two numbers create the high and low channel. 2) On the 15 minute chart, wait until a candle closes with a low that is higher than the high channel, or a high that is lower than the low channel. At that point enter either a buy in the first case or a sell in the second. 3) At the same time, the EA could place stop and TP. Lots of options for that. I don't code MQ4 yet. But if he were interested, this is the sort of thing that Steve Hopwood could probably code faster than it took me to write this post.

--- 帖子 #3012 ---
Well, I can see where there might be confusion and I'm sorry. I should clarify. For H1-4C-BOs , yes there is confirmation of direction on the 3 TFs, in fact, that is the only way a pair can make the "short list". But for Consolidation BOs , by the very nature of price consolidation the TFs may be mixed. The only thing we know for sure is that sooner or later there will be a BO. How we determine direction is by observing PA and confirmation of at least a couple of TFs.

--- 帖子 #3038 ---
Fading horizontal lines. I know that LG’s method deals primarily with diagonal trend lines and breakouts but the same can be done using horizontal lines of support and resistance. I rarely use Rsi when I trade but it can be applied when fading large lines of S+R just as well This cable trade last year is typical of how powerful trading S+R can be whether its breakouts or fading a major level as was the case here. This thing happens time and time again and check out the direction on the Rsi looks familiar right. Really zoom out on the first weekly chart and notice how the level is screaming out at you to be traded.

--- 帖子 #3207 ---
Firstly A very nice thread based on the basic's of Price Action. I want to say right at the start that if you feel this post is irrelevant please remove this post or PM me and i will remove it.. I have watched this thread develop and the three tap on a trendline is a strong signal for a reversal I have noted that a lot of people are then struggling to find a exit point. Therefore if i may i would like to put forward one of my rules ( I have used this rule for many years). Iam a big fan of trendlines and therefore I have to be a follower of Alan Andrews, now I think most are familier with the Pitchfork however I have found that most do not know how to trade it and I think it maybe usefull with this trading method. As we know all pairs return from the outer range to the median line 80% of the time, therefore if we use the trendline as Lawgirl recommends as a upper or lower line of the picthfork we can then say that the pair on a confirmed bounce of that line should return to at least the median line... Now you can either use the Indicator thats standard in the MT4 platform or you can work it out for yourself, ( I can help if anyone whishes to learn) Now the next question is what happens if the pair does not return to the Median line well in most case's it will return to test the last high/low so we then have a new target. The last question we must ask is how long should we wait for the pair to reach the Median line before we close the position, this can be answered simply by looking at the points from which the Pitchfork starts...of course we have a A,B,C point... A is the first point and the longest point, B is the second point so we count the candles between the two we then count the candles between B and C which ever has the largest is the count we use, we then count the candle from point C into the future this will give us a time frame , now the price should hit the Median line within this time frame if it does not then the move has failed and we close the position and wait for a new setup, it should return to a point level with B or C and may well pass ( breakout of the range). I hope this helps. Glenn

I will look at putting together a PDF file over the next few days, but in the mean time two charts to show the indicator and how it can be used on a chart, as you can see the upper/lower line are trendlines so all the Indicator is doing is showing two more parallel lines which we use as targets/support/resistance lines. We must remember that by using trendlines we are only using " Significant Pivots" as reversal points. In the GBPUSD chart you can see how we can use the Pitchfork on a breakout. Glenn

--- 帖子 #3213 ---
The points are the last three high/ lows, I would sugest that if you are comfortable with placing a trendline at a low/low or high/high then use that to setup your Pitchfork, you can take the last high and subtract the low from it and then divide it by 50% that will give you a start point at the median then just run a parallel trendline which will give you your median line....

--- 帖子 #3328 ---
Hi there I suggest you read post 1 again, as that answers your entry question - the third tap is the set up, but you must wait for price action to confirm b4 you enter trade - ie that bar or the following bar must be going in the right direction for the trade (all RSIs confirming)- you will need to decide how much confirmation you need b4 you enter; there are various confirmation methods discussed in the thread As to exit - again there are quite a few discussions on that in this thread; I suggest you read the thread and make some notes about possible exit techniques; you could do worse than use 2 units and take profit on 1 unit at 20 pips or at first resistance point and trail the second unit, but the purpose of this thread is to show people how to identify potentially profitable set ups; it is up to you how you enter and manage your trades after entry. You will see that Lawgirl says a number of times that she sets her TP and SL based on SR areas, but it is up to you how you manage your trade

--- 帖子 #3586 ---
FxSnip'r...Perhaps if you think of it this way: The trendline is acting as resistance. If the trendline is on the top, then the resistance should keep price from going up and you want to look for a downward bias on the RSI arrows and a downward bias bar...looking to go short. If the trendline is on the bottom, then the resistance should keep price from going down and you want to look for an upward bias on the RSI arrows and an upward bias bar...looking to go long.

If you open a daily chart of the USD pairs, you will clearly see that the USD pairs are currently trading at the previous resistance levels. Look at daily charts of AUDUSD, GBPUSD mainly and you will see what I mean. So, if the old saying "old ceiling becomes new floor and old floor becomes new ceiling, we "should" see this level hold as support for now. So, if you are planning on going short here, please be careful of these levels. I will personally be looking at this level as a FLOOR to bounce off. One exception would be if news are so influential those levels will mean nothing when fundementals are strong one way or another. --- 帖子 #3709 ---
I'm not familiar with that . What is the rule of 72?

--- 帖子 #3710 ---
The Rule of 72 has some amazing mathematical accuracy used worldwide to tell how many days, weeks, months or years it will take to double ones money. Divide 72 by whatever percentage number you like..in your case 5%, so 72 divided by 5 = 14.4, which tells you that ideally every 14.4 days (since 5 was a daily goal) your money will double. Say one wanted to average 20% per month: 72 divided by 20 = 3.6, meaning at that rate, ones money would double every 3.6 months. Powerful incentive. I play with it all the time.

Due mainly to LG, I have been spending more time looking at H4 charts and in particular how to identify trend and changes in trend I am sure it is no news to more experienced traders, but it is interesting to see how large range impulse bars break trend lines as the supply and demand balance is upset in one bar If you do not get in on the initial trend line break, it is a good heads up to watch out for the retracement and the second leg down GBPCHF shows two nice examples in the attached chart of an impulse bar breaking a trend line - signalling a trend change and to look for retracements

--- 帖子 #3739 ---
Bars showing strength - ie typically bars with small wicks, larger than average bodies and larger than average range You will usually see them as bars breaking through SR or trend lines or out of consolidation - and usually signal start of a new move You can tell which is the impulse direction because the bars are larger and usually there is little overlap of the bars, whereas retracements will usually have smaller bars and more overlap The initial move down on GBPCHF was a good example of strong move down followed by retracement. Initial leg down was 347 pips, second leg 359, with a rather pathetic third move . Most reliable moves are the second leg after strong initial impulse move in new direction

go in your metatrader folder ! inside of metatrader folder go in "Experts" folder ! inside "Experts" folder go in "Indicators " folder and paste there ! (.mq4 file or .ex4) you must have something like this : c: program files metatrader interbankfx experts indicators does'nt matter what kind of file it is .mq4 or .ex4 (mq4 is source and you can modify,ex4 is already compiled works but you cannot modify until you have the source) so in this moment the difference is that the file is an ea or an indicator ! you know what do u have .. attention ! if is it an EA you must paste it in Experts folder ! if is an indicator you must put the file in indicators folder ! after this you have to restart platform and look for indicator in custom indicators and for EA in Experts advisor wich you find in left Navigator window (CTR+N) now if you want to see charts like most of here go to indicators (left side in navigator window) and add rsi with period "3" to your chart ! after that add from custom indicators (from navigator windows) and add Lawgirl's Trend Display v1.02 wich u find at first page of this thread ! In Lawgirl's Trend Display v1.02 indicator properties chose "true" value for 'ShowCurrentPaintOnly" and "RSI_WindowName" u can set collors for your candles ,backgorund and with this 2 indicators ...save as template ...and load on others pair ! i hope was helping for you ! good trades to all and a lot of thanks to LawGirl for this thread ...indeed like a home !!

Wally...I certainly wouldn't want you to not emulate LG's criteria, only that you arrived late and the trade was already underway. In that case, either pass on the trade (there's going to be a lot more of them) or try to find an advantage for your entry...in this case the pullback. If you're late to the party and you don't get a pullback, just pass on the trade and wait for the next one. If you start chasing the market you set up habits that are very hard to break.

I'm sure you guys have already been asked this question, but I'd like to know how many of you place limit orders near the third tap. For example, PH22's potential short setup on 4 hr GBP/USD looks promising. If we wait for confirmation candle, we potentially miss some if not all of the move. If a limit order is placed near the third tap and a tight stop is placed above the nearest major support, we can maximize profits by setting a 2:1 risk reward ratio. Now I know there will be more losers that way, but the winners will be greater. The loses will seem less significant. To do this the 4 hour RSI must be pointing in the opposite direction to that of the weekly or even daily since it is a lagging indicator. Does anyone trade this way and if so I would love to hear the result. Thanks.

Hi all, I have been a longtime fan of FF and all of its members (even the somewhat less than entertaining ones), but I must say that it is such a pleasure to check in with this thread and see the genuine enthusiasm and cooperation that Lawgirl has inspired in so many traders. Good on you LG! And good on all the great contributors. I have been a big fan of RSI for many years and it is a pleasure to see this indicator made use of in such a simple and effective way. I look forward to making more profitable trades with it, and with the help of the indicator. At this point, I must confess that I am not a fan of the 3-tap method of entry, but using the indicator for entries on the H1 charts with agreement from PA has proven to be a very effective way to use LG's approach. I posted a chart with an example. From the entry idea that LG uses on the H1, it seems to be quite alright to take entry based on all arrows on the indicator agreeing, and the H1 bar being more than 50% toward its close. Most important - and I really mean MOST important - is to be sure PA really shows the probabilities in your favor. Other tools that I believe are very useful when working with RSI in the manner that LG is, are watching for the two types of divergences (Hidden, and Classic) and to be drawing trendlines based on closes and not swings (as LG is does). I'd be happy to post a couple of charts with examples of the divergences and trendlines but it seems that we are all big boys and girls here, so I'm assuming that these terms are understood overall that they can simply be referred to, and utilized where appropriate. -Joe
