--- 帖子 #3966 ---
In the spirit of naked charts, here is an example of something I like to see in the time frame I am trading, BEFORE I consider whether it is worth risking anything on an indicator signal. It shows how the RSI (preferably H1 and up timeframes) can show the market's hand. I believe this works quite well in conjunction with the overall strategy here. It requires no additional indicators, or rationale for how the trades are taken. This example does not offer entry criteria because LG's method already suggests what needs to be done after this type of chart pattern occurs. This is merely intended to point out what is already in front of our noses on price charts when the market is speaking. Hope this is helpful. Just a brief comment on divergences here. For those who don't have a lot of experience with them, it is very wise NOT to consider divergences as trade signals. Rather they are more safely used in trading as a signal that one side or the other has become unstable, or more aggressive. With confirmation, that instability or aggressiveness can be used to make money, protect profits or avoid losses. -Joe

--- 帖子 #4088 ---
Just a little inspiration ... think about it If you have a $10,000 starting balance in your Forex trading account. Assuming very minimal risk trading (much like is done in this thread), you would risk about 1% per trade, on a 3-tap 4HR trade this would be about a 50 pip SL. On a BO it is about 25 pip SL. If 1% = 50 pips SL would equal about $100 loss. That would mean your lot size is 0.2 lots ($2 per lot) which is minimum risk. Assuming you take about 10 x 3-tap trades per week on average and you have a 60% winning percetage with R:R of 1:1 that means you will win 6 trades and lose 4 out of 10. This should give you 300 pips (6 winners) - 200 pips (4 losers) for a total of +100 pips. Assuming 10 x BO trades per week as well, with 25 pip SL and TP. The same winning %age and R:R , you would have 150 pips (6 winners) - 100 pips (4 losers) for a total of +50 pips. If you do a grand total, you would have +150 per week. If each of your pips was equal to $2, you would have a grand total of $300 per week. which amount to 3% a week. If you risked 2 % per trade, you would be loking at 6% profit per week. NOW here is where compounding can really make a difference in your account balance. Now if you continue to increase your lot size so that you are making 6% per week on your balance, your account balance would double every 12 weeks ... Also note that after 52 weeks (which is a complete year), you account balance would have grown to 20 times its size. With that in mind, you would have $200,000. Now imagine if you can stay consitent for a couple years .. yes you guessed it, you would be a millionaire Do you agree that you are seeing 60% or better winning percentage? Do you agree that you average 10 3-tap trades per week? Do you agree that you average 10 BO trades per week? Just imagine the possibiliteis and keep this goal in mind.

--- 帖子 #4105 ---
Keeping track in pips works really well, so long as the lot size is constant. And it provides an OK basis for comparison. But go back to the example of 3 tap trades with a 50 stop, and BO trades with a 25 stop. Assume a risk:reward ratio of 1. And assume 60% wins for each. With constant lot sizes, the three tap trades are twice as good: they yield twice as many pips. But, if you adjusted lot size so that risk was always the same percentage of your account, then the two strategies would be equally profitable. The Three tap trades would give more pips for the week, but they would do it on lots that are half as large as the BO trades. In terms of actual dollars earned (and dollars risked) the two types of trades would be the same.

--- 帖子 #4106 ---
Agreed. But I didnot want to put so much weight on the BO strategy, so I gave it only half the weight of the 3-tap trade. But, as you menitoned, if you double the lot size then they are equal in terms of dollars in the end. Thanks for pointing that out.

--- 帖子 #4110 ---
Assuming your first 6 paragraphs above, which are based on very sound MM and certainly doable with the disciple most of us have or will have with a little more experience, ...think of this...let's say that when your account reaches $15,000, you pull $5,000 out of it and use it for monthly bills or take the family on vacation or whatever. This will happen every 6 weeks or so. How many of us couldn't use an extra 5K every so often? This may mean that a spouse would not have to work and could stay home with the kids. Or getting totally out of debt. Or buying that car we might need (or want). Or ___________. Managing your trading account this way has many, many advantages. First, and I believe most importantly, the trading pressure stays the same, the MM stays the same, and the emotions stay the same. Risking 6% on a $10,000 account is totally different than risking 6% on a $200,000 account. Another important factor...the time we spend doing this is often resented by our families. There is nothing like handing your spouse $5,000 to spend as they please because of our trading and as a "thank you" for their patience with us doing this! It can change everything....just another way of looking at it.

--- 帖子 #4117 ---
Hi Holister--All of the TLs you drew are correct. None of them are wrong. Much depends on when you arrive at the pair. The order for focusing in on a pair is first, the 3 TFs in confirmation, then look for set ups. Look at your bottom left chart..yes, the trade has already occurred, and it was a profitable one. In that case, adjust the TL by moving the line from your bottom first tap...is there a reentry? No, not yet and there may not be...move to another pair, at least for the time being. There are no correct and incorrect TLs (as long as you know fundamentally how to draw them and you do). All of our charts are different, we are in different time zones, with different feeds. That's why I call this trade what you see, but that is what makes this simple system complicated also, because nothing is exact. But you are getting it, so welcome... --- 帖子 #4148 ---
It is important to study charts for many reasons, most of which we will not discuss at this time. Gap chart study is particularly interesting, because we can learn so much from it. Look at the AUDNZD H4 chart below (a chart we don't normally trade because of the spread). Using your Crosshair bar to measure Friday's close to Sunday's open, you will notice that it is approximately 53-55 pips. We start licking our lips...because we say to ourselves, "most gaps are filled, most gaps are filled" and we are banking about 50 pips in our heads. Not a bad start for the week.....we think. This gap was no exception, it did fill...but look at what it did before it finally did so toward the end of the week. Hanging on to this pair for that 50 or so pips would have produced a DD of about 140-180 pips. How many of us are willing to risk 180 pips for 50 pips? Now, it could be that PA continues downward, but we don't know that at this point.

--- 帖子 #4174 ---
Open the indicator in the chart for the pair you want to trade. Now go to menu under "Charts" and go down to "Indicator List." Double-click Lawgirls Trend Indicator and the window will open up. Click "Inputs" tab and go down to "Pairs to Trade." Double-click on all the pairs under "Value" and just type in pair you want displayed for that chart. Click "Okay" and "Close." You should be all set!

--- 帖子 #4296 ---
Hi dfstone, LG from page 1: Recently Asked Questions 10/27/2010 Q: Does one wait for the close of the 3rd tap candle before entering or enter immediately?. A: When desired trade is long and 3rd tap candle is long (green on my charts), enter immediately. When desired trade is short and 3rd tap candle is short (red on my charts), enter immediately, because both a set-up and a trigger has occurred in each of these scenarios. Q: I notice that usually when the 3rd tap occurs, the RSI is not supporting the direction of the desired trade. Is it important that the H4 RSI support the direction of the weekly and daily RSI at this point? A: It is important that the H4 RSI the daily and weekly RSIs show the same direction before entering the trade. Remember there is a difference between a trade set-up and a trade trigger. The set-up is the 3 taps, the trigger is PA in the right direction . This is consistent with the question above. Q: Do you use M30 or M15 charts on the 3 tap trades? A: Although I don't use shorter time frames (TFs) for 3 tap trades, some traders have indicated to me that they use these TFs to observe price action (PA) before entry. I do use the TFs for breakout trades (BO), discussed below.

--- 帖子 #4301 ---
I have tried to recreate that 3 Tap trade. A TL can be drawn connecting the 3 candles on the H4 chart....a set-up. The trigger came on the next candle when PA headed in the desired direction. But look what happens if you move the 1st tap away from that hammer candle and place it on the next candle...a 3 Tap trade. Some traders may have see that setup that way and not the way I saw it. No matter...look at the trigger candle for either interpretation..that was a 100+ pip move. I hope this helps.

This is all you need. Unzip files and do the following: 1) Copy Includes to experts/includes folder of meta 2) Copy Indicators to expers/indicators folder 3) Copy VHANDSTRADE.mq4 onto experts folder Before starting, make sure you save a special lawgirl template with teh RSIs a) All you then need to do is drag the expert onto a chart. b) Right click on chart and select expert advisors then strategy tester c) select visual mode and input the required dates. If you want todays trading then select start today and end tomorrows date. Click start. Once a chart opens up with the required replay, right click on chart and select the template. VOILA. you are ready to replay todays action. You can also speed up the day by dragging the little slider on bottom left. Enjoy everyone and get the practice in as its free especially on the BIG trades that you missed. if only we could wind back the time to trade those trades

--- 帖子 #4661 ---
I have been noticing for the last week or so that many of you are all over the map with 3 Tap trades..going back weeks, even months on H4 charts, drawing 3 Tap TLs and trying to get the RSIs to "fit". Some of you STILL do not have period seperators on your charts. Successful 3 Tap trades are analysed in a particular ORDER . All should go back and read/re-read page 1 of this thread. That order is this: 1. Scan the RSIs for confirmation of the 3 TFs . List or pay attention to only those which confirm.....forget any other pair at this time. I visually scan and do not totally rely on the indicatior, but that's up to each trader. REMEMBER: Generally by Tuesday you will only be working within the confines of the current week (those period seperators) for the 3 Tap trade. Many of you still do not understand this. 2. THEN, go back to each listed or noted pair and look closely at it for a way to enter. Start with the H4 chart....ask yourself: "Do I see a 3 Tap pattern here?" and/or "Do I see any consolidation here?" If no to either question, move to the H1 chart and look for a way to enter there i.e. a BO. Do this for each pair that made your short list. This order is essential to consistent success here. Ask yourself these questions: Q: What are we doing here? A: We are trying to make money by trading forex. Q: How do we do that? A: We follow a routine in our analysis for every single trade we consider taking. Q: What is that routine? A: We do all of the above and in that order. Q: Why is that important? A: Because when we use that order of analysis, we are putting the odds of a successful trade significantly in our favor. Q: How is that? A: Because we start our analysis by knowing the direction we should be trading into, then we look for "signs" (taps, TLs,etc.) that further indicate to us that there will be a successful trade in that direction. If we don't find those signs, we move on....even though the 3 TFs confirm direction. Q: Will this analysis give us successful trades every time? A: Of course not.... But I do not know of a better system, not Elliot Wave, not Martingale, you name it....that gives us a better edge at true success.

--- 帖子 #4830 ---
The setup would be the 3 Taps for a 3 Tap trade or the S/R lines for a BO trade. The trigger comes after the setup..it can be hours after the setup in fact. The trigger gives us the entry into the trade after the setup has occurred. Sometimes a trigger never happens, in which case we abandon the setup. In the chart above, the trigger will be PA heading up, in which case the candle (will likely be the next candle, or even the candle after that) will turn green, and the RSI H4 indicator will turn up. That is the trigger which tells us to enter the trade. Requires patience.

--- 帖子 #4837 ---
Finding logical SL and TP levels: 1. Minimize your chart (minus button on platform [-]). That's called pulling back on chart. 2. Using same TF, look for a levels of support and resistence. I did not see any on the H1 TF for this pair. 3. If you don't see any, move to next higher TF. In this case the H4 chart. Again look for levels of support and resistence. I still did not see any on this TF for this pair. 4. Move to the next higher TF, the daily chart...ah ha...there they are very clear. 5. That is where I put in my TP at around 84.26. Same thing for SL.

--- 帖子 #4838 ---
Yes, we only think about setups on confirmation on the 3 TFs at the time of set up. They may move around somewhat after setup, but we can't control that as long as the longest TF (weekly for a H1 and H4 trade) stays with us.

--- 帖子 #4856 ---
People confuse the 'trigger' and the 'setup'. The 'setup' is the set of conditions that need to be in place before a trade can be 'triggered'. At the time of writing, lawgirl has identified twosetups, with their associated triggers: 1. Setup: you have identified a trend and drawn your 2 tap trendline: • Trigger: a third tap of the trendline 2. Setup: you have identified a candle breakout box: • Trigger: a breakout of the box In both cases, major patience is required to wait for the trigger, which in turn is easy to miss. The trigger is PA after SetUp. if good we jump in. I hope this understanding will Help Bro... Must Practice to make perfect.. I'm still learning too.

--- 帖子 #4965 ---
Hi all, I am posting this chart because I have been on this thread for many days and I think some of the chart reading components that I have marked off here would be very helpful for some of the decision making that is often discussed. These are very basic things that I have trained to watch for on any chart in any time frame. They show clear examples of when the market is "saying something" that everyone can hear, but not all can interpret. As the GBPUSD chart progressed this week, these elements began to appear. I do not normally leave a chart marked up in this way for an entire week because it is annoying, but when these elements combine to suggest important things like bias, then it can save lots of $ and :-( to be able to recognize them in context and most importantly - in time. In the future I will refrain from such complex charts, but I hope that this is useful to the thread and the great traders here. I tend to take much fewer trades than all of you do because I am much more conservative, but that doesn't mean I don't see lots of good trades. Lawgirl, if this is out of line with anything you are doing, please feel free to tell me and or remove this post. My intention is to fill in what I perceive as a small gap in some of the chart analysis. Sorry for such a lengthy post... What an excellent trading week we all had, and I thank you Lawgirl for being such a very cool support and always on the money. (pun intended) -Joe

--- 帖子 #4980 ---
I suggest you look back through your 100 trades and see what would you would have done if you had taken only your 20 best signals. By best signal, I mean without the benefit of hindsight. Then look at maybe your 25 or 30 best signals. Then 50, then 75, etc... If you are seeing significant dropoff, I would think that's a clear indication that you are overtrading and/or jumping in at the wrong times (either too early out of impatience, or too late to try to chase the trade). One of the hardest things to resist is the temptation to be doing something, to always be in a trade. I'm really working on the idea of being patient and letting the market show itself before pulling the trigger.

--- 帖子 #4990 ---
Lets say your goal was 10% a week, and you traded a system like the 4 candle breakouts here, using a 20 pip stop. You risk 1.5% per trade, which I think most people would accept as being reasonable. You would need to average somewhere just below 30 pips a day to reach this target. Does anyone here think that is really impossible? I'm willing to bet that Lawgirl is doing better than that. So what about getting to 1.3 million in a year? There are tremendous psychological differences between risking 150 dollars on a trade in a 10K account, and risking $15,000 on the same trade with a million in the account. There's no logical reason for the difference, but we aren't talking about logic. We are talking about a person putting $15,000 on the line for a trade where every tick probably costs what the person was used to making in a day or more. On top of that, there is the simple problem of volume. At $1 million, you would have to be putting on trades with about 750 standard lots. At some point on your journey to $1 million, liquidity and slippage will almost certainly become issues. 10% a week is possible, even with consistency. 10% a week compounded is a much dicier proposition.

--- 帖子 #5118 ---
The H1 4C BO charts you posted here puzzle me. They all seem to be characterized by higher lows and higher highs. I don't see how these can be breakouts. Of course, if you are also willing to trade any continuation or momentum after the first four hours of the day, that's fine, but I think its a different idea than what I've seen before. Here's how I understood these trades before. Most brokers days tend to end somewhere near the close of the Asian session. Around that time, volatility typically slows. Thus you tend to have pairs whose RSIs are all pointing one way, but that are also in a rut. From there, I've seen breakout trades. The set ups here look different to me. It's the start of the week, so the RSIs aren't set at all. And instead of being stuck in a rut, these pairs are already trending. I have no problem with trying to find a way to jump onto these trends, if there's a good reason to expect them to continue. I'm only pointing out that these set ups look both different and new to me.

--- 帖子 #5214 ---
Among all the trading strategies, gaps may be the easiest to test. I just looked at a year on the GBPUSD. I used 8 pips as the cutoff, and found 16 weeks where there would be no trade because the gap was smaller than that. That leaves 36 trades over the 52 weeks. With a 100 pip stop, there were 31 winners and 5 losers. The winners went for 884 pips, so the net was 384 pip before spread and commission. Assuming around 3.3 spread, the net goes down to about 265 pips. There were two winning trades that you would have to hold for over 30 4 hour bars. After that, the next longest trade was 17 bars, Most winning trades closed the gap much faster. With a 50 pip stop, there were 28 winners and 9 losers. The winners grossed 695 pips, netted 245 pips before spread, and about 126 pips after spread. If you set the stop equal to the gap, so your R:R = 1, you would have gotten 24 winners and 12 losers. If you set the stop equal to 1/2 the gap, so your R:R =2, you would have gotten 19 winners and 17 losers. Both of the last scenarios do not include spread. I did a quick look at the numbers and it looks like the spread would eat up about 20% on the 1:1 scenario, and maybe a bit more on the 2:1. What does all this mean. Suppose you risked 2% of your account per trade. With 100 stop loss, you would make somewhere around 5.5% for the year. With 50 stop loss, you would make somewhere around 5%. With stop equal to gap, you would make closer to 20%. And with stop equal to 1/2 gap, the earnings would be higher, maybe as high as 33%. If people wanted to check other currencies or longer time frames, its really very easy to do. I don't understand why so many people are so willing to jump into live trading on something that they never bothered to test for themselves.

--- 帖子 #5382 ---
The basic theory behind the system is simple: follow the trend. There are lots of books (Trend Following and Trend Trading for a Living come to mind) about trend following that employ other methods, but the basic idea is typically the same. First, you have to identify the trend, and then you have to find a way to jump on board. Take three tap trades: First step is to identify the trend by looking to the RSIs. If the RSIs on the two higher time frames are pointing strongly in the same direction then its a pair worth watching. But finding the trend is not enough. Next step is to find a good way to jump on board. Within a trend price tends to bob up and down. The three tap idea is based on the observation that, on a pullback, price has a tendency to bounce off of a trendline. If price has recently bounced twice off of a line, then it will likely bounce off a third time. So the second step is to find spots on the pairs worth watching where the price either has recently bounced for the third time, or looks like it is about to make the third tap. Finally, this system looks for confirmation. Lawgirl calls this a trigger. With three taps, the confirmation comes when the time frame you are looking at (typically H4) and the two higher time frames all have their RSI's pointing in the same direction. This confirmation will coincide with price already moving in the direction of your trade. So, three elements to a three tap trade: trend identification via RSIs, signal of a likely pullback and retracement via the third tap, and confirmation of price action by having full accord between the three RSIs. Other systems will use other tools to look for the same things. The really heartening thing about this system is that it is not magic at all. It's a sound application of some basic principles that seem to work over time. Lawgirl's unique contribution, I believe, is the use of the RSI(3) over three time frames as the means for identifying the trend. Lots of trend identification ideas seem either to identify the trends too late, or too often, both leading to bad results. It may be that LG's approach, like the little bear's porridge, is "just right."

--- 帖子 #5434 ---
Your BO is good but I think another issue to be addressed is SL. When you're trading BO, your SL should not be more than the other end of the line + spread. Putting SL almost 20pips outside the other end means you just wish to give some money to the market unnecessarily. A BO failure always pushes market far on the other side and putting SL far away is giving back too much. My two cents this morning. Forgive my bad manners, goodmorning Gentlemen and Babes PC2

--- 帖子 #5514 ---
Yes, both setups need to be in agreement for an A++ trade. If you only have one of the two setups and the RSI's are in agreement, I consider that to be an A+ trade. When they happen together, the odds of a great trade increase dramaticaly. I don't take these just any time that both conditions are true. I , want to see the H4-3T happen first, most likely the RSI's wont be in total agreement at that time. Then , I want to see the breakout happen within a few hours, two or three at the most, with four hours maximum. After four hours I feel that the real advantage has expired. Not that it will not or could not still be a very nice trade, just that it no longer has the force of the dual confirmation behind it. The CADJPY breakout occured about two and a half hours after the H4-3T. The USDCAD breakout occured about three hours after the H4-3T. For either of these trades I'm looking at the M15 chart for the breakout confirmation, and yes price action needs to reflect the momentum as well. IF, the H4-3T setup occurs and the H1-4C-BO setup occurs in thirty minutes or less, then... , I think that would be an A+++ trade. When this happens I'm usually looking at a M5 chart for entry because I want to get in as early as I can...depending again on price action.

--- 帖子 #5520 ---
I don't mind if you want to reference my response. It's your method that brings all this together, I'm just trying to isolate the excellent trades from the good trades. I watch the majors mostly but also keep an eye on the others as well. To keep a close watch on them all is a bit daunting but it's doable becaue of the time frame involved. I do pay close attention to the spread, which influences whether I want to take the trade or not. If the spread is large, then I'll just pass on the trade. I draw all potential H4-3T's that I see and adjust them as the market moves, regardless of the RSI's. At times I'll have two H4-3T's drawn, a bullish and a bearish. Then I adjust them as the market dictates direction. I draw all the H1-4C-BO's at the close of the fourth hourly bar from period separator to period separator. At times I will start drawing these sooner...depends on what the RSI's are showing me.

--- 帖子 #5570 ---
The H1 4 candle breakout set-up: 1. Find the directional bias on weekly, daily, H4. All must match at the time of set-up. 2. You will be looking at the bodies of the first four H1 candles of a new trading day...disregard the tails (wicks)....whenever that is for you. That is one reason period seperators need to be placed on the chart. 2. Place horizontal lines at the highest high of these four candles' bodies (not including the tails, if any) and the lowest low of these four candles' bodies , again, disregard the tails. These lines are really just R/S lines. 3. Wait for a breakout in the direction of the bias. Has anyone coded an indicator to draw the lines?

Hi All, Thank you for everyone's contribution! I hope many will find this indicator helpful. This is a Hanover's indicator, modified by dgodfrey for Lawgirl's H1-4C-BO method. Please read Hanover's link for details on the settings. http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=256848 As an example, user can specify 1) number of days back or just the current day, 2) hours for box as well as line, 3) colors, 4) timeframe to determine 'candle body's' lines, etc. It's a great tool with many options! The modified version (Daily LinesBoxes OC) works perfect with Lawgirl's H1-4C-BO method. It's quite awesome! Daily Lines Boxes (original version) Daily Lines Boxes OC (Lawgirl's modified version, 'OC' stands for Open/Close) Happy trading to all! Leftcoaster

--- 帖子 #5703 ---
End of the month is a good time to go back and take a look at your favorite pairs and assess where the pair has been during that time and more importantly, where it might be going the next month. I like to print out the monthly chart for a few pairs so that I can refer back to them from time to time, mark them up, make notes on the them and watch the PA changes throughout the month. For example: USDJPY This pair reached 7 year lows in October 2010. Notice how PA has been making perfect lower lows and lower highs since 2007 (beautiful waves). But this past month, PA turned around and started up. If past PA is any indication of projected PA, it should continue up to the 86.60 area, maybe higher. It will be very instructive to watch. Again, I highly recommend for everyone, especially newer traders, to pull up the charts, place R/S lines on them, mark them for 3 Taps, and print a few out to watch throughout the month.

--- 帖子 #5804 ---
Statistically, the gap ( difference between Friday's close and Monday's open) usually gets filled before the week is out. You want to trade towards Friday's close. For gap up, you short. For gap down, you buy. Most of the time, you can grab 10 or more pips within the first 2 or 3 hours.

--- 帖子 #5989 ---
No, it is not a random start of the day. It is your broker's start of the day. My broker's new trading day starts at 5:00 pm EST (New York), which is 2:00 pm my time PST (California). It is my understanding that all brokers use 5:00 pm for end/start of new day. But when is that according to your local time? It is those first 4 H1 candles that is the measure for this BO trade. (That is why period serarators are a must.)

--- 帖子 #6044 ---
I am not lawgirl but its definately not the same thing since the bodies of the 1H candle with almost certainly represent a wider range than the open/close of the 4H candle. So if you want to use the 4H you would have to use H/L and not O/C. And it shows in the pic you posted it is a valid trade since we're only looking to short (trend is down). --- 帖子 #6050 ---
There are several different breakouts here. There is the H1 broker opening four candle breakout, the H1 consolidation breakout, and the Two Tap, move to H1 for confirmation breakout. The last is simply a variation on the three taps, so I won't talk about it here. The idea is the same as the three tap trade, but it looks for a different trigger. The H1 consolidation breakout is the easiest to understand. It pays no attention to RSIs. Instead, in an H1 consolidation, the idea is that the trading range is holding steady and actually getting smaller and smaller over a fairly long period of time. The longer the consolidation lasts, the more likely that there will be an explosive move to break the consolidation. Thus, when you see a long period of consolidation, you simply draw your horizontal lines at the top and bottom of the consolidation channel. Where, exactly, those lines will go will depend a bit on the channel, but if its not pretty obvious where to put them, then you probably don't have the kind of consolidation you are looking for. Then, when price moves outside the channel, you wait for a decent PA confirmation. I think LG uses a full candle on the M15 chart outside the channel. Stop goes on the other side of the channel. As I said before, the trend doesn't matter too much because the long period of consolidation is an indication of extreme uncertainty in the market, and the price is just as likely to move either way. I have a harder time understanding the broker opening four hour breakouts on the H1 chart. LG says that you use the opening of the day that your broker uses. I'm not sure, but I'd be willing to bet that there are brokers that use at least 8 different times for opening. To me, this implies that this technique might work on almost any four hour period. Having said that, I am very skeptical about whether that's true, and I doubt that anyone has thoroughly tested it. I once thought that the rationale was as follows. My broker, and LG's both start their days during the doldrums of the market. That's typically from about 4pm EST to about 11pm. Volatility at that time is low, and there isn't much movement in most of the currencies, especially the non-Asian ones. The channel that you draw thus often resembles a mini-consolidation channel, and the trade seems to work like a consolidation trade. What happens is that Frankfurt or London opens, and the currency takes off again in the direction of the prevailing trend. And of course, the trade already has an edge because it only looks at currencies where the RSis all line up. Recently, LG has also noted trades of this type where its pretty clear that the pair is already trending. When this happens, I see what's going on as a kind of momentum trade. The RSIs are lined up, the PA is moving favorably, and you jump on the trend. What the four candle, one hour trades have in common with the three taps trades is the three step process to get into the trade. There is 1) the filter of trading in the direction of the trend as confirmed by the RSIs, 2) the signal of price breaking out of a pre-defined channel, and 3) the trigger of Price Action in the direction of the trade (here by a full M15 candle outside the channel). The basic consolidation trade also has three elements, but they are different. First, there is the requirement of a long consolidation, the longer the better. Then the signal of price moving outside the channel, and again the trigger when PA confirms that the move is strong enough to trade. I hope this helps. And I'd be more than happy to be corrected if I have mis-interpreted something.

--- 帖子 #6159 ---
I rechecked the first page, and it doesn't discuss straight consolidation trades. The whole point of a consolidation trade is that the market has been going nowhere for a while -- the longer, the better. Now, if the market isn't trending, and there is extreme indecision reflected in a long line of spinning top candles, then it doesn't make any sense to try to look to the RSIs for direction. The really nice thing about long consolidations is that they are incredibly easy to see, much easier than a three tap set-up. This isn't an evolution of the method. It's simply a different kind of trade from the two that LG discusses on the first page. Another different kind of trade is the Gap trade, which has only been a feature of this thread for about the last month. Instead of looking at them as evolutions on the method, I think its probably better to think of them as different tools in your kit.

--- 帖子 #6180 ---
I will attempt to answer this question, "What is price action?" but it will be inadequate as there has been much written about PA and most of it is beyond the scope of this thread. Basically, PA is the path or footprint of the money as it is being traded. Following PA is the original, "follow the money", because that is literally what we are doing when we watch the movement of the PA, represented on our charts by candles, go up and down. Trading PA is the only way to trade naked, in that PA is happening in real time. Hence, indicators as the RSI are considered lagging indicators...i.e. they lag or form after the movement of the naked price. However, each candle representing PA has a relationship with the candle before it, as well as with the candle after it. The relationship of the candles and placing money (an order) on that relationship is called "trading". Our success as traders depends on how well we are able to interpret that relationship.

--- 帖子 #6181 ---
"Watch price action" means look at the last few candles, and analyze what they are telling you. Price action is what you see on the bare chart (no indicators). Price action does not lie. Get a book on reading candle sticks or go read up on babypips.com website for some basics. " Do a google search for "reading price action

--- 帖子 #6262 ---
Different brokers will have different liquidity providers so will have price feeds showing different prices at any given time; look at your two charts and you will see that the high/low prices on several bars are different because of this. Your two brokers may have different start times to the trading day so the H4 bars may well overlap. The "3" period setting on the RSI is relatively fast so any differences as explained above will be exaggerated when shown in the RSI indicator.

--- 帖子 #6263 ---

--- 帖子 #6299 ---
Apart from the mentioned book by M. Pring ( " Pring on Price " ), I suggest reading " Reading Price Charts Bar by Bar " by Al Brooks. Common repeating bar formations like pinbars, engulfing bars etc. and their use in combination with support and resistance can be found in the james16 thread. There I would read the first 100 - 250 pages and then go through some of the posts made by jarroo ( a senior there ). His posts show how price behaves at major levels and gives you a good learning experience how ceratin single bars on higher timeframes such as weekly, daily and 4h " look " on lower timeframes such as 1h or even 15 min. Hope that helps. ( Also you might look for 1-2-3 reversals, Joe Ross, Ross Hook etc. just Google it or look here in FF. It is not as important as the above mentioned but quite useful as further confirmation. ) _______________ michael

--- 帖子 #6351 ---
Welcome to the thread, TIA. That is a good question and there are probably many good answers to it. I would highly recommend that you start with only 3 pairs, any pairs, to concentrate on for awhile. Post charts and mark them for 3 Taps and BOs until you see those setups without having to draw a single line. I scan about 20 pairs and generally come back to about 3 to really concentrate on. I'm looking at trend confirmation first, then long term support/resistence, then a way for a possible entry i.e. 3 Taps, H1 4C BO, consolidation BO or a channel trade.

--- 帖子 #6353 ---
I would like to add one thing here. If you have the W and D pointing in one direction, and the price is very close to the third tap (either on its way to making the tap, or just having made the tap), it will be perfectly common for the H4 RSI not to line up. The H4 coming into line can then provide the trigger for the set-up. So, if you are looking for trades that are likely to be three tap trades, it may be best simply to concentrate on W and D to find your candidates. If you only look at pairs where all three RSIs are pointing strongly in once direction, you are likely to find many trades where it is too late to get in. Price has already made its third tap, and moved in the direction of the trade.

--- 帖子 #6516 ---
Hi David, sorry it's taken me so long to answer you. 1. Yes, as soon as the gaps can be evaluated after the market opens, I usually choose one or two of the "best" pairs to trade. "Best" is totally discretionary..how large a gap, over all longer term direction, any RSI confirmation of the direction I will be trading, etc. 2. Mine generally is about 100% of gap size, but I just "eyeball" it. I never actually look at numbers and say this is what I am looking for. Gaps can go further than the fill too, so often a trader can get more pips than the actual gap size. 3. I generally do not set a SL on a gap trade, but I don't recommend that anyone else follow my example. Experiment with the SL, if you find that 1:1 ratio is too tight and allows for no play..loosen up on it. I personally really hate to lose a trade that would have been a winner because of a rigid RR ratio. 4. Yes, see #1 above. 5. Yes, 25-30 pips Hope this helps, David.

--- 帖子 #6548 ---
Just keep in mind what the channels are for. The most important thing is that the channels define the stop. So, the channel opposite the breakout direction shows the point at which the reasoning behind the trade failed. With that in mind, you could use either wicks or bodies to draw the line. You are looking basically for the point at which there seems to be the greatest resistance. Your stop will be very close to that point. Asking for more precision than that, in my opinion, is a pipedream. Consolidation breakout trades should move pretty well. So the entry point isn't quite as crucial as the stop. I think that's why LG waits for a full 15 min bar for confirmation. The trade should move well for a few bars, so it's OK to give up 15 minutes or so for better assurance of a successful trade.

--- 帖子 #6549 ---
Maverick, The lines PipPete drew are designed to define a consolidation channel. The more hits you can get on a line the stronger (supposedly) that line is. Placing the upper line on the high body of a candle tags a lot more highs, including wicks, than a line using any of the high wicks would have done. Placing the lower line by using a wick low, tagged a lot more of the lower wicks than using a low candle body would have done. Overall, this gives a trader more confidence in being able to pull the trigger when either line is broken by current price action. Edit: Sorry Duffy, didn't see your post.

--- 帖子 #6551 ---
Hi David, I do not typically wait for the close of the BO candle to close above/below the S/R level. That is when I will move to the M15 chart and wait for a complete close outside of that level. However, the last few trading days have made me a little more conservative, in that I want to see more confirmation that the BO is not a false one. So I am waiting for more than one M15 candle to close and continue in my direction before entry. I only look at reasonable S/R levels fr TPs and SLs, which will often be the prior day's high/low, but I don't ever intentionally look at the prior day's highs/lows for a level. Nothing wrong with it if that's what you want to do. I don't use H1 RSI for exit purposes, although I find greater comfort in the trade if H1 stays with me.

I don't trade exactly like LG but here are my thoughts on this: I consider any BO of the zone valid but some are much better than others, as I'm sure you are aware of. I use trend lines to get me in the trade after the inital BO. On the M15 chart the inital upward BO stalled, then pushed higher and made a retracement right back to the top of the zone. The first trend line showed a break of the trendline that stalled, reversed and then pushed a bit higher. There really wasn't a lot of confirmation on this trend line so it would have been a stand aside for me, while the second trendline showed very good confirmation during the retracement. Once price pushed above this trendline the stop could have been placed either below the current pivot low or the preceding pivot low, both for a small risk trade of at least a 1:1 RR. The largest disadvantage to this trade would have been the weak W1 RSI. I did not personaly take this trade so this is all hindsight, which is a lot easier than doing it on the hard right edge. Price is currently @ resistance and there's reasonably strong resistance just above current price but so far has been good for 20 or 30p's. As I'm posting this, I see that the M15 is doing a retracement, but one should have easily been able to take 20p's or so here. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #6649 ---
Yes, LFB..the approach is a little different at the beginning of the trading week than at the end of the trading week. Reliance on the weekly RSI, which I believe to be the strongest trend indicator available anywhere, is not "firmed up" until about the middle of the trading week. So we look for other confirmation for a trade. That is why BOs are so good for the beginning of the trading week. The same is true of the monthly RSI, we are now in the 5th trading day of the new month. Can we totally rely on the direction of the monthly RSI at this point? I don't think so, although I have never seen hard data on timing. But as the month proceeds, the momentum of the market is such that it simply cannot be turned around easily. Somewhat like a huge ship that has to make a sudden stop...can't be done. When we have the direction of the weekly RSI and the monthly RSI confirming each other as we have now on several pairs, we are beginning to see trend "power". The 3 Tap trade, coupled with an H1 4C BO with conforming RSIs is the most powerful setup and trigger, I believe available anywhere. I do not know of and have never seen a better "edge" for a winning trade.

An mq4 file has to be compiled for MT4 to be able to use...this is explained on the post where the download link resides. The easiest way to compile the file is to close MT4 and restart MT4 again. When MT4 opens, it checks all the mq4 files and compiles any mq4 file that hasn't been compiled before.

--- 帖子 #6792 ---
I've been giving this alot of thought and believe that basically there are 4 steps to becoming successful in this crazy business. Just my opinion, so please add your own comments. 1. Losing - because of one, or a combination of poor money management, lack of discipline, insisting on reaching that TP no matter what, poor set up and entry strategy, poor exit strategy, letting a winning trade turn into a losing trade, "knowing" what the market will do. Ego; 2. Making pips, then losing them - reaching a daily/ weekly goal, then continuing to trade believing you "know" what the market is going to do, the "just one more trade" syndrome, just a few more pips. Ego; 3. Making pips, and keeping them - reaching a daily/weekly goal and stopping live trading, using the rest of the trading week to review charts, watch PA, experiment with set ups and trigger. Humility. 4. Withdrawing profits from account - repeating step 3 again and again until enough money has accumulated for a rewarding withdrawal. Then repeating steps 3 and 4 over (and over) again. Humility. Every trader goes through these steps to one degree or another. The goal is to get to step 3, then on to step 4. I personally struggle with sometimes reverting back to step 2.

--- 帖子 #6978 ---
I would be happy to LFB. I trade from $10,000 accounts live and demo. At one time I traded 2 full contracts per trade with a bigger account. Now I use 1 full contract ($10) per pip because the market has changed somewhat and because I want to trade like I hope most of you are trading, whether live or demo. I am prepared to take a 50 ($500) pip loss on any trade, which is 5% of the "seed" money. I never adjust that with wins or losses...it's always 50 pips. I don't pay attention to R:R ratios..I tried that and found it was a waste of time for me. (might be good for some). I will risk $500 to gain $400. I have laser like focus on 100 pips per week live and will trade until I get that, on demo I usually get many more pips per week. Once I add $5000 to my base/seed account, I withdraw it and repeat the process over again until I build up another $5000...very boring stuff, because my risk is always $500, my goal is always 100 pips. I take profits 20, 30, 40 pips at a time. I am not looking for long pip runs although I think they are great. I just want that 100 pips per week. I hate, hate, hate letting a positive trade turn into a negative one, although it's going to happen from time to time. If I am watching the charts, I seldom set my 50 pip SL. If I am in profit for a trade, I will often move to BE. Looking at this current GBPUSD trade..I will let it go to my TP level which was a R/S level that looked reasonable to me. Sometimes I will exit early depending on PA.

--- 帖子 #7029 ---
I am introducing a new filter to our trading arsonal..the Zorro Continuation (ZC), I call it although it is just a wave pattern that has been used for decades. I am still testing it and have already posted several charts showing it. The Zorro lines are not to be viewed as trendlines, rather they are merely directional lines indicating a breakout (BO), a pullback and hopefully a continuation in the direction of the BO. The RSIs remain our mainstay in determining strong directions. The neat thing about the ZC is that we look for it after a major BO in one direction or the other. It is a way to re-enter a trade after taking profit from a good BO. Please ask questions or give comments...like I said, I am still testing it.

--- 帖子 #7099 ---
Your broker's day starts two hours later than LG's. If you look on her chart, you can see that she is into her second hour of the new day, while you are still on the tail end of the last day. Thus, her daily, H4, and H1 RSIs are all showing strong positive, while yours are not. This difference occurs frequently. I've noticed the same thing between my charts and Scrutch's. I have not yet decided whether it has any real meaning for the portability of this system. It's clear that some people get strong signals at times when other people are showing nothing, and the only basis for the difference between the signals is the time difference between the brokers. Does that matter? I really have no idea.

--- 帖子 #7103 ---
As far as the market is concerned, there are only a few regular time intervals that have any true meaning. Week opening and closing. End of Month. End of Year are the big ones. (Summer doldrums would be another, I guess on a large time frame). Then, on a daily basis, there is the open and close of the major markets -- London, New York, Tokyo, Frankfurt and Sydney. Everyone knows, for example, that fairly big moves tend to happen just after London opens. Also, people talk about the Frankfurt fake-out. Let's suppose that during the Frankfurt session, price starts moving toward a third tap, and makes it to the tap. Then, at London open, there is a reversal and it looks like we are on the way to a good three tap trade. Take two traders. One has a broker that sets its new day at midnight, New York time. The other sets the new day at New York close of market. Because the first trader has a new day closer to London open, his daily and H4 RSIs will always be more sensitive to the moves from Frankfurt open and London open. As I said before, I don't know exactly how this difference will pan out over the long run. And I don't think anyone else really knows the answer to this either. It would take a considerable amount of testing to figure it out. However, I think it's likely that there is a significant and systematic difference here, and a difference that derives solely from an arbitrary vertical line on the chart. Edit: The only thing I'm really suggesting here is that you might find your results differed somewhat if you switched to a broker in a different time zone. That doesn't mean that the method wouldn't work anymore. A robust system should be able to perform well despite such minor differences. But it's also possible that, because of the fairly predictable movements when markets open, some broker's time zones will do better than others.

--- 帖子 #7111 ---
Even if you use the lower time frames, the brokers rely on different banks and different feeds, so even the ECNs and STPs will have variations. The market makers will have even larger variation, since they are quoting their price, which is yet another level removed. But with that said, it should be possible for a coder to come up with a normalized RSI indicator that allowed the user to select the daily start time, instead of using the broker's time. I'm not suggesting that anyone do this. In fact, I think it's probably a bit pointless. But it should at least theoretically be possible.

--- 帖子 #7120 ---
At timeframes from H1 &amp; down, there shd not be any difference in the indicators. But for H4 &amp; D1, there will SURELY be differences if the brokers uses different time for start of the day. Depending on the broker, an H4 bar may be from 10:00 to 14:00 GMT for one broker whereas it is from 08:00 to 12:00 GMT for another broker. These 2 H4 bars MUST be different. They CANNOT be the same. Similarly for D1 bars, as price at 05:00 EST is unlikely to be same at 06:00 or 07:00 EST. But the difference is usually small becos market is normally very quiet in early morning. I think best choice is for day to start at 22:00 GMT now (&amp; 21:00 GMT during DST period). In both cases, it is 05:00 EST, which is the start of a forex trading day. That is why I prefer brokers who start the day at 05:00 EST.

--- 帖子 #7156 ---
Always know which stage you are in! 1. Losing - because of one, or a combination of poor money management, lack of discipline, insisting on reaching that TP no matter what, poor set up and entry strategy, poor exit strategy, letting a winning trade turn into a losing trade, "knowing" what the market will do. Ego; 2. Making pips, then losing them - reaching a daily/ weekly goal, then continuing to trade believing you "know" what the market is going to do, the "just one more trade" syndrome, just a few more pips. Ego; 3. Making pips, and keeping them - reaching a daily/weekly goal and stopping live trading, using the rest of the trading week to review charts, watch PA, experiment with set ups and trigger. Humility. 4. Withdrawing profits from account - repeating step 3 again and again until enough money has accumulated for a rewarding withdrawal. Then repeating steps 3 and 4 over (and over) again. Humility. Every trader goes through these steps to one degree or another. The goal is to get to step 3, then on to step 4. I personally struggle with sometimes reverting back to step 2.

--- 帖子 #7202 ---
AUDUSD I am introducing a new filter to our trading arsonal..the Zorro Continuation (ZC), I call it although it is just a wave pattern that has been used for decades. I am still testing it and have already posted several charts showing it. The Zorro lines are not to be viewed as trendlines, rather they are merely directional lines indicating a breakout (BO), a pullback and hopefully a continuation in the direction of the BO. The RSIs remain our mainstay in determining strong directions. The neat thing about the ZC is that we look for it after a major BO in one direction or the other. It is a way to re-enter a trade after taking profit from a good BO. Please ask questions or give comments...like I said, I am still testing it. Attached Thumbnails http://cdn.forexfactory.com/attachme...1&amp;d=1292386853

Hi LG, hi All I am planning to go live since January with this system, and that is why i am performing a lot of back testing. At the first stage i have focused at BO trades. Looking GBP/USD pair i have found that this BO trades are profitable when traded during significant and well visible trends (at H1 candles). Those trades should be avoided during side trend (for example have a look at time period 10th September to 10th October.) because loosing probability is sky high. My point form those analyzes is: If you consider taking 4C 1H BO for any pair check if: - it is in strong up or down trend now. - how are last few BOs looking, if they are clean ones, or those dirty chopping bastards. Maybe this will help you to increase good trades ratio.

--- 帖子 #7280 ---
Analysing a forex chart is much like analysing a legal program...you go from the broad to the narrow. In law we go from the general legal concept--the broad-- to the particular facts and issues at hand--the narrow. In forex we go from the broad (the weekly or montly chart) to the narrow the H1 chart. For purposes of analysis I am using the EURUSD chart. Starting with a totally naked weekly chart, zoom in so that approximately 5 years of data is on the screen as below.

--- 帖子 #7281 ---
Next, place horizontal lines at the most significant highs and lows. I am using red lines..as below. There is no right or wrong way to do this, just don't "overmark" the chart. I have placed 5 lines on the chart...so marked.

--- 帖子 #7332 ---
Foreigner's are required to pay income tax on income that is sourced in the United States. The code provision which defines U.S. sourced income is 26 U.S.C. section 861. It puts that income into a few categories: Interest, Dividends, Personal Services performed in the U.S., Rentals or Royalties from property held in the U.S., Dispositions from sales of Real Property, Sale or Exchange of Inventory, Underwriting Income, and Social Security Benefits. At first blush, it seems pretty clear that money made by trading Forex doesn't fall into any of these categories. Thus, it may be that you won't be taxed on your forex income. If you make any real money, I would definitely ask a tax lawyer about this before filing any return. I am a lawyer, but not an expert on this stuff. This seems counter-intuitive to me. I would have thought that the U.S. would try to grab more things that have some connection to the United States. And if your account is in the United States, then there is a pretty good argument that you are making money here. That said, the tax code is very often counter-intuitive. So maybe there is no tax. And then again, a plain reading of the statute, like the one I just did on 861 often gives wrong results. What I'm trying to say is that it looks like there is at least a good argument that the income is not taxable here in the US. But it would take more research to know for sure. And if it actually becomes an issue for you, then you should definitely get a better opinion from a tax lawyer.

Another approach would be to go to the 15 minute chart and put up the Average True Range indicator, with the time period set to 16. All you are looking for is the last value in the indicator. This will give you the average total movement every 15 minutes for the last four hours. Then set your order for that distance away from the channel. At consolidation time before London open, this probably isn't off all that far from LG's 10 pips.

--- 帖子 #7406 ---
JG, you mention a global trend several times. I have no idea what a global trend is. The RSI is an oscillator meaning it goes from one point to another. It basically moves up and down, sometimes sideways. But it is also a leading indicator, meaning it indicates what the market is about to do. We don't look at the RSI for overbought/oversold purposes, I believe that is a waste of time for the purposes of this thread, as this is basically a trend trading thread and although recently we have been looking at reversals, that is not the main purpose of this thread. The RSI gives us the overall strength of the market at any point in time. The RSI does not always give perfect signals. That is why we use it along with PA, R/S and TLs to get us in trades. Using patience, as watching the M15 chart before entry is, I believe, about as much confirmation as it is possible to get in the forex market and even that fails sometimes. I have no idea why you consider MAs more reliable indicators than the RSI. MAs are lagging indicators, they give a signal after the market move. I have said this several times now. I believe the RSI weekly signal from about midweek to the end of the trading week to be the most powerful and reliable indicator of trend direction that there is. If someone can show me a better one...please let me know.

Good discussion oradba, fitness and bimmerbob...it is one of the most difficult things about trading..to give up the indicators. The 3 Tap setup and trigger are two seperate steps, don't forget. 1: Theres' the 3 taps (the set-up) and 2: there's the trigger (PA in desired direction). Actually the order is this: 1. Confirmation of direction on 3 RSIs 2. 3 Taps in confirmed direction 3. Trigger by watching PA often on lower TF

--- 帖子 #7481 ---
I check the actual RSI line direction, not the indicator, "frame by frame" or in this case candle by candle on the H1 chart initially with the vertical line tool. The line is between 4 and 6:00 in each frame. It is impossible to tell what the RSI indicator showed in retrospect, but not the actual RSI line. (Another reason to never rely entirely on an indicator!) Moving up to the H4 chart, do the same. You will note that the line is dragging the bottom..it can't do anything else as it cannot go lower and PA is not going up. Same is true on the daily chart..dragging the bottom. PA is also continuing down, PA trumps RSI, at least in the short term. Assuming I had taken notice of this pair at the BO and without the indicator's arrows, I would have entered this trade short on the M15 chart after it cleared the support line. Even getting out after that red candle that cleared the support line..that would be about 60 pips.

I think the confusion I see in some recent posts is that lawgirl is trading the system just like she always has, lining up her trades with the simple RSI without the extra RSI arrows, which came later. They really don't mean all that much most of the time ( the arrows I mean ) as they tend to switch direction very quickly What is more important is what price is doing. Draw a short term trendline. See that the Weekly, and Daily are in conjunction with the RSI direction. When the hourly or 15min chart breaks in your direction and out of support or resistance, enter the trade. Remember: trade what you see! I'm not trading this way because I was distracted trading so many crosses but I lurk here from time to time.

--- 帖子 #7493 ---
I would like to introduce a new trade set up using a naked chart and the traditional RSI(14) with 70/30 levels. This is not original with me. I first saw it introduced by Kathy Lien, but I am sure it is older than she is. Basically it is reversal trend trading. Trading from overbought to oversold and vice versa. I am mentioning it now because there is a set up forming that might be interesting to let ride during the holidays. Please, if you are interested in this trade, try it first on a demo account. It is very simple, but profitable. Here is the set up: --Daily chart (anything less gives false reads) --RSI (14) with levels set at 70 (overbought level) and 30 (oversold level) See EURAUD chart below: For a long trade (which is setting up here) --RSI must be less than 30 i.e. under the 30 line --Wait for a green (up) candle to close (tomorrow at 2:00 p.m. for me). --If RSI has gone above 30 at the close of the candle, enter long at the open of the next day's candle. --Place a SL at the lowest point of the green candle. That's all there is to it. Look at GBPCHF and EURCHF too. They may be setting up soon also. Managing the trade : This is what Kathy recommends and is very effective. --Exit half the position at half (1/2) of the risk i.e. if the SL is at 100 pips, take profit on half of your position at + 50 pips. --Move the other half to BE. Exit the other half if: --BE is hit (duh... ) --PA moves into overbought area (above 70) and heads down out of that zone (below 70). Sell at market as soon as PA moves below the 70 level. The opposite for short trades.

--- 帖子 #7501 ---
I tested this method over the last three years on the GBPUSD. Because the entries are at bar opening, and the exits are well defined, it's very easy to test quickly. Over three years there were 21 trades. Six were losers. Fourteen went to break even after reaching the halfway gain. And one was a pure winner. The winner had an R/R of 4:1. What does this mean. Assume that you risked 2% of your account on each trade. Over three years, you would make a return of 10% on your account. The losses and breakeven trades would keep you almost dead even, while 80% of your gains would have come from a single trade. Twenty one trades is not big enough to evaluate the system. I'd want probably 50-100 trades before I had any faith in the results. That said, the testing was enough to convince me that this method was not for me. I have two basic problems. First, the trades, especially winning trades, can take a very long time. The pure winner took over two months to complete. A couple of the breakevens only got back to break even after about a month. If you traded this from your regular account, then with the no hedging rules in the US, you would be prevented from making a contrary trade on that pair for the entire time that you were in the trade. It looks to me like the potential gains may not be worth the lost opportunities. Second, I don't know how I could get the right position sizes for this system without changing brokers. The stops are often over 200 pips, and sometimes as big as 400 pips. With a 10K account, assuming 2% risk, a 200 stop lets you trade one mini. That's the minimum trade with my broker (and I don't have a 10K account). So I could reduce my %risk/trade, and thus reduce the rewards. Or I could pass on the trades with the bigger stops. However, it looked like a big opening move made it more likely that there would be a good trade. So, I don't see how I could trade this system without going to a micro account. It's really incredibly easy to test this system, and takes no time to do. Spread and slippage are non-issues here, since they are almost a microscopic portion of the trade. And daily data is also pretty solid. So a backtest should be almost exactly as reliable as a forward test. If you are interested in this method, by all means, trade it on demo first. But you should also do some thorough backtesting for whichever pairs you decide to do. (Testing 10 years on a pair should take maybe an hour or an hour and a half. And yes, I know I made the same claim about testing Gap trades a while back, to deaf ears. But it's worth trying again.)

--- 帖子 #7805 ---
You are correct..that USDJPY BO picture could be the poster child/chart for BOs in this system. Your EURUSD arrow did not point to a BO, only a wick/tail poking through. We want to see a multiple candle BO, at the very least on the M15 chart and on the H1 chart, we want to see the candle body breaking. Watching for entry on the M15 chart would have kept you from entering that trade, so there would have been no need to set a SL. Remember that we have time to observe PA on most good BOs. There is no need to jump into a trade at the first hint of a BO. You will notice on your chart that a long BO did occur a few candles after your arrow. It was good for about 30 pips, but there was an immediate reversal on the subsequent candle which produced a very nice short trade.

--- 帖子 #7855 ---
Hi Hawaiifive9, IMHO just follow these steps - one by one: 1) Download the indicator Lawgirl's Trend Display v1.02.mq4 to your computer. 2) Find the location of Meta Trader 4 on your computer. For example: c:/program files/Meta Trader 4 3) In that location there should be a folder called "experts". Open it. 4) In that folder there should be another folder called "indicators". Open it. 5) Copy the indicator into the "indicators" folder. 6) Open the Meta Trader 4 program. If it is already open, close it first and then reopen. 7) Open a chart, or example: EURUSD. 8) At the left, there should be a window titled "navigator". 9) In that window, there should be a group called "Custom Indicators". Expand that group. 10) Find the indicator Lawgirl's Trend Display v1.02.mq4 . 11) Drag the indicator into the chart. 12) A pop up window will appear. It shows different settings that you can change. 13) After you press "OK", the indicator with the trend arrows should appear. Hope this helps. If you still have problems, please let us know in which step exactly.

--- 帖子 #7906 ---
The arrow indicator tracks the direction of the current bar in that time frame almost all the time. What this means, is that if there is a decent current bullish bar, the arrow will be strongly up. If there is a decent bearish bar, the arrow will be strongly down. And when the arrow points sideways, the current bar is likely a doji. I've seen some exceptions to this, and it has generally puzzled me. Since that is almost always true, it does look like the H4 arrow may be out of whack. Take a look at other charts and other timeframes, and see if there are other things that simply don't look right. The RSI indicator is pretty simple to understand. It's basically the average of the upbars over the period, divided by the average of the downbars. There's a smoothing operation that takes place in the way its calculated, but what I've said is the basic idea. The arrow simply monitors the change in the RSI since the last bar, and that change will almost always be a simple reflection of the direction of the current bar.

--- 帖子 #8082 ---
Hi Whatfx, A Gap Trade occurs when there is a difference in price between last week's Friday close price and the price at the opening of the current week in Monday. We assume that price will move to fill the gap, and trade accordingly. You can see some examples of gap trading at this page, from post #7658: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...57876&amp;page=511 Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #8091 ---
Geula, I pulled this below from the front page. If your saying that rsi on weekly,daily, 4hr is pointing down...........Then we are good to go! It doesnt say anything about 1hr RSI Warren Check Trend on Weekly, Daily, and H4 Charts This is the most important part of this method. All three (3) timeframes (TFs) must be in agreement (confirmation) on direction. Perhaps, the easiest way to do this is to attach the RSI Arrow Indicator to your charts. The indicator and directions can be found here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost.php?p=4127792 It is important that you develop the ability to confirm the RSI directions without using an indicator because you should visually verify the positioning of the RSI on the H4, Daily, and Weekly charts before entering a trade. Scan through any or all pairs you wish to trade and jot down only those which have confirmation of direction on all three TFs. Do this by observing the RSI .

Please read the first post of this thread: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...30&amp;postcount=1 LG has done a great job explaining her system there IMHO. If you have questions, please ask. --- 帖子 #8098 ---
I read the book Jesse Livermore - World's Greatest Stock Trader by Richard Smitten over the weekend. While Livermore's personal life was nothing to admire, his trading advice has much to offer. I highly recommend this book...it reads like a intriging novel and there is lots to learn from it...how to trade..how not to live. Livermore basically traded trends (like we do), but constantly looked for trend changes, as he believed that it was a change in major trends that hurt most traders. Here are just a few of his suggestions: 1. Know the direction of the major trend of the few stocks (I shall substitute pairs) on which you are concentrating. He chose only the industry "leaders". 2. Never enter a trade with your full position . Livermore sent out "small position probes" of 1/3 of his intended full position to test his appraisal of market direction. If the first probe was positive, he added the second position, etc. 3. Always watch for end of trend hints . Livermore looked for market price stalls (consolidations), with heavy volume, where price was not making higher highs or lower lows (ditch/channel PA). Heavy volume with no movement in price, he believed, was a strong clue or warning of a potential trend change. He would then send out a "probe" to test the change. 4. Do not spend time trying to figure out what moves the price of a particular pair. Rather, he says, examine the tape (ticker tape for him, for us..PA). The answer is what the PA says, not why it is saying it. The tape (PA) is never wrong.

--- 帖子 #8156 ---
There are no tricks except don't expect too much from a gap trade. It is counter intuitive and counter trend. We need to get in and out as soon as possible. Sometimes they fill quickly and sometimes they take time, but if PA is continuing in our direction, we generally don't worry about how long it takes. Today was a little different. The gaps filled in about an hour then PA did an about face on these pairs. They may still fill, but it is not worth being down 50 or more pips for a gap trade of 15- 30 pips. PA is always correct.

For example, please see this post by LG: http://www.forexfactory.com/showpost...postcount=6985 You can also search this thread for the word "zorro" and read some more trade examples.

--- 帖子 #8235 ---
The indicator will only plot five time frames. The H1,H4,D1,W1,MN seem to be what this method requires and most users want to see. If you want to see the lower time frames just enter M1,M5,M15,M30,H1 in the periods to trade. The time frames need to be the same syntax as MetaTrader...M1 is valid while 1M is not. Separate the time frames by using a comma and no extra spaces. From the following list: M1,M5,M15,M30,H1,H4,D1,W1,MN the user can enter any five time frames they would like to see displayed...but only five.

I don't endorse this but if you insist on showing all tf's on one chart... Make a copy of the LawGirl Trend indicator mq4 file, rename it or just use the new one with the Copy name. Either compile the new file or re-boot your MT platform. You can now invoke a double instance of the indicator on your chart. The indicators are going to fight each other if they are both placed in the same window. You will have to play with the comma spacing, as the M15 and M30 have an extra character to deal with. --- 帖子 #8472 ---
A ZC trade is a H1 4C BO trade that pulls back and then continues in its original BO direction. This happens very frequently after a good BO. I call it a Zorro Continuation (ZC) trade because it bears the "Mark of Zorro"! ZC = BO--&gt;Pullback--&gt;Continuation

Whether it then returns to the upside remains to be seen. One can play the retrace. It is the only time I use a fib line to go from the BO to the reversal candle to get an idea of where PA might go.

--- 帖子 #8515 ---
Most of the time, the RSIs simply show the direction of the active candle. If its up, the RSI is blue. Down, and its red. If its a doji, then the RSI is sideways yellow. That happens well over 90% of the time. Thus, the RSI arrows can turn on a dime, especially at the beginning of a new candle, or when price is still near the open for the candle. Having said all that, it's pretty amazing how well it works to have all of them in the same direction, especially considering how little at times they can indicate.

--- 帖子 #8522 ---
I do not believe there is repainting going on with the indicators, merely a reflection of what is happening with price and momentum at this time. The monthly is unsettled now-- being the 2nd trading day of a new month..the weekly should be getting set by midweek and even more reliable by Thursday. We have never paid too much attention to the H1 RSI. The secondary use of the RSI is to indicate trend (the first being overbought/sold which we pay no attention to). The RSI measures turns in price by measuring turns in momentum. My theory of watching the face of a clock for understanding the turns comes from studying a man named Andrew Cardwell who determined that an RSI level of 50-80 indicated a long turn/trend and an RSI between 50-20 indicated a short turn/trend. Don't know if his helps, but hope so. I find them remarkably reliable, coupled with pure PA and S/R areas, but they are not perfect. And I guess from time to time they will be just as erratic as PA itself.

--- 帖子 #8560 ---
Hi cwl0375, IMHO, there is no magic formula for finding a good BO confirmation through 15M candles. But, there is common sense. Some examples: If 15M candles' bodies fully breaking the resistance/support - that's a good sign. If the 15M Candle is relatively bigger than the previous ones and goes in the right direction (bull or bear) - that's a good sign. If one candle goes up, the second one down etc. and price seems to be ranging in 15M - not a good sign. IMHO, it's a judgment call what PA is doing and where price is trying to go. Just My Humble Opinion, love to hear what people here think about this subject! Thank you!!

--- 帖子 #8620 ---
LG: I think its worth drawing a distinction between the RSI indicator, and the arrow indicator that's used here. One of the things that first drew me to this thread was the idea that it was a "chart lover's" method. The basic function of the arrow indicator is to relieve people of the chore of looking at the charts on the higher time frame. Then, what seems to have happened, is that people place some incredible faith in what the arrows are doing. It's very easy to see what the arrows do. All you need to do is look at the higher time frames. You not only can immediately see what the arrow is doing, but often, you can see when the arrow is likely lying. I don't really have anything against the short-cut. But its not for me. I may use it from now on to help select which pairs to look at. But once I'm focused on a pair, I will make sure to at least look at all the charts for the pair. I'm still learning, and I think there's more to be learned from looking at more charts and maybe taking fewer trades.

--- 帖子 #8626 ---
I would like to make a comment on the RSI indicator repainting question. It is NOT repainting. The definition of a repainting indicator is that it will repaint after the close of a bar or several bars ago to adjust to the optimum level. These are great indicators for showing what happened in the past but nearly impossible to trade the hard right edge of the chart with. The RSI changes while the current bar is still open...but the RSI indicator changes as well. Once the RSI value is printed for a closed bar, it then shows the current bars RSI value. The only repainting of the RSI indicator is just keeping track of which direction the RSI is pointing at the moment... as LawGirl stated in her post. The difference between the RSI indicator is that the indicator is always showing the value for the open bar, while the RSI keeps track of the historical values, plus the current value.

I don't pay that much attention to the mid point of the last swing...but an easy way to do this is to click on the trend line to show the grip points (the small boxes at the beginning, mid point and end of the trendline). You can watch the level around the middle grip to get an idea of a 50% retracement to see how price reacts there. My attention is on the S/R lines that I have drawn...nothing fancy or complicated there. I see an approximate 30p's between support lines and that's enough for me to consider taking a trade. You have to keep in mind that the white line shows me there was a 100% retracement of the previous down move, so this may just be a minor correction before it heads back up again. That's why watching the PA is so important in putting on a trade like this. Please don't mention this to LG, but I've been known to watch the M5 (sometimes even the M1, sheee...even a tic chart now and then) charts. I want to see price making LH's and LL's to justify an order placement and how price is reacting to my support level area. Change your 4 hr chart to a daily chart, you now have 3 candles on a tap, you have monthly rsi pointing up, you have weekly rsi pointing up, you are now waiting for your daily rsi to point up so you can trigger the trade. Make sense? Edit: What im trying to say here is that we are not looking to trade the bounce (because we dont know the bounce will happen), we are looking to trade the confirmation of the bounce, which is why all 3 rsi's need to be in agreement. Would you trade the daily candle when the rsi isnt pointing up yet? I wouldnt id wait for rsi confirmation. Would you trade the 4 hr 3 tap when it hasnn'y bounced up yet? For me id wait for confirmation of the bounce/ trend by waiting for the 3 rsi's.

--- 帖子 #8821 ---
The whole point of a 1hr consolidation trade is that pice has not been moving. And the longer that it has remained stagnant, the better it is for the trade. So, no, the RSIs are not important. It is simply not a trend following trade, because by definition, the consolidation shows no trend at all.

--- 帖子 #8822 ---
In downtrends, you draw the trend lines from the top, not the bottom. You want price to retrace back to the trend line, and then move back in the direction of the trend. With the line you are drawing, that cannot happen.

--- 帖子 #8856 ---
It is not an H4 3TAP trade, because the chart you are showing is an H1 chart. It's possible to take the same sort of trade off the H1 chart. And, if that's what you intended, then this trade would be a legitimate three tap set-up. The entry would not necessarily be at the end of the bar. Rather, you would enter when the price action confirmed the trade. As a practical matter, that means either when the current candle turns green and starts showing some bullish motion, or (what amounts to about the same thing) when the H1 RSI starts pointing strongly up, to 2 or 1 o'clock.
