OK, i like keeping things simple: 1) consolidation is a steady range over time. 2) Range is an identifiable number of xx points/pips. 3) Therefore, a consolidation is generally within 2 parallel horizontal lines. 4) Flag is typically a price channel that is counter-trend. Never heard of "a consolidation of preceding momentum", sounds a bit fancy, but learning all the time......

--- 帖子 #8958 ---
I call this pair the "gift that keeps on giving". But why, let's take a look at it in a little detail. A classic entry technique in trend trading is to enter on either the highest high on the last 40 days for a long trade , or the lowest low on the last 40 days for a short trade. If the market is going to trend up, then it must make new highs. If the market is goind to trend down, then it must make new lows. Here is a daily chart for EURBGP. You will notice the last 40 days are highlighted. PA tells us that we are looking for a short trade, thus the lowest low of the last 40 days is marked with a vertical line and by the arrow.

--- 帖子 #8959 ---
Disregarding the more current PA to the far right of the chart, just by observing PA and marking that lowest low of that 40 day period, we are alerted to a potential profitable downtrend. As we only need the vertical gold line marking the lowest low, I have removed the arrow and the highlighted area. Moving to a lower hour TF and using the H1 4C BO system for entries, here is what we have seen over the last few days...a steady march of PA downhill and right through that lowest low support line of the last 40 days. What is the significance of this? It indicates that there should be more downside to this pair. This general entry technique, by the way, is one that made a group of traders called the "Turtles" billions of dollars in the commodities market.

--- 帖子 #8978 ---
There's a very good book about the Turtles called The Complete Turtle Trader by Michael Covel. It's well worth reading. Very few of the Turtles had any trading success once Dennis shut down the program. The few who successfully trade don't use the Turtle system anymore. It doesn't look like either Dennis or his partner went back to trading the Turtle system. Furthermore, the system was developed for commodity markets. I think there are important structural differences between Forex and commodities, which make the commodities markets much better suited to that kind of trading. Specifically, I think that commodities are much more prone to bubbles and crashes than currencies. Governments and businesses have a very strong interest in holding back extreme price moves in currencies, and less of the same interest when it comes to say pork bellies or orange juice. I tested a few variations of the Turtle system on Forex about three years ago. I tried doing it with the original rules, and then with a few variations to take into account a Forex day being so much longer than a day on a commodity exchange. It didn't find anything that worked very well. Ultimately, the turtle idea works because it takes advantage of fat tails and black swan events. (Most traders work on some variation of mean reversion. The Turtle system takes advantage of the idea that price movements are not distributed according to a bell curve, but instead that there is are more huge price swings than the random distribution would predict.) The biggest problem is that it is extraordinarily risky and requires huge capitalization to make work, even with very conservative money management. However, the story is a great story and well worth reading. And it really illustrates the kind of personality it takes to be a great trader.

--- 帖子 #9063 ---
Sounds like you are managing your losses well. There is no way to avoid losses that I know of or have ever read about. I use reasonable R/S levels as stops. However, I am reading a book by Van H. Tharp that has made me rethink this way of placing stops. Tharp says that the problem with R/S levels as stops is that everyone knows that they are the logical places were stops will be placed. He says, "Quite often, markets tend to stampede in reverse and fill everyone's stop orders before they quietly return in the direction of the trend." To quote the Turtles again, they did not place actual stops because of this tendency of the market, rather they had mental not actual stops for their trades. Tharp goes on to suggest that stops be placed at levels that are not "logical" to the market. Someone else I once read said to place stops "where you are sure the market will not go."

--- 帖子 #9090 ---
Hey all- I'm done for the day so I thought I'd mark up a chart. Seems like some folks on this thread are really nailing it! Please forgive the crazy color scheme- it was part of a grand design but got out of control due to lack of multiple "undos" on my paint program. Just read bar by bar instead of following the text first. The reason I am posing the question you will see at the end of my analysis is this: I lost a lot of money trading breakouts. I would take the break out and when price inevitably retested the breakout zone I would panic and close my position for break even or just a few pips. But when I would take a loss from a stop, I would lose more than I was making from my aborted breakouts, which slowly bled my account dry. Now I like to get in early (not TOO early! ) with a small stop instead of waiting for the breakout. This can be dangerous too, since if you don't know what you are doing those small losses can add up. Anyway since this is the Naked thread take a look at my perspective on how it's possible to just read bar by bar to get a better idea of who may be winning the eternal buyer/ seller wrestling match in your time frame, thus where price may be headed and how you may wish to join it. Cheers, Taters Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #9256 ---
Channel trading is taking trades back and forth or up and down as PA moves within a given area (channel/ditch). This is somewhat risky, but when PA is ranging, it's a good way to pick up a few pips at a time. The trade must be monitored. Channel trading EURUSD through the London session could have picked up about 200 pips.

KillerAntz if you wish to read my advice here comes one: If you are neither as successfull nor as experienced as LG newer EVER "forgot" to set SL, because you always can be wrong. As a newbie you always have to have SL set and risk calculated acording this SL. You can be successful dozen of times but one wrong situation will always clear your balance. So my advice and what i do is to remember that no matter how good setup looks, how wonderfully all fits together i always can go wrong so you can sometimes double the risk (i am trying to not) but you can never play all or nothing.

--- 帖子 #9438 ---
Hi redart007 Here is what i do. I always try to set TP at reasonable price, then i watch PA, and if it stalls or seems to reverse i quit the trade when it retraces the same amount of pips that have left to TP. Other words i always try to keep at least 1:1 risk reward ratio so when PA moves to TP i do the same with SL.

--- 帖子 #9461 ---
IMHO, there are many false breakouts during the Asian session because of the lower volume. I won't go into the cultural reasons for the lack of volume, but it's a fact. I've had limited success at that time, but many traders advise caution. Also the 1st hour of of the London session "stop hunters" routinely challenge S/R levels to take out stops. From the 2nd hour of the London session (when the Brits seem to stop their shenanigans) to the 2nd or 3rd hour of the New York session seems to be the most reliable for true BO's. I live in Japan, so I've learned to look at any possible breakouts usually after 6 pm JST. Often the biggest ones occur at 2 or 3 am after I can't keep my eyes open anymore. (Soooo side-splittingly funny ) I don't know how many times I've fallen asleep at the keyboard waiting for something I'm fairly sure is going to happen. Next thing you know I wake up and the the position has changed 75 pips. Whatever time zone you trade in, be aware that the volume changes with the different sessions. If you go to the OWANDA website, you can get a desktop widget that shows the Asian, London, and NY sessions start and finish times as well as real-time progression. You can set it for your own time zone. This is a free download.

http://fxcodebase.com/code/viewtopic...60ce60042c9e81 It's part of Alexander Elder's impulse system. The bottom is a heat map showing 15min, 30min, 60min, 2hr, and 4hr time frames. The candles are painted in accordance to the 5min version of that same indicator. The chart is a bit messy, I've been tinkering around with the beta version of TradingStation (love it). Edit: if you Google Alexander Elder's impulse system you can read more about it. Removed link. PS: re-read this post and it seems like I'm advertising. Just for clarification: I'm not.

--- 帖子 #9816 ---
IMHO, what LG means is very simple: ALL brokers start the day at 5:00 pm EST (New York). But each trader can have a different local time , according to their local time zone. We use the separator to mark the beginning of the week on each trader's platform. It's much easier than trying to shift the trader's local time to a GMT time. Hope it's clearer now...

--- 帖子 #9885 ---
I don't totally agree with you on not having to do with the RSI itself. Depends on alot of things, including how far along in the trading week we are. For BOs, true we don't much care about the higher TFs, because we are not looking for a long term trade in particular. I always like to see as many TF confrimations as possible, but for BOs-- PA trumps RSI. That said, the H4 and H1 should be in agreement with the direction of the BO. We have no way of totally avoiding false BOs. They weren't so much a problem this past week, but were a real problem the preceding 2 weeks. Waiting for additional confirmation from the M15 chart helps prevent some, but again not all. If the weekly RSI, H4 and H1 are all agreeing, PA is heading in desired direction, and we have waited for extra confirmation of directin on the M15...and there is STILL a false BO.....I cannot think of anything that we left undone, which we ought to have done.

--- 帖子 #9923 ---
Have you ever wondered why, when you enter a market, that market almost instantly (even if you ultimately have the future direction correct) moves against you and takes your position out of the money? The why, is because 90% of the time when you push the buy or sell button on your dealing platform you have been manipulated into doing so. To this some traders will instantly defend their trading decisions and say “no, that is not so, I only enter when my trading system tells me to” What these traders fail to realise is that the Market Makers are manipulating the traders BELIEFS about future price, and they are doing this by causing standard market indicators to come into play when they want them to. Market Makers MAKE a market, this is their role, THIS is what they do. How do Market Makers Manipulate Market Maker manipulation is not carried out on a surface level. By surface level I am referring to the charts that you see on your screens. 90% of traders look at charts to try to glean meaning from movement and patterns. This is a facade, a facade presented by the industry to achieve one outcome, an outcome similar to a slot machine. Let’s pause for a moment to consider the outcomes of a slot machine. 1. You can win on a slot machine 2. You can lose on a slot machine 3. Slot machines have payout rules. The outside perception of a slot machine is that it is there for a bit of fun and you can win if you play and this next spin COULD be your big win. At the heart of a slot machine is a set of rules but contrary to popular belief these are not payout rules. They are KEEP PLAYING rules. By paying out ‘just enough’ to keep you interested and presenting to you the POSSIBILITY of the big win you will keep feeding the machine. The machine that is ALWAYS removing a percentage for the machine owner and tax man. There is nothing covert about this, we know the rules (although there are some that think they have a ‘system’ to beat the slots’) yet you see people pumping in money for hours on end with their own ‘lucky wrist flick’ that gives them the edge over the electronics. Lunacy, yes but that does not stop them playing. The Market Makers manipulate the biggest slot machine in the world. Just like the rules of the electronic slot machine, the financial markets have rules. The spinning wheels that you see on the slot machine are the market charts you see on your screen. The ‘patterns’ that you are told to trade provide the payout percentage for you and the payout percentage for the machine owners. (The Market Makers) This outcome is just like the slot machine that has pre programmed payout rules. The outcome desired has one single purpose which is to KEEP YOU PLAYING. You will never beat the Market Makers but you can join them. Joining the Market Makers involves the abandoning of charting patterns, standard indicators, and $97.00 secrets. It involves the learning of how the Market Makers run their business. Learning how to read the one true constant of the financial markets which is the manipulation of traders BELIEFS about future price. Once you understand how your beliefs are manipulated as a trader and then apply that understanding to the market, never again will you look at the markets and experience a feeling of unknowing or uneasiness. This is an original article by Martin Cole. Forex Trader for near 20 years Please note* These are MY opinions, I have traded my opinions for near 20 years. If you have different opinions and trade them successfully then they are every bit as valid to you as mine are to me. There's been an ongoing debate for years about which session actualy "controls" the direction.

--- 帖子 #10137 ---
Responding to Floppynuts above (I have trouble with that name!) Yes, the 4C BO is set up daily on the first four candles of the brokers new day. That is the R/S framework by which we look for H1 4C BOs, but not necessarily the CBO. I think you are asking what prevented us from entering short. The short term RSIs did indicate short at the first sign of a BO, indicated on the chart below with the red vertical line. But switching to the M15 chart, watching PA, the first 2 candles are very small green candles. Red flag goes up ..I tell myself, "I have to really watch this PA before I get in." Now I am going to wait for at least 2 more full candles to see what they do. They look pretty good. But as soon as the 2nd red candle closes, the next open is with a green candle. Looking at the RSI, I notice that it is turning up. Red flag again . I'm not going to get into this trade short. Patience would have saved a short entry here. It's always a good idea to wait a couple extra M15 candles in the market we have had the past month. Do the same analysis for the long BO here and you will see that it took even longer to get in..about 7-8 full M15 candles until finally a solid entry candle and it was still about a 50 pip trade.

--- 帖子 #10153 ---
This touches on the principal of "Trade What You See" part of LG's method. There will be a lot of difference in the way the BO's look on different broker platforms. At times a US EST broker time frame will look very good on the first four candles, at other times a London based broker will look very good. I explained to Fitness09 a couple of pages back that there will be times that your chart defines the H1-4C-BO as spot on, other times a different broker time will look much better. There is a continous ongoing discussion about which session really controls the major moves. Usually the discussion is locked between the US and London but I've seen users that are convinced that it's Asia, Japan or whatever. Each has their own views on this and I've never seen any hard study that was done to determine which is the best session to watch. I would think that the best way to approach this is to "Trade What You See".

--- 帖子 #10189 ---
Has anyone stopped to consider that the fact of the matter is that the MARKET does not KNOW of a tap? The market is a CONSTANT STREAM of prices, we as humans IMPOSE on the stream a time frame, to which we place a conceptual meaning. The real danger in life and indeed is trading is to trade a CONCEPT that one has formed based on a particular thing meaning a particular thing. How do you separate out a 'tap' from the constant stream of 'taps' to mean any one thing? The human minds seeks form, always seeking form and this tap is just one example of that. Traders, especially new traders all want to BELIEVE in things that SOUND like they should mean something. "Tap" is just a name that has been placed on a arbitrary price change. You would be far better of considering what CAUSED the price tic change rather then trying to name it and give it some sort of elevated status any other price tic due to a name.

--- 帖子 #10190 ---
Has anyone stopped to consider that the fact of the matter is that the MARKET does not KNOW of a tap? I must say that concept has crossed my mind many-a-time. Indeed the market has no memory. For me, it has become a process to try &amp; identify when professional money is at play &amp; the most active time of the trading session. --- 帖子 #10318 ---
Hi LG: I think self-evaluation has been a key factor for me in terms of moving from Stage 2 to Stage 3. One of the things that has helped me is that I created a Breakout worksheet. I fill out all the information I consider before, during, and after taking a trade. It does several things for me: 1) It slows me down; 2) It forces me to justify my decision to take the trade; 3) It provides me with a space to write my comments about the trade while I am in it, and after the trade is finished. 4) It give me a written record of all my trades, which allows me to track my growth, remind myself of the lessons that I learned, and even express my frustrations in a constructive manner. For example, here is what I wrote after taking a failed trade last week: "You jumped into this trade before finishing this sheet. You need to prepare better. You took a bad trade, and had an opportunity to get out at Breakeven. Why didn't you take it? Get it together. You have to mechanical in your entries, and unswerving in your dedication to your process. This trade was a disaster, and you deserved to loss. You lost because of you." While this entry might seem harsh, this level of honesty and self-reflection is helping me turn the corner.

--- 帖子 #10322 ---
Just my 2p's worth: 1) Have you been falling in the trap of trying to identify market turns? try and be happy if you can capture anywhere around 50% of the pips between turns. 2) Do you find yourself wanting to be in a trade most of the time? It may be an idea to alert yourself to watch PA around pre-defined levels - mainly immediate S/R levels, unless it is an obvious trade ofcourse. I am assuming you trade LG's system only. 3) Believe me, often there is a sense of satisfaction merely not being in a trade. 4) I would recommend disciplining yourself by just sticking to BO trades for example, until you gain more confidence. 5) Do you ever try to "revenge" trade? 6) Are you always applying consistent risk/reward principles? Unless all of the above is acknowledge and practiced, money management remains just a fancy term. Losses are part of the game anyway, the point is to keep them to a minimum. And yes, in case you are wondering, I have been there too.......

--- 帖子 #10324 ---
No problem mate. Sometimes it takes a third person to bring to the surface what you know already anyway, but exercising a state of denial. One of the things I make a point of always remembering is that stop-hunting is a dealer's delight. This job is made easy for the dealer because one, for example, tries to identify turns, like millions of other retail traders, and dealers are fully aware of this. So either you have to have massive stops, or get into the habit of entering a position after a retrace, by which time hopefully the spiking of stops has been executed and you're onto a home run. In effect, LG's BO sys works much like that (waiting for confirmation). Also, only deal with a consistent unit(s) of currency; quantify your stop loss in terms of money you will lose as opposed to number of pips (compare how much easier it is to place chips on a roulette table rather than actual cash). Also, try and train yourself to guage the strength of the trend you are trading in. Say, in an uptrend, is the price heading up in the direction of 1 o'clock or 2 o'clock? In time you will learn to place smaller/bigger SLs dependent on trend strength.....but, practice is essential.....good luck!

--- 帖子 #10330 ---
FWIW, I learned a lot about trading the FX markets from Ellie Taft, a trader I have a lot of respect for, and the author of "Dad's Legacy, Blazing the Forex Trail to Your American Dream". She cites an 8-year performance study which showed that 36.3% of all profits came from trades entered on a Friday, as opposed to Monday, 11%. Tuesday, 20%, Wednesday, 12.5%, and Thursday, 20.2%. These stats were based on regular 24 hr. trading days 5pm EST to 5pm EST. I live in Japan. The time here is GMT+9, and my trading week ends on Saturday morning at 7. When I get up every morning, I'm looking at the start of the Asian session. During the week, and while perusing this forum, my mid-afternoon is when most Americans are contemplating hitting the sack. But by the start of the New York session, I'm ready to turn in. In real-time we can talk about active trades because then, we're on the same page. And while I don't keep those kinds of stats for my own trading, Ellie's stats seem to me to be fairly accurate. That being said, your post seemed to ask about the number of times positions are taken on a daily basis as per day. For myself, I have a basket of 9 pairs that I look at daily. Same 9 everyday. I never trade outside these 9 pairs. LG looks at far more markets than I do. Some look at less. A lot of people here like the Swiss Franc crosses. Some only trade the EURUSD. My point is that the way one trades will affect the amount of "looks" one has to see a trading opportunity. And as for the day and the amount of trades...well, I usually don't expect much out of Mondays and have been known to (cough, cough) blow Mondays off. But I never miss a Friday . --- 帖子 #10389 ---
Whenever you buy you have ALREADY created a belief within yourself. If you doubt this then the next time you want to buy, try selling. Crazy! Yes BUT the point is you will NEVER buy or sell a market until you believe the market is going to move in your favor and that is a fact. We are always predicting. Since you cannot yet see the next shape at the right hand edge of the chart, you are predicting what that shape will be. EVERY trade is prediction. To trade successfully over the long haul one must change the perspective on how one looks at the market. The market is not their for a traders benefit. The market is money extraction machine run by the market makers. We are allowed to participate as 95% of trader supply fuel for the machine. IMHO The way to success is to view the market for what it really is (a money extraction machine) and then before EVERY trade ask a question.......IF I was a market maker how would I extract money from the masses? Well how would you...........If you view the market from this perspective it takes on a whole different meaning.

--- 帖子 #10464 ---
Having period separators on your chart really helps to focus the trading area. Please read my comment above about being too early in the trading week to look for 3 taps. Had you been set up for a breakout (BO) trade, you would have caught a run up of over 100 pips. Look in this order for trades from the beginning of the trading week: 1. Gaps (if you like the action, it's not for everyone) These trades are usually good for 20-30 or more pips. 2. H1 4C BOs after the first four hours/candles of the opening and there after all week long after the first four hours of each new trading day. 3. Consolidation BOs at any time throughout the trading week. 4. H4 3 Tap Trades after a trend has been established.

Yes, you got it..we don't worry so much about longer TF RSI directions because these BO trades are over fairly quickly...usually from 1-4 hours, so it is great to have the H1 and H4 RSI favoring the direction of the BO. Again, PA trumps RSI direction for these types of BO trades.

Some schools of thought say dont trade the first break - wait the pullback and then a return to the desired direction. Hope it helps

--- 帖子 #10645 ---
As with comment on Strick's, what was the RSI suggesting at the time you entered the trade? I am by no means suggesting that the RSI is a holy grail, just that you should at least refer to it if you choose to have it on your chart. I also often find that upon initial breakout, the channel can act as a magnet to price, drawing the price back into the channel, frequently dispatching it out the other side; so unless you are confident with the entry, it might be wise to wait for a retrace and then enter, by which time hopefully the SL hunting has also petered out.

--- 帖子 #10693 ---
The difference is because FXCM has a no-dealing desk price rates while FXDD is a market maker. It means FXDD is re-quoting the price. FXCM just streams the actual price to the platform which is provided to them.

--- 帖子 #10696 ---
Actually the real reason for the difference is because Different Brokers operate off of Different GMT offsets. This causes the daily and 4hr candles to be off from broker to broker. FXCM is GMT -5 and FXDD is GMT +2 so this means FXCM's daily bars close at 5pm EST and FXDD's daily bar closes at 9pm EST thus causing the 4hr candles to be off by 1.

--- 帖子 #10728 ---
I do not trail my stops because sooner or later they seem to always get hit. I rarely set a stop for the same reason..they seem to always get hit unless they are around 100 pips away which I often use as a stop, when I set one. I do not recommend this to others, however. I never look at R:R and will set a 100 pip SL looking for 30-40 pips. However, I will never allow myself to take a 100 pip loss on an H1 BO. What I have found is that often, like today, most "reasonable" stops would have been taken out only to have PA then go in the desired direction. As you have probably read here, I am particularly goal oriented and look to make 100 pips a week. I find it extremely easy to do most weeks. This was a very good trading week and I hit my goal early. With that goal, I am looking for 20-40 pips in a breakout. I often miss bigger "runs", but I don't care...I never look back, I only look for the next trade until I have my 100 pips. After that, I demo trade and experiment the rest of the week. If there are several pairs setting up and all things appear equal, and say 3 are setting up for long trades and one is setting up for a short trade, I will always take the short trade, as I much prefer shorts to longs. Not sure why, but they are more profitable for me. It is probably not a good idea to have more than two correlated pairs going at once, although on a particularly good trend, I may have 3 accounts each in the same trade. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #10736 ---
Interesting what you say about long and short trades. For the small moves we are talking about, it probably doesn't make any difference. But in the broad picture, longs should be easier than shorts. Let's say a pair starts at parity, say USDCAD. From the perspective of the real economic players, a move to 2.00 is the same as the move to .50. Each move makes one currency worth twice as much as the other. That means there is always a little less fundamental pressure on a long move than a short. But as I said, it probably makes no difference to our trades. (The same reasoning explains why losses are so much worse than gains. If you lose 50%, you have to make 100% to break even. But if you gain 50%, you only have to lose 1/3rd to lose it all.)

--- 帖子 #10737 ---
If you think about it, there shouldn't be any difference between longs and shorts in FX since going long EUR/USD equals going short USD/EUR. And in spot FX, it's USD/JPY while the corresponding futures at the CME are being quoted inversely. That being said, I prefer shorts, too. In the stock market and the indices, they just move quicker while up moves usually take more time.

--- 帖子 #10742 ---
I think that point is true for a majority of markets. The structure of Forex, I believe, is different. If you took a basket of currency heavily weighted to the dollar, I would agree that it's much more likely for the dollar to fall quickly than for it to rise. But in Forex, we trade the relationship between currencies. If the Dollar falls quickly, that means that GBPUSD shoots up, because the relative value of the pair goes up.

--- 帖子 #10845 ---
Sorry, I can't post them..they have come and gone. But you can go back and study them yourself. You should be looking at the difference between the Friday close and the Sunday open. For me with FXDD that is around 2:00 p.m PST. Basic gap trading is this: if there is a gap up of more than 25 pips (25 is arbitrary) then enter a short trade. If there is a gap down of more than 25 pips, then enter a long trade. It is counter intuitive and no one seems to know exactly why some platforms show them. I don't care why they happen, they are generally profitable, as most gaps will close up, if not completely, at least partially.

--- 帖子 #10886 ---
Hi Survivor, Welcome to the thread! I will try to answer your questions as far as I understand. LG and everyone please correct me if wrong. 1. Basically we look at the RSIs of 4H, daily and weekly to define the trend. It is explained very well by LG in the first post of the thread. It is true that the RSI can change until the candle closes. However, when all RSIs point in the same direction it is a good setup, because it's a good indication of the overall trend. 2. If you are referring the the 3Tap H4 setup, we do require connecting 3 points ("Taps") to establish a trend. This is also discussed in the first post of the thread. Hope this helps. If you have more questions please ask...

--- 帖子 #10920 ---
I did this early on in my trading career with a system that only ever failed 2 times in a row over a span of 3 years, 2 in backtesting and 1 demo. Most of the time (in my experience) when you finally go live on a system, it seems to do the worse (either week, month, whatever) exactly when you go live as if the brokers know you are doing it. Never fails for me, but the martingale system actually worked for me for about 6 months. I was happy. Then the unthinkable happened and the 3rd failure hit. Fortunately, the 6 months of gains covered this one loss. Unfortunately for me, it happened again 3 more times over the next 6 months. Just a change in market. Besides that, mine only went 3 deep with larger stops meaning I needed larger lots to recover. This meant the 3rd trade was quite huge lot wise. Talking about sleepless nights and sweating. I thought about only trading the 3rd one and hoping for the best, but it happened so rare that you couldn't make any money off of it. Of course I say rare until the market changed. Anyway, it taught me a huge lesson in that you should always expect the unexpected with forex. I'd say don't do it.

--- 帖子 #10965 ---
Some people, including myself, asked the question why did LG's day start one candle behind ours, and people gave the reason that it was because of her broker. I just downloaded the new version of the software my broker uses, and I noticed the delineation was an hour ahead of where it usually is, and it was because I forgot to change the time to CST. I went and changed it to CST, and the day marker went ahead a candle. So, if we wanted our charts to start with LG's charts (bc of the 4 1hr BO trades), then I could just leave it a GMT+0:00. No one may care, but an "ah ha" moment happened, and I thought I would share it with the people who were asking about that.

Aloha - I think I'm starting to "get it", however a few things are being stubborn allowing me to get my head around them: In #1 above, mention is made re: RSI activity &amp; the first post is suggested reading. The first post encourages to enter upon the 3rd tap (not wait for close of candle), while it is entirely possible the RSI may not be favorable at the close of the candle. Enter mixed emotions #2 above addresses Survivors concern about needing 3 points to establish a trend. If 3 points are required, then there are quite a few 2 point trend possibilities-until the close of a candle can establish a 3rd point, and at the same time is now the 3rd tap. Sooooo, there now being a 3rd tap, entry should be asap - not waiting for the close (as per page 1). This scenario basically dictates the 3rd point used to establish trend is always the 3rd tap. Any commentary to help clarify is welcome...

--- 帖子 #10991 ---
Aloha - Think I've got the broker session differences figured out . I'm trying to understand why the precision as submitted on page 1: A. Find the directional bias on weekly, daily, H4. All must match at the time of set-up. B. You will be looking at the bodies of the first four H1 candles of a new trading day...disregard the tails (wicks)....whenever that is for you. That is one reason period seperators need to be placed on the chart. The new trading day hours may vary from broker to broker. The market &amp; price action are not aware of this, so my high / low can be considerably different than another broker, simply due to their "business hours". So, are we dealing with a method that has certain characteristics unique to the start of a new business day? To suggest that going back 2 candles is okey dokey seems to take away from the thunder of the prescribed set up. Seems as though conflicting results would be a given.......or not?

--- 帖子 #11069 ---
If that pair had been under my radar...which it wasn't, here's what I think I would have done. I don't think I would have entered long because of the quality of the H1 candles. The next to last green candle marked by the arrow is the first one to close totally outside the resistence line. But let's assume that there was an entry on that candle. I enter, I don't bother to have a stop or a TP, because the trade it right in front of me. PA goes up on that candle and on the next candle. I am watching it at every hour change now and am up about 15 pips. The third candle opens and it is red....I'm not liking that. Then I notice that PA is a an H1 resistence level and now I really see a red flag. PA will do one of three things at resistence levels...even minor ones like this. 1. go right through it; 2. try to go through it and "bump" it several times before it either succeeds or gives up trying or 3. be repelled by it.. .which is what happened here in no uncertain terms. I take my profit at the open of the red candle and sit back and watch PA and the RSI direction. By the second red candle marked by the red vertical line, the RSI has gone below the 50 mark and it looks like it is going to continue down. I may have entered short there. Entry around there would have been about a 100 pip move. If I have waited for PA to clear the support line, I would have waited for the next H1 candle and entered from the M15 chart like a regular H1 4C BO entry. This entry was good for about 60 pips. Either entry would have been a winner. That is the beauty of following only a few pairs and not the whole market. I have said several times on this thread, a living can be made following one or two pairs and trading what you see on them.

--- 帖子 #11073 ---
I look for the quality of the candle...is it mostly wicks, is the body solid, can I see it moving? Along with that, I watch the RSI..not the arrow, but the RSI itself. Take the USDCAD chart above again. Looking at the RSI line, it made a dramatic turn downward..remember that the line is following PA. The line is telling us what PA has done and is doing..not what it is going to do, but what it is doing. This is what I call "reading the trade". Try to never let a winning trade turn into a loser. It will happen sometimes, but generally when I analyse why it happened to me, I realize that I had set an arbitrary "goal" for the trade by setting a hard TP. PA doesn't care about my goals. Of course, we often have to set hard TPs and SLs because we cannot monitor 24/7 and that's when we try to use reasonable R/S areas. Ideally though, like the USDCAD trade could have been, we trade in the moment, reading the trade and following the "instructions" it gives us and going where it tells us to go.

--- 帖子 #11118 ---
Aloha - wanted to put a few things out there for ANY response/commentary/pros/cons etc. 1) When we "box" the high &amp; low of the candle body after 4 1H candles, we can switch to a 4H to also see the info that the "box" provides. In both instances, there are more often than not the wicks above &amp; below the candle body, which may be seen as "exploratory" prices. 2) I'm sure we've all seen price break the "box" but not the price of the exploratory high/low...resulting in a retrace, sometimes for the good &amp; sometimes not so. 3) Sooo, I've been working with price to break the "box" &amp; also break the wicks' high/low (15M) as a confirmation, with surprising degree of success. 4) If I'm in a really conservative head - like trading GBPJPY (which is like watching a water beetle on crack), I'll wait for a close (confirmation) outside the "box" (15M), then trade the break of the high/low of that candle. If the high/low has not broken the exploratory, I'll wait for it to do so for an immediate entry. 5)As a side bar, I've also had a certain degree of success using the other side of the box as SL (adding 3-5 pips).

--- 帖子 #11188 ---
I see exactly what you are talking about. Most times watching the M15 chart will keep us out of trouble, but I may have entered long there too on that H1 green candle. However watching from the H1 chart, the next red candle would have told us something..fast. Exit a long position on that red candle. Then either ride the next 3 red candles down (channel trade) for 15-20 pips or more conservatively, stay out until PA is more decisive. The next long green candle (another channel trade) would give us another 15-30 pips. Then the real ride starts. At first it looks like just a channel trade, but turns into a true BO trade. That move is good for around 60 pips. I did not catch any of this..mind you and hindsight is everything. But watching just that pair.checking it every candle change would have been lots of fun and very profitable. I am convinced that watching..watching..watching is the key to this current market.

--- 帖子 #11215 ---
Hi I've been trading 3-taps for a few months on all pairs available on IBFX. However most of the times setups will appear on more than one pair at the same time. To be on the safe side I don't take pairs related to each other at the same time (E.g. EURUSD + GBPUSD) because if one setup fails the setup on the other pair (most likely) may fail as well. At the same time I take trades only on pairs not direct related to each other (e.g. USDCAD + EURNZD). Cheers

Almost exactly right, except on a H4 chart, we don't watch the M15 chart.,....don't care what it is doing as the TFs are too far apart. --- 帖子 #11389 ---
Exit Plans for H1 4C BOs are different if the trade is being watched then if the trade is NOT being watched. If watched: Then follow PA and the RSIs using reasonable S/R lines as goals. If not being watched: Set reasonable TP and SL at S/R lines. If in the money when you check on the trade, take half off the table and let the other half ride with SL at BE+. Can do that with a watched trade also, of course.

--- 帖子 #11394 ---
Study your charts, go back through a few pairs and note how many H4 spikes you can find..not many. That is why the trade needs more room, time and to be monitored from an H4 chart. An H4 trade "deserves" at least a candle change to find it's way. The higher the TF, the longer the trade. For example: I entered the AUDJPY trade at the end of the 2nd hour of the H4 candle. The next H4 candle changes in about 10 min. This is a positive trade, but assuming it was not, I would stay in the trade at least until the candle change to see what PA and RSI does.

--- 帖子 #11573 ---
LG...I enter when price breaks the high/low of the "scouting candle" &amp; ONLY wait for a close above/below that spike if I am being CONSERVATIVE . If I am feeling a little more aggressive, I wait for a close outside the box (regardless if it breaks the scout or not), then I enter when the high/low of THAT candle is violated. Actually, if I'm in a 3T mode, I go to 15M on the 3rd tap, and if I feel the trade is a "continuation", I wait for a 15M CLOSE (above/below) SR, and then enter when price breaks the high/low of that closed candle. More confirmation

--- 帖子 #11574 ---
As a sidebar to my previous comments: Typically, I will box the entire price range of the high / low that has taken place in the 1st 4 hours, including the wicks. Now - if price looks like it's going to break the box either way, I go to my 15M chart. IF price closes outside the box, I'll enter the trade when price breaks the high/low of that closed candle. If price breaks the box, but does NOT close outside of it, I now have my "scouting wick". I can now decide how I wish to proceed as per the discussion(s) recently posted. For me...the 3T entry is more structured, as I previously outlined. If continuation is indicated, that entry will wait until a 15M candle breaks S/R &amp; CLOSES beyond the break. THEN, I'll enter when the high/low of the closed candle is broken. Confirming the confirmation - hehehe

When Feb starts to get in the 50's during the day the sap begins to move and the buds start to swell. The more heating degrees we get above 40's the more the buds swell. As they swell they become tender to lower temps. The chemical companies will run freeze test each week to see what temp will kill at what degree. This is the time of yr we have to start smudging or use wind machines or water to raise the temp. Wind machines will only give you 3 to 4 degrees, what ever the upper air inversion is. If you look back at the scenery pic you can see a few machines in the background. Our heating season can last until 1st of June.

--- 帖子 #11620 ---
Thanks LG &amp; everyone else posting here, &amp; the moderators for making this forum a pleasant experience, &amp; excellent place to exchange &amp; transform ideas, learn &amp; grow. I've read the 1st 50 pages or so, &amp; checked a few charts, &amp; I like what I see. I checked out the 3 period RSI by inputing the formula into a spread sheet, then applied various Closes to see what results I would get, &amp; found that if the latest Close equalled the previous Close, then RSI(3) remains unchanged (horizontal or 3 o'clock). While this information doesn't assist with your other o'clocks, I find it helpful in that I can put the last Close of Weekly, Daily &amp; 4Hour bars on the 4Hour chart, &amp; can see how many pips price is from 3 o'clock in the various timeframes on the one chart. Hope someone finds this helpful. Thanks again LG &amp; Team. Billy T

--- 帖子 #11820 ---
We don't take the time to try to understand why one pairs moves and the other does not. All we try to do is to follow what is happening at a particular time, with a particular pair. Great traders, as Pete said, know that the market is always right...whatever it does, it is right. That's why there cannot be ego or emotion involved in successful trading. If we are on the right side of the market and make pips, we are happy and move on....if we are on the wrong side of the market, we take our loss and move on.

--- 帖子 #11831 ---
How to calculate the value of one pip (point) on the spot for gold and silver? By dividing the cost of one contract for the number of points, we obtain the value of one pip of gold - $ 10, one pip of silver - $ 50. The above calculation would be for a full size lot. Calcs would have to be revised for the mini and/or micro lots. Gold and Silver are calculated in points and tics...not pips, but it's just a acroynm thing and the contract size for Gold and Silver is totaly different than the curriencies.

--- 帖子 #11845 ---
Remember that 3 Tap trades need confirmation of direction on the weekly, daily and H4 RSIs. This confirmation has been hard to come by as of late, hence, in my opinion, there have been fewer good 3 Tap set-ups. Additionally, it is generally taking until mid trading week or later to find this confirmation. As I scan charts right now, I see only four pairs that have the weekly, daily, and H4 confirmation and two of them have weak daily confirmation (but I would still count them). This is the first criteria for even beginning the search for a 3 Tap set-up...confirmation on the 3 TFs. Then to step 2.

--- 帖子 #11846 ---
I will try to answer some of your questions. 1. Weekly confirmation is not needed for BO trades as they are generally only 1-3 candle trades. 2. I tend to sometimes ignore S/R lines, but I don't recommend that others do that. I am trying not to ignore them and I generally do not for higher TF trades. 3. No. I don't take them immediately. I always move to the M15 chart to wait for an entry. Sometimes I wait for 1-2 hours for a close below/above a R/S area and more recently, a close below/above a scout or probe wick. Following the M15 candle PA keeps me out or gets me in a particular BO trade . Regarding bias...I have no emotional or ego driven bias regarding any pair. I may have a trend bias depending on PA and trend direction, but even that, I am willing to abandon immediately if the market "says" to do so. I prepare for trading by repeatedly scanning charts, looking for general trend direction and making note of the pairs I want to go back to review. Then I "break down" the pairs that I will be looking to for trade set ups--meaning I look at them on different TFs and make note of what might happen. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #12041 ---
Personally, I set my BO lines using the wicks - kinda like a master candle trade, only the wicks can be on any of the 4 candles. This gives me a high &amp; a low on price within that time frame, &amp; price "always" either tries to break through or will move away from those parameters - that's all price can do. If it's a BO, the close outside &amp; entry just beyond the close can help as a form of confirmation. If it's a reversal, I count back 3 candles from the reversal candle (15M) &amp; enter at break of high/low of the highest or lowest of those candles. Good for confirmation &amp; keeping out of whipsaws. Need the room in the channel or box tho'...I like to set a pip target for half the pips of the range of the box.

--- 帖子 #12305 ---
Hi Walad, the BO setup does not need confirmation from the monthly, weekly, or daily RSI. That makes it far too complicated. Because this trade is generally a "fast" trade, meaning sometimes over in just one candle, PA is what we are looking for. Then as PA goes, the H1 and H4 candles will follow. And if a BO trade goes on long enough..of course the daily RSI will follow, etc. For this trade, PA trumps RSIs...but again...the RSIs will follow as PA goes. PA is the master of the RSI and RSI is PA's obedient servant. Once you see PA moving through a S/R line, move to the M15 chart and watch for entry there. Hope this helps and glad you have joined us.

--- 帖子 #12380 ---
Hi all, Have a question. After entering a trade, do you guys monitor it like a hawk or you will look at intervals. The reason I am asking is that I tend to monitor it closely and don't let it run enough or I get too upset with retrace and up with losses...

--- 帖子 #12381 ---
I don't no if I will answer the way LG would or the others that monitor this thread. I will try to give you my opinion. I like watching it like a hawk if I can. During the time waiting I may go up and down in the tf to reassure me of my trade direction. Then continue monitoring the smaller time frames for direction. I like to look at the other currency at the same time. Example if I entered a trade short with usdjpy then will waiting for it to go to the next resistance level I would watch ausjpy, eurjpy, gbpjpy, or etc to see the strength that jpy has with the others. It may help you see the other currency's s/r levels that effect your own trade as well. Buy looking at different tf such as 1hr. 4hr. daily, weekly etc you will get a feel for what you may need to risk on pull back or where you don't want to go there. If your going to walk away from a trade because of work then I set a smaller tp and sl according to my risk comfort. I'm sure others can elaborate even better than I. Hope I have not confused you.

Hey guys, I'm trying to come up with good values for Breakout levels. I know that it's best to watch candle strength, wait for closes on smaller TF, etc. However, sometimes I am not able to stay around my machine and would just like to play around with some set and forget levels, similarly to how LG mentions she sometimes does this before she goes to bed in post 1. For instance, we could use upper BO level + 1 ATR(500) as a Buy Stop level and lower BO level - 1 ATR(500) as a Sell Stop level. We could then use the lower BO level as a stop for the buy stop and the upper BO level as a stop for the sell stop. What do you guys think are good values for a validated BO, if you had to make it mechanical? 1ATR(500), 2ATR(500) or just a standard pip value? Or maybe something else? The reason I think we would want to avoid the latter is because some pairs are much more volatile than others. IE, comparing EURGBP to GBPJPY. Different pairs should probably have different validated BO levels. Looking forward to everyone's input, especially yours LG. Thanks in advance

--- 帖子 #12458 ---
CrucialCraig: I will be interested in coming up with a mechanical break out levels. I have a similar problem of not staying in front of computer during the London or New York session because of my time zone and work schedule. I have been playing with H1 4C BO for some time with a mechanical buy/sale stop order with not much success. I live in west coast so I set my stop order around 10/11 PM our time and close in the morning. With this type of set up (set and forget), I found that RSI 3 direction is not really very helpful. Even if I found RSI level for 1 hr, 3 hr and daily is up when I went to bed but still the price finally moved to down in the night. This week, I have started little differently and that matches with your concept. I am not paying any attention to RSI direction. I am just putting a buy stop order slightly above the last swing high on the top of 4 hr upper break out level. Stop loss would be few pips below the lower level of 4 hr break out. Similarly, a sale stop order also. Just one week is too early to determine the success of this strategy. The only problem with those days when just a spike gets the orders filled and reverses. -FX_California

--- 帖子 #12459 ---
Hi FX_California, Good to hear someone else is interested in looking at whether this type of approach can be profitable. I'd like to clarify a few things that might help: As far as I know, you should not be using RSI for 4 1H BO trades. Since they are usually pretty short and we are just trying to grab a few pips, RSI signals are often too late to give us a good BO trade. 10-11pm PST is a little too late to set your trades, don't you think? You must miss quite a few BOs. I would recommend setting them shortly after the 4th 1H bar closes (around 6pm PST). I'm also pretty sure we need to look at less than a Reward:Risk ratio of less than 1. LG, please let me know I'm incorrect here but I think we need to give these trades a little room to breath. I'm contemplating starting with a 2:1 Risk to Reward ratio. Lets see what we can come up with once some of the higher level traders can give us some input. How much room have you been leaving between the BO lines and your buy/sell stops? I think we need a minimum of around 15-30 pips. Anything less than that would surely get triggered on false breakouts. The smart idea might be even 30+. This is where I'm hoping LG can help us out since she has so much experience with these BO trades. -CC

--- 帖子 #12482 ---
I believe this is because regardless of whether DST is in effect or not, our broker (FXDD) opens at 5pm EST. So when compared to some foreign markets, we are actually seeing the market an hour earlier than we were a month ago. FXDD doesn't shift when they open up their trading for the week when DST changes; they open at the same time regardless. You could compare it to an international export company. When DST hits, that export company is not going to adjust the time it opens it's doors to make sure that it is still in sync with the foreign import companies. They will continue opening at their normal operating hours, IE 8am EST. Which season is better for American traders using a broker such as FXDD? Who knows. I think Gap trades can be profitable at either of the starting times. At least that's how I understand it.

--- 帖子 #12755 ---
No..all manual. You don't have to be glued to the monitor though. Just look for setups when you can. They happen 24/7. For 3 Tap Trades : Try to keep the entire list of pairs RSIs/Arrows posted permanantly on a chart and when you have time, glance at it and see which pairs have RSIs confirming in the 3 TFs we are concerned with....then look for set-ups. For H1 BOs : Check the charts anytime after the first 4 hours of your new day. London session is best, no doubt about that, but I never trade that time and I do pretty well.

--- 帖子 #12763 ---
Well, once you have downloaded the indicator to your computer, you open your HD, then go to "Program Files", look for "MetaTrader4" folder, then open the folder named "experts", the search and open the folder "indicators", you'll see a bunch of files the with extensions such as ex4 or mq4, finally just copy the indicator you previously downloaded and paste it in this folder, or just drag it into the folder... you'll have to reboot MT4 before you can see it on the indicator list. Hope this helps.

That means from 6:00 p.m. PST to 6:00 p.m. PST the next day for me....because my broker's new day starts at 2:00 p.m. PST....but each trader has to determine their own broker's start time. --- 帖子 #12832 ---
It is the Ireland news. This might be a real big deal according to Reuters. Dublin wants to impose losses on banks' senior unsecured bonds not covered by a state guarantee, which currently amount to over 16 billion euros, as part of a new deal with the European Union, the European Central Bank (ECB) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF). "A sustainable and comprehensive solution for Irish banking that involves recapitalization but also involves an element of burden-sharing ... That is certainly the outcome that the government is looking for," Simon Coveney, minister for agriculture, told state broadcaster RTE. Under an EU-IMF bailout agreed late last year Ireland can impose losses on banks' junior debt, but the ECB is opposed to treating senior bondholders, which are ranked on a par with depositors, in the same fashion for fear of a contagion risk. Ireland's new government, elected in February, has said the state cannot afford the current EU-IMF bailout deal and European finance ministers will decide on what sort of concessions they can offer Dublin in coming weeks. They are awaiting the results of fresh stress tests on Ireland's banks, expected to show a capital hole of around 25 billion euros, on March 31 before deciding on any new deal.

--- 帖子 #12886 ---
Hi jason, well that explanation is just one way we've been using to enter, it was first introduced to me by LG of course and it's always improving, so with a little practice you might as well come out with a better method and share it with us... Regarding SL and TP, well I don't want to sound boring and repetitive but when it comes to BO trades, it's all about observing PA, at least for me. Let me explain a little further: 1. When I enter a BO trade I will watch PA closely and come to any decision based in PA's actual behavior. 2. Open of new M30 and H1 candles are specially interesting moments to observe PA, you can come to a decision on getting out of a trade by observing PA at this points. 3. Support and ressistance levels are also important to watch when PA comes close to them and you are in with a trade, as you observe how PA behaves around this zones you can come to a decision on staying in or getting out (taking a gain or assuming a loss) 4. The next thing I consider when entering a BO trade is trend, normally if I got in a BO trade in the direction of a mayor trend (look at the NZDUSD chart I used some days ago) by this meaning daily trend mainly, I'll cut it some slack if it goes against me, because the odds are PA will eventually go with the trend. If I entered a BO trade in the opposite way of the trend then I'd be a little bit more conservative and AGAIN observe PA for signs to get out. I'm sorry I can't give you an exact number of pips or something, but this is the way I handle enters and exits, and the exact number of pips you can bear an opposite move depends on your risk level and personal trading style. I hope this helps tho', and should you have any further comment just let me know and I'll do my best to help.

--- 帖子 #12900 ---
Hi WP, well this are interesting zones / moments for me to observe PA because it gives me information on whether the direction of the movement will continue or a reverse might occur soon. What do I look for in PA movements? Well, let's say we got in a short BO trade and PA just hit a support level, I'll watch closely and see if PA will go through this level or bounce on it, or I'll just plainly take my profits and get out. It all depends on current market conditions, how PA got to this level (i.e. did it got here with one single long movement?), and how it reacts when reaching this level. Experience, as usual, plays a crucial role in observing PA and taking decisions based on it (not that I have a lot, but we build it day by day right?) Regarding candle changes I usually observe PA in a new M30 candle to see if price will move in my direction with renewed strength or it has run out of momentum, and possibly get out. In a new H1 we must be looking for signs of reversal, say if we were short and after watching the new H1 for the first minutes you see it is starting a bullish movement then you know it's time to get out. This might sound too simple to write and hard to apply, but again, practice makes the master, and we're getting there... so, hope this helps, and have a great afternoon!

--- 帖子 #12902 ---
IMO this has lots to do with trading psychology, we must be aware and come to terms with the fact that not every trade we get into will hit my TP in the next few minutes and sometimes PA will start to mave against me just at the moment I got in. What I do here is just wait and observe, you can't just get out in panic as soon as PA goes against your trade in the first few minutes! Take into consideration that you had a valid reason to get into that trade (you had it right?), so you also need a good reason to get out of it, this reasons may vary but fear of losing should not be one of those reasons. Reaching your maximum planned loss for your risk / reward level or watching PA give a set up to go in a trade against your original position are some valid reasons. This is just my opinion, some people in here treat this differently. Hope this helps!

--- 帖子 #12918 ---
Glad you are getting something out of this strategy. It is so simple, it often seems complicated, if that makes sense. It does require judgment, patience and flexibility...things every trader does not have innately, but can develop with study and experience. Because the 3 Tap is based on the H4 candles and is generally confined within the current week, the more H4 candles that have occurred, the more likely the 3 Tap set ups. Therefore, we see very few at the beginning of the trading week. Tuesday through Thursday produce the most 3 Tap set ups. Remember too, that the weekly, daily and H4 RSIs in the same direction are the tip-off to look for 3 Taps.

--- 帖子 #13045 ---
Hi qweretyq, that's such a good question and LG had a great explanation for it. I do the same thing , analyze S/R levels on multiple time frames and adjust my TP accordingly. Here are some of my rules that help me determine S/R levels and try to follow as much as I can: 3T's – to be valid S/R line must touch 3 most recent bottoms or tops , the more the better Write down S/R levels on H1 D1 W1 MN for pairs I'm watching S/R around round numbers are always stronger Areas of resistance become support and areas of support become resistance Whenever S/R not clear stay out S/R around major news might not be valid Hope this helps.

I agree with everything you summarized except no. 5. S/R levels will always be clear on some time frame. The higher the TF the more run room, but less "structure", for lack of a better word, because PA seeks levels, yet rarely goes straight up or down to that level. I look at it this way: PA aspires to reach a level/goal. Those levels/goals are R/S levels or areas. If those levels/goals are too far away, PA will "play around" before getting there. Kind of like walking home from school was...you knew where you were going, but you took your time getting there--stopping to talk to friends, kicking rocks back and forth, etc. That's why S/R levels as close to your trading setup time frame are the most obtainable...less "playing around" opportunity.

--- 帖子 #13155 ---
IMHO...wait for more confirmation. I've tried to enter as early as possible which usually results in a trade that I wished I had never taken. The probe at the top happend on the bar you entered on...after the fact. So...if you had been trying to buy about six bars later you would want to keep that probe in mind. BO trades can be taken in either direction, but keep in mind that they are short duration trades. Once in a while they turn into longer term trades and it's a sweet ride. LG uses the H1-3T for the longer term trades and the RSI's have to be in agreement before entry.

I´we been working with the same issues and currently on demo because of similar experiences. IMB(borrowed)O especially with SL´s you have to accept mentally that you will lose the money invested if the trade goes to SL. This kind of mindset might work atleast in 3 taps, where you can set a side for a while and "forget" the trade. One way of seeing this is that by entering a trade you have allready accepted the fact that there may be a loss (this is the hard part atleas for me). By accepting that loss you can really let go of the money and let the markets do their stuff. Sometimes it will end to profit and sometimes loss and it´s the probability of your system to make profitable trades that counts. It´s also about the trust and confidence you have on your system. You have to have trust in it to do what it´s supposed to do and "forget" the money invested in a single trade. It´s so easy to think that narrowing your SL you decrease your losses, but what happens is that you will end up losing more trades because your trades lead to SL more often and have no room to breathe (as LG said). This kind of a mindset has helped me to go on, but unfortunately I can´t (yet.....) say this with a voice of deep experience of making serious money in forex. I´ve thought this so that it doesn´t matter if your original 3 tap is invalid or your timing to enter isn´t exactly right. When 3 tap is formed even though it stays on e.g. a resistance level and doesnt break out immediately it is still more probable that it will evidently break out to the direction of the trend. Sometimes it will and sometimes it wont, but the probability to go with the trend is higher. It may take a day or two to do so and if it doesn´t end to SL it is still more probable that it will evidently go to the direction of the trend. Just an idea of successful 3 tap going to wrong way. If you took it like this and according to the definition of trends the following low cant be lower than the last one so if you put your SL below the last low, there is rather high probability of success if the trend doesnt change. How long should you ride. One way to exit is to trail your stops just below previous low (or high) while the price goes on. If you would have stayed with this originally 3 tap for two weeks, it would have made easily + 400 pips or even more so 140 pips risk for this one would paid off good. There are several other 3 tap setups also during the trend. On this example there is a scout wick just before the entry. If one had waited the price to pass that wick, there wouldnt have been an invalid trade. Yóu can also see that with tight SL´s several of them would have hitted SL.

--- 帖子 #13227 ---
The Difference Between Demo and Live Trading : Psychologically it is just different and there is no getting completely around it. But we can minimize the transition as much as possible and we do that with familiarity i.e. doing the same thing the same way over and over again until we are so comfortable with the process that we are almost bored. I highly recommend demoing with the size account that you will be trading live. $5,000, $10,000 or higher. That way the lot sizes are exactly the same in the transition, thus taking away one psychological problem. It makes little sense to demo on a $100,000 account then move to a live $5,000 account as everything changes--lot size, potential profit and loss, your entire mind set. Sameness/consistency is what we are looking for in making the transition. It's much like an animal trainer teaching a dog a trick...same thing over and over again, with rewards in between. A $10,000 live account is ideal, if possible. Trade it with the same lot size over and over until the account gets to $15,000. Do not vary the lot size until you reach $15K. Withdraw that $5,000 and do something with it. (Give it to your spouse to spend without any questions asked...they deserve for all the time you have spent on trading and ignoring your family!) Then start again with the $10K with the same lot size , same everything, until it gets to $15,000 again, pull out the $5,000. start with the $10K again....nothing changes..no psychological hurdles to overcome because it never changes, as we are not trying to double our account (even though we are doing exactly that) Trading is really very boring because of the sameness of it all.

--- 帖子 #13330 ---
You will only use the wave pattern when trading the 123 reversal pattern. This part of the method is just an added bonus. The "flag" or pull back is the basic methid. The key to unstanding this trading method is knowing the trend. For that you must take a larger view of the 5 min time frame. Second you must be able to idenify multiple areas of support and resistance. This determines whether trend is up or down. The ability to determine trend appears to be the hardest part of the basic method for most.

--- 帖子 #13352 ---
Hi mark, well I don't know if you can even change the way MT displays the period separator, because asi you know, they are aligned with your broker's new period. There should be no problem if you trade BO's for the first 4 candles of your broker's new period, but if you don't want to do and want to make your charts seem the more alike to saay LG's charts, the you could just set the Daily_LinesBoxes indicator to cover the candles you want it to cover. Making it clearer, for example: if your broker's new period starts two hours later of LG's new period (this means 2 H1 candles of difference) then you might want to set the following on your LinesBoxes indicator: Start Hours: -2 End Hours: 2 This way your indicator will enclose the two H1 candles previous to your new period separator and the two H1 candles next to the period separator. Hope this helps

My evening has gone with some analysis with 3 taps on E/U. 10 months backwards. Used only 4 h timeframe so these do not take into account possible trend changes in larger TFs. I tried to include even the ones which could have been like 3 taps when they existed (taking them is always aiming at moving target anyway). I took them from about a half of the trigger candle. Nor did I took any S/R lines into consideration. A little bit different and maybe more realistic setting than in my previous analysis. I didn´t start them on monday and some of them continued to the next week. If you put your SL below/above last swing low/high, it seems that 13 of them hit SL. Most of them during times when there was no clear trend or ranging to both directions. --- 帖子 #13412 ---
As Fitness said, I also like to keep things simple and don't overthink the process. There are a few things I always like to consider when taking a 3T and they help me keep things simple: 1. Go with the mayor trend, (this seems obvious as we look for confirmation on RSI and this mark the trend, but as you'll see in the chart below first days of month/week may give a different look on the RSI and the actual trend) 2. Once I found a setup I like to switch to H1 and look for an entry here (PA in the direction of my trade, just a personal preference) 3. Observe PA closely in case trade went right on against me and not rush into assuming losses if I don't see any clear signs of reversal on the actual trend. This chart shows a beautiful wave pattern on EURCHF and I actually traded the last retracement short, because RSI pointed south for both W1 and MN (first days of the week / month of course). It was a bumpy ride though and I didn't enjoy it so much, but eventually it was worth +30 pips.

--- 帖子 #13466 ---
The first four hours set our daily range against which we measure or judge price action. It makes us ordered (if that makes sense), by setting our boundaries. It gives us a structure or framework from which we can function. That's really all there is to it. Yes, you are correct in thinking that any consolidation period of 4 or more candles could make a good set up. Again, that would give us a period of time from which to measure price action. It can and does work on any TF. H1 4C is my way of finding a point of reference in a market that is in continuous motion.

Thanks for the link; I think it is worth posted the scenarios right here! Will it break now? Here are five scenarios: 0.25% hike, unclear message: In this scenario, Trichet hikes the European Minimum Bid Rate by 0.25%, and doesn’t send out a clear message about future moves. This will likely result in a “buy the rumor, sell the fact” outcome, in which the Euro slides, and has a chance of losing the recently conquered level of 1.4282. Probability: high 0.25% hike, clear message about making a series of rate hikes: By keeping the heat up with “Strong vigilance”, the Euro is likely to rise, with a chance of proceeding to the 1.4450 level. Probability: medium 0.25% hike, clear message that this is a one time event: In this case, Trichet returns to the normal tone of “monitoring the situation”, which means no more hikes in the near future. This will likely result in fall of the Euro below 1.4282 and towards support at 1.4030. Probability: medium 0.50% hike: In this scenario, the markets won’t wait for Trichet – the Euro is likely to move higher and can even break above 1.4450. The extent of the move will depend on his words, but this scenario is definitely Euro-bullish. Probability: low No hike: Some members said that the move isn’t certain, so there’s still a small chance of this happening, although the higher inflation gives it a very small chance. In such a scenario, EUR/USD will lose 1.4030 very fast and Trichet’s words will become meaningless. Probability: very low

--- 帖子 #13552 ---
I believe we have had much discussion about this, but no harm in repeating it. Q: Whenever you see price breaking thru the s/r line, do you wait for the h1 candle to close completely outside that line and THEN move to M15 to look for entry? or do you move to M15 as soon as you see price moving thru the s/r line? A: I put the pair on my watch list as soon as I see the H1 candle move out of the S/R area. That is the beginning of a set-up . The trigger comes when a M15 candle has closed completely outside the S/R area and is continuing in the desired direction. If a scout/probe wick has been sent out past a S/R line, we should wait longer..maybe even another M15 candle or more before entry. There cannot be a hard and fast rule like "wait until two complete candles close before entry", because every trade is different and entry is not an exact science. PA trumps everything and what it does determines when we enter.

--- 帖子 #13603 ---
I'll try to help a bit with SL and R/R. For 3TH4 SL, if set, is absed on resistance around 100pips away from entry to give enough breath room. It doesn't mean that trader will wait until it is hit. PA must be observed and earlier exit shall be applied when scenario is obviously no longer valid. There is no rule regarding R/R. Even for 30pips SL may be 100pips away. It is essential to watch PA and prevent winning trade from becoming lossing one. Please look a couple of pages back and you see some trials done by Whistlepips on hystorical data. He was so kind, so he shared his observation regarding SL and TP and also regarding possible wins and losses. Simplified, but interesting. I'm sure that LG will correct me if it is necessary.

--- 帖子 #13613 ---
Enter after a close of an M15 candle COMPLETELY (including wick) outside the S/R lines marked at the first 4 candles of your brokers' new day. However, do not do so blindly...give enough time to watch to see what the next M15 candle is going to do. Is it going to continue in the BO? Or is it turning around? If it turns around and has sent out a probe (wick), then that probe becomes the new S/R line and the waiting and watching process begins again. Hope this helps..

--- 帖子 #13712 ---
Im not sure theres a clear answer to your guestion. Check out Anthars explanation on page 895. I think that it is really good. Enclosed is a part of it, especially the first point on going to the direction of the major trend has really helped me with 3 taps lately (and of course all the explanations of LG). Can you predict has there´s been a turn in the major trend? Maybe you can and maybe you can´t 1. Go with the mayor trend, (this seems obvious as we look for confirmation on RSI and this mark the trend, but as you'll see in the chart below first days of month/week may give a different look on the RSI and the actual trend) 2. Once I found a setup I like to switch to H1 and look for an entry here (PA in the direction of my trade, just a personal preference) 3. Observe PA closely in case trade went right on against me and not rush into assuming losses if I don't see any clear signs of reversal on the actual trend. --- 帖子 #13887 ---
You already know there's a win in every loss, and this is great. I can just say to you... IMHO, looking backt at a loss trade with the intention of analysing what you did wrong, what made you stay in when you could've closed and the emotions involved in it is what ensues the win in that loss. On the other hand never look back at your lost trade with regrets or complaints of your actions, you did the best you knew or could at the moment, regreting it or "punishing" yourself for doing something you can't undo is like banging our head on a wall, it's crazy acting. Don't take this the wrong way, it's not a criticism directly for you in any way, it's just a thought that equally applies to me and to any other person that finds some use in it. Soo focus on your current trade, know you are improving trade by trade, and go get the coming trades armed with the experience your recent losses gave you. Wish you a succesful week at the end!

--- 帖子 #13922 ---
There is a results tab in the visual tester - see the attachment to this post. Right click on the results table, save as report (html) - it will produce a detailed statement of all positions made during the test. That is why I think everyone can benefit from this test, because it will be possible to check every position, TP and SL, and the test will be more credible than someone making entries in ms excel sheet. There should be also log files for the test in the following path: /yourPlatform/tester/logs. Moreover these logs can uploaded in the Journal tab of the visual tester. (i haven't checked how it works yet, but looks very promissing - maybe we could share logs from the test). I will be using LG setups and indicators. CustomCandle is only because it is not possible to change TF during the test. If CustomCandles need a clarification then I can make one. I do not advise using this candles in trading and I do not use them myself, because they make the picture unclean (eg. for me consolidation and S/R zones mess up with custom candles on my charts). The simpler, the better. Agree. PM me please

--- 帖子 #14153 ---
Guys, what you need to remember about the 3 taps trades is that you are trading either the top or bottom of the channel. If the channel is broken and the trade goes against you, then you need to watch the PA closely. It's very likely that there will be a retest of the channel. If that fails get out and move onto the next one - you should never be losing 100+ pips on individual 3 tap trades in the hope that PA will once again turn in your favour - let the candles do the talking. Good luck for the rest of the week.

--- 帖子 #14157 ---
It's very important to treat every 3 tap trade individually and you should do your homework before you jump in on the trade. For example, work out where the important supply/resistance levels (S/R) and then plan accordingly. Price action on the 15 min charts will tell you when to jump in. Once you are in, you can then set your stop loss above/below the nearest S/R levels. If the trade goes your way, then once you reach the first S/R level then maybe reduce your stop loss by 50% (moving straight to B/E could end up very frustrating - alot of the time the trade will re-test your entry level and then move on in your favour). Or simply take the pips at the first S/R level and move onto the next 3 tap. It depends on the trader - some may just get in and out and be happy with 20 to 40 pips. Some may be of the opinion that the trend is their friend and hope to ride it all the way.

Be prepared for changes all the time, I had the same problem of hanging in shifted trades to long!! Now I use a simple moving average to alert me I put this MA on all my charts its 20 on the close for a 1H chart so that makes 80 on a 15min and 5 on a 4H chart. To make it more easy to spot click on line instead of bars or candles If the price come near the average get prepared for a probable switch of market direction.
