I just did some checking with sl on H1BO´s on E/U from any consolidation for the last couple of weeks. I concentrated on London &amp; NY sessions, but didn´t see any significant differences on Asian. What I saw was that the amount of sl is related to the risk. I.e. the more sturdy the breakout, the bigger the sl. Makes sense, doesnt it? The more risk you take, the more the profit also. Depending from the situation, sl was from 15 to 40 taken from 1 hr BO candle. Not more, not less. This is by no means a thorough check and should be adjusted to the overall wideness of range of currency pair in concern. In e.g. gold or oil, it probably should be more and less in e.g. usd/jpy.

Potential ZC setting up

--- 帖子 #14326 ---
They are very simple, but fun trades. There are 3 stages in a ZC (Zorro Continuation) trade: 1. the original directional PA move..be it up or down; 2. a PA move in the opposite direction for as brief a time as one candle; 3. finally, a PA move or return to the original direction . (Up, Down, Up or Down, Up, Down) This is really just a wave pattern. Step 2 is always a "pullback" or "retrace". It is called Zorro because of the "mark of Zorro" from the movie character Zorro who went around marking things with a Z. Our "Zs" are mostly a little sideways. It is called a Continuation trade because ultimately PA returns or continues in it's original direction..be it up or down. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #14373 ---
The H1 4 candle breakout set-up: A. This is a price action (PA) trade and the weekly RSI direction does not need to match the direction of the trade. Because this is considered a "fast" trade...meaning over in a few hours at the longest...only the H4 and H1 candles need to confirm direction, but they will do that if PA moves in the desired direction. B. You will be looking at the bodies of the first four H1 candles of a new trading day., whenever that is for you. Disregard the tails (wicks). Period seperators MUST to be placed on the chart. C. Place horizontal lines at the highest high of these four candles' bodies (not including the tails, if any) and the lowest low of these four candles' bodies , again, disregard the tails. These lines are really just R/S lines. D. Wait for a breakout in the direction of the bias. E. Enter from the M15 chart, when at least one candle has completely cleared the R/S line in the desired direction. The entry takes discretion, as the quality of the candles is important to observe. NOTE: You can set this up several hours after the fourth candle that you are observing. For example: My first four candles are from 2:00 pm - 6:00 pm. I may not get to the set-up until 8 or 9 p.m. That is ok, in fact, that gives time to observe PA. Do verify the directional bias again, however. PLEASE SEE POSTS #1029 - 1032 ON PAGE 69 FOR COMMENTARY AND CHART EXAMPLES

--- 帖子 #14589 ---
This is an interesting pair at an all time high. Take a look at what is happening. We know that PA can do a very limited number of things when it hits such a huge resistence level. I think of a resistence level as a kind of line of defense...it is there to hold the line, to keep the PA "crowd" back. What happens when the PA "crowd" meets the line of defense (we saw this at the Royal Wedding over the past weekend...the bobbies holding resistence lines to keep the crowds in check). The PA crowd can only do one of three things. It can 1) bump the resistence line , pull back and bump it again, like a crowd surging, it can 2) go through the resistence if there is enough volumn and momentum i.e. a large enough crowd, or it can 3) be repelled by it and turn around and "go home". Which one of these events is happening on this chart? I believe at this time, it is number 3.

I'm far from being an expert, since I just started trading this method, but I have had a few BO trades go against me this week. Mine came from taking the trade to soon without waiting for confirming PA. What I mean by this is that it would show one strong M15 candle and not wanting to miss a potential move I would take the trade only to have PA stall and retrace. So without specifics I would say this might be the problem. What I'm seeing is that I need to wait and see PA confirm the BO and accept the fact that I will be missing some of the move. Another thing is that if the BO is against the main trend, I need to monitor the trade closer and take whatever it gives me when PA shows signs of stalling. On a more general note: there have not been a lot of big moves this week. I think that is because of the expectations of a poorer US NFP.

--- 帖子 #14635 ---
It helps, LP, to have your R/S lines marked at the first 4 candles. Here are the steps: 1. Determine the main trend...here it is long; 2. PA should first go in the direction of the main trend...which it did here; 3. Then PA should turn around and go in the other direction...which it has and very decisively....that would have been a good move to catch; 4. Finally, PA should turn again and head into the original direction. A good ZC would look more like the chart below.

--- 帖子 #14658 ---
No problem. Channel trades are really simple. Once the S/R lines are established, price often bounces back and forth between those lines...I have no idea why and do not care. But, this happens very, very often. We have seen this time and time again throughout this thread, but on the H1 chart. Pippete is a trader who seems to especially like these trades and has posted many of them. I shall try to point you to them. On the current chart, price is at an all time high at the resistence level. There are only 3 things the new monthly candle (May) could have done. I discussed that a few pages back. For now..the first week of the new month, price has been repelled by the resistence line and has turned around-- thereby heading down the channel. What to expect? Price may or may not continue on down to touch the bottom line (support line). That would take months to happen. Keep in mind, though, that the farther we get into the month in a particular direction, the harder and harder it becomes to turn price around on the higher TFs. It is kind of like trying to turn a huge ship around on a dime...can't be done. Hope this helps.

Hey CC How do you trade your gaps ? Is this something LG has in her thread somewhere? ( As I have read the entire thread ) If not can you point me to were I can get a better understanding of the the Gap Method you are using. Thanks in advance

--- 帖子 #14738 ---
It's been discussed. Basically if it gaps up you sell, if it gaps down you buy. The gap needs to be large enough to cover the spread and give an acceptable return. Not all gaps close, but most do. Sometimes it takes a few hours or a day, but it's usually within the first few hours. One thing to be aware of, is that sometimes price will move in the direction of the gap before it turns to close the gap. Taking this into cinsideration, one should not blindly enter on the gap, but should monitor price and pick a good entry.

--- 帖子 #14739 ---
Excellent explanation and covers all there is to gap trading.

--- 帖子 #14741 ---
My stops are not for the feint of heart, and I don't recommend using them unless you are well educated on risk:reward scenarios and how the profit/loss chances of a particular system can greatly influence how different R:R ratios can be safely implemented. Take a statistics class and you will understand why there are a large number of R:R ratios that can be used profitably (This is just my personal opinion/findings. Unfortunately, I am still working a full time job - take my advice with a grain of salt!). Personally I have found higher Risk:Reward ratios to be more profitable in the long run in regards to gap trading. I consider myself an aggressive trader so occasionally I will take a hefty loss; but I use sound Money Management and it would take a few consecutive bad weeks for me to get into real trouble. I might be starting a separate thread at some point but for now LG has been a great educator and this is my home -CC Also - Some Google searching will bring up some good resources where you can learn more about gap trading and why it is and always has been a successful trading tool is financial markets.

--- 帖子 #15018 ---
In commemoration of reaching 1000 pages and while waiting for the paint dryingly boring monthly chart trades, I have been working on a new entry on the daily charts that seems to be working very well. It is quite simple. 1. There must be directional confirmation on both the weekly and daily RSI . If monthly also, the better, but not necessary. 2. Enter in the direction of the RSI within the first few hours of the beginning of your new daily candle (whatever time of day that is for you), say within the first 6 hours (although 6 is arbitrary). The point is, we are trying to capture as much of the full day as is possible. 3. Immediately place a 30 pip SL. Then forget about it. 5. Next day at around the same time check the trade. It will have done one of 3 things: a) hit the SL, b) taken off, or c) ranged around. If: a) Oh, well...go to the next trade; b) Great, decide whether to TP or add a position if direction continues; c) Wait it out, That's all there is to it. Rinse and Repeat....

--- 帖子 #15019 ---
The CLASSIC head fake Use the 15 min candles.... You are in a strong current trend... often a 'retrace'; not always... 'Suddenly'... Approaching the 'top of the hour' Look for this in the last 3-4 minutes of the current 15M candle: note the Time remaining on the candle http://img196.imageshack.us/img196/8125/gbpq.png With in the LAST 10-20 seconds... place your trade... (I loaded up.. but a single entry is FINE!!) Be 'ready' to BE WRONG! (You won't lose much if you are... seconds count) FINGER on the exit trigger. (I have 2 experts: Close all trades/Reverse all trades) Then...... Either: within the LAST 1-5,6,7 seconds you should (begin) to get your confirmation ... and the creation (10/30 seconds) of the NEXT candle should absolutely get you positive. http://img856.imageshack.us/img856/3650/gbp.png Whether you take 'quick' profit or hold depends on the PA. I watched that next candle... and exited all positive. Obviously I was 'wanting' to hold .... but "You never know... until you find out" http://img860.imageshack.us/img860/3650/gbp.png It's one of my FAVORITE 'moments'.... I wait for it all the time. Believe it or not.... it's a fairly 'safe' trade... when you anticipate it. Not saying 'safe' because of any guarantee... I'm saying 'safe' because (timed properly) you can EXIT if you have to with very little loss... and HOW MANY TIMES have you seen the momentary head fake SCARE you out of a good position only to watch the resumption of a trend? I find the 15M Candles are the best ones to handle the timing properly. Hope this helps some with handling the Price Action. Cheers, G.

--- 帖子 #15077 ---
Good questions, TradinSD. Yes, you will always want the M15 candle PA to be confirming the H4 and H1 RSI directions. If the M15 moves in both directions over several candles while looking for an entry, chances are the H1 direction has changed or fluctuated, indicating lack of strength. I monitor these trades on the H1 chart, as I do not like the M15 chart for following trades only for entries, but that is just a personal preference...just as I prefer short trades over long ones...no good reason. Yes, stop is based on risk tolerance. But more and more, I am looking to let winning trades ride and even adding positions on positive moves. And yes, look to S/R lines to see where price might be going or where it might get "hung up". Hope this helps.

If you think this is complicated or I have not been able to explain it well, just forget it as its not important as long as the use of the H1 BO indi is concerned. The charts look a bit different because of the reasons stated above but the Price action is the SAME (noticed?) So, if you are in India and your 1st 4 hours look different than others, doesn't matter (its the same case with me, since I'm from India too..cheers!). Try to get to the logic of H1 BO and just apply it to your chart and trading.

--- 帖子 #15180 ---
There is no TP on this trade setup. This trade is intended to take as much profit as the daily candle has to offer.....or hit the 30 pip SL. That's why it is entered as close to the open of the new daily candle as possible, when the weekly and daily confirm direction. If the trade survives the day and confirmation continues the next day, add another position. There could eventually be a dozen or more positions. The overall purpose of this trade setup is to eventually catch a trend that lasts several days to months. With added positions along the way, the potential for pips is tremendous...could be hundreds of pips, even thousands. Look, for example, at GBPUSD on the monthly chart and notice that huge move down that started in Aug 2008 and lasted 7 months...thousands of pips. That's the kind of move this setup can catch .

--- 帖子 #15266 ---
I'll try Zaq, but I don't have any special insight into price action. But maybe I can give you a different way to look at it. Think of PA as the walking around or "pacing" back and forth of the price of the currency pair. We observe this "pacing" when we watch PA, as it is happening in real time. This "pacing" becomes a footprint on the chart, and this footprint becomes a candle. A candle is the footprint of price. A closed candle tells us everywhere the footprint has gone ...everywhere. But it does not tell us where the footprint is going. We cannot control this nervous pacing footprint, we cannot tell it what to do, or where to go. It acts like a stubborn mule that is sometimes obedient, but too often willful. It gets tired and sometimes rests for awhile (consolidation), but we cannot prod it and make it get up and move, we can only wait for it to start moving again, sometimes fast and furiously, at other times slowly and deliberately. However it moves, the best we can do is study where it has gone as an indication of where it might go. That is what we try to do here, with R/S lines and the RSI indicator that tracks the footprint. Watching BOs is watching pure PA as it is happening. Using the M15 chart for entry is as solid an entry as I know of...but still, this nervous footprint can do what it pleases, when it pleases, so we get surprises. I know of no way to avoid them.

--- 帖子 #15369 ---
The first step of finding 3 Taps is to look for conformation of direction on the weekly, daily, and H4 RSIs. This is critical. Some people start by looking for the taps first and trying to get the confirmation later, but that is not the procedure. Sounds like that is what you are doing. Here are the steps and in this order : 1. Scan the RSIs . Eliminate any pair that does not have the 3 RSIs confirming. List those that do. 2. Go through the list of confirming RSI pairs one by one ...starting on the H4 chart. Observe the direction and the candles. Look for the 3 Taps...which is only a trendline...is a 3 Tap there? Is one about to be there? 3. Remember a setup is different from a trigger . A setup is the 3 Taps. A trigger is PA or the candle, moving in the desired direction. Never enter a short position on a green candle. Never enter a long position on a red candle. This is where patience comes in. Sometimes we have to wait for a H4 candle or two for the trigger and by then the RSIs may have changed, so the trade is no longer valid. Sometimes we find the setup and trigger too late and have to decide whether we have missed the bus. (That is a good time to check the daily or weekly charts, maybe we could enter on a higher TF.) That's all there is to it. DO NOT look for the Taps first...the RSIs will eliminate most pairs right off the bat. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #15389 ---
Where's the question? ps - got it. Yes, many do wait for the candle close but this close is not conclusive. Many times a candle closes above a resistance but still falls back and continues going down. Waiting to confirm the break out is prudent. But do note when it happens. Normally a critical candle close happens at the open or close of a trading session (NY, Asia, London, etc.). If this happens at this point, it is wise to wait and see how that open takes it. Also check which level (s/r) has been taken out by this close and with what force. A strong move taking out a significant level is more likely to survive.

--- 帖子 #15393 ---
Since we are talking about him... here are what he considered his most important rules and in this order: 1. Decide on the overall direction of the market . Be sure of the basic trend. It is the line of least resistence. 2. Develop a entry strategy. Probe the market. Test it by trading small positions first. Do not rush in with your whole position until the market is tested this way first. 3. Be patient and wait for the move to play out. i.e. number 2 above. Livermore first started using this approach in 1906. He used it for the remainder of his trading career. He credited this strategy for his success. Notice, dear traders, that we are also following this strategy!

--- 帖子 #15395 ---
The very interesting thing about 3 Taps is that we "find" them, we cannot generally anticipate them. We find them because we are looking for them AFTER the RSIs are telling us to look for them (confirming direction). That confirmation of direction is like a neon sign flashing "look for 3 Taps, because conditions are ripe for them!....look for 3 Taps, because conditions, etc." So we do what we are told and go looking. When we find a good 3 Tap line (remember, a 3 Tap is just a trend line..generally with wave action taking place between the taps..but not always or necessary) it may already be triggered and we have to determine if we want to enter or not depending on lots of factors that I really cannot teach a trader, but mainly on PA and how far into the H4 candle it is at the time. But we might find just the setup with no trigger and have to wait until the next candle to determine what PA is going to do before we enter. Never enter a long trade on a short (red) candle. Never enter a short trade on a long (green) candle. Summary: A 3 Tap long with third tap on a short candle = setup but no trigger A 3 Tap long with third tap on a long candle = setup and trigger [opposite for 3 Tap short] Entry is just that simple....and just that complicated.

For the H4 3 Tap, we do start within the current week, although reaching back a few candles into the prior week is ok at the beginning of the trading week. You chart: Yes, the RSIs are correct, but there is no 3 Tap..so move on to another pair.

--- 帖子 #15422 ---
The very interesting thing about 3 Taps is that we "find" them, we cannot generally anticipate them . We find them because we are looking for them AFTER the RSIs are telling us to look for them (confirming direction). That confirmation of direction is like a neon sign flashing "look for 3 Taps, because conditions are ripe for them!....look for 3 Taps, because conditions, etc." So we do what we are told and go looking. When we find a good 3 Tap line (remember, a 3 Tap is just a trend line..generally with wave action taking place between the taps..but not always or necessary) it may already be triggered and we have to determine if we want to enter or not depending on lots of factors that I really cannot teach a trader, but mainly on PA and how far into the H4 candle it is at the time. But we might find just the setup with no trigger and have to wait until the next candle to determine what PA is going to do before we enter. Never enter a long trade on a short (red) candle. Never enter a short trade on a long (green) candle. Summary: A 3 Tap long with third tap on a short candle = setup but no trigger A 3 Tap long with third tap on a long candle = setup and trigger [opposite for 3 Tap short] Entry is just that simple....and just that complicated. http://www.forexfactory.com/images/m...ading_dark.gif

Thanks in advance.Quote: Originally Posted by zaqzaq Can anybody tell me in relation to LG's 1hr 4 Candle breakout system why is it only the 1st 4 hrs of trading you take into account in your time zone? Would I be correct in thinking that any 4 hr period of consolidation would be a good setup along with Weekly, Daily and 4hr +RSI?? Thanks for the help! The first four hours set our daily range against which we measure or judge price action. It makes us ordered (if that makes sense), by setting our boundaries. It gives us a structure or framework from which we can function. That's really all there is to it. Yes, you are correct in thinking that any consolidation period of 4 or more candles could make a good set up. Again, that would give us a period of time from which to measure price action. It can and does work on any TF. H1 4C is my way of finding a point of reference in a market that is in continuous motion.

--- 帖子 #15558 ---
Hi Snowman, Sorry about the chart, here it is again. My understanding of the 3 tap is that if the price makes a higher low (after a down move) we can draw a trend line which connect these 2 points. I learned that: "Highs are defined as a level where the market ceases to rally and U-turns in the opposite direction. You can spot a high between four candles, when the two to the left and the two to the right are lower than the center wick, which is highest." That's from "The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading" (Jarred F. Martinez) So if I understand it correctly there should be at least 5 candles to find a new lower high necessary for the trend line. But the trend line on the H4 chart was drawn through the bottoms of 3 consecutive candles which does not look like the 3 tap to me. It looks like 3 tap on lower time frame, like on the M30 chart where we can spot the higher low (point 2 on trend line B ). And the point 3 is the third tap. That's on M30 chart though. If i look on H4 chart I would draw trend line A (see H4 chart, the black trend line) and the third tap would be the tripple bottom like you say.

--- 帖子 #15583 ---
Tipico, I think what LG and I are doing is moving the 1st trade's SL to BE before entering a 2nd position. And no, we don't move the SL of the 1st to the new SL. Why? Because the 2nd trade has not yet proven itself as a 'runner'. The first trade is definitely a runner, we don't want to ruin this trade on something unproven. At least that's how LG helped me see it. Once the 2nd position gets up quite a bit, you could use your discretion on whether to set the SLs to the same level.

I would like to second that. Trading in the Zone by Mark Douglas is a must read. Then read it again and again. It helped me overcome emotional trading. I am now an automaton following the rules and executing the trades and consider the Stop Loss the price I am willing to pay to see if I am right about the trade. No emotion. Also it is very important to keep a trade journal. Along with the details of the trade record the rules used and most importantly your emotional state after the trade is closed. Also did you break the rules and why? Record your mental state. Are you elated, bummed, depressed, ticked-off or whatever. Vent and use strong language if you need to. --- 帖子 #15770 ---
Here we use the RSI indicator only to give us a heads' up on the trend, as all of these methods are trend following methods. No indicator that I know of can predict the way the market will go, however this simple little indicator is as good as I have found in "predicting" direction. However PA always wins out over RSI. You will have to decide whether to use it or not.

--- 帖子 #15771 ---
All indicators have a margin of error may it be the setting vs time frame etc. The more indicators you have the larger the error could be making the trade. Indicators are like news reporters that arrive at the scene after the event happened. They all have their own story leading up to the event but which ones correct? Study… Price action only! What pair were you looking at?

--- 帖子 #15777 ---
I would recommend entering from 12am-6am GMT. That's 8pm-2pm EST. This is when there is trading going on in Sydney and Tokyo, but the big dogs haven't started trading yet. My theory is by 12am GMT both sessions have been underway for atleast an hour or so, so things have settled down a bit, but there are still people trading that know what happened in recent events (news from previous days). However, some people have successfully traded at all hours, this is just my preference. I would recommend limiting when you look for entries, but other people may not. I would also highly recommend not trading against the overall trend you see on the Daily charts. I look for HH/HL for long positions and LH/LL for short positions. I never counter-trend trade with this system. Candle strength is also very important. Lastly, when you see a trigger, switch to M15 and wait for candle movement in the right direction. Keep in mind you may miss some good trades using this filter. Can you envision the pair going in the direction you are looking to enter? This comes with screen time, but look to enter on retracements and continuations. Look through this thread at examples of ZC trades (LG's Zorro-continuation method), these are more likely to be successful trades in my experience. Post your charts when you enter and we will try to help.

--- 帖子 #15808 ---
Thirty pips is totally arbituary, josch. It could just as easily be 40 or even 200. I arrived at 30 because that is the amount I was willing to sacrifice to catch the beginning of a trend...the price to get in the game..so to speak. Because there will often be 9-12 open trades at one time, 30 pips seemed reasonable---that's less than 3% of a 100K, 10K, or 1K account at 9 open trades and less than 4% at 12 open trades. So to answer your question, MM is also involved.

--- 帖子 #15868 ---
The arrows do go nuts after almost every time period change, so yes, they need time to find their way after the daily close/open. I have been tracking the monthly RSI for the past 3 or so months and have noticed that it takes 8-10 trading days into the new month for the RSI to settle into a position. Then after about the third week into the month, if the arrows are either red or green, they seldom change..sort of like that big ocean liner turning around....its hard to do. If the arrows are neutral, then they can go either way. I think the implications are significant for monthly trades...although I haven't had the time to exactly work out the implications.

--- 帖子 #15965 ---
not really explained.. but if a pair is down i'd say above 20-25 pips from friday's close to sunday open at 5pm est.. i take the bet that the gap will fill.. and i usually have a 1:1 risk/reward.. so my stop on a 35 pip long would be 35 pips under where the sunday open is.. take profit would be at gap fill, or just before. others on here have wider stops, but for such a small profit, i dunno if it's worth it.. i demo'd my 1:1 strategy for maybe 20 weeks at the end of last year / beginning of this year.. and i wanna say about 18 out of those 20 weeks gaps filled.. although lately luck on getting sizable gaps hasn't been too good. but good luck!

--- 帖子 #15969 ---
Hi LG and other MT traders, I'm starting to question the validity of MoneyTree triggers on Sundays (Monday trading days). Think about it this way... Every day, we avoid taking triggers in the first 4 hours of a trading day, which is approximately 17% of the trading day. The reason we (or atleast I) avoid trading during these hours is due to false D1 RSI signals. So early in the day, the D1 RSI direction can be very unstable. Similarly, I feel we should consider skipping the first day of every week due to W1 RSI direction instability. This would be 20% of the trading week , which would be in line with the discretion we use on the Daily RSI. What do you guys think?

--- 帖子 #16034 ---
To those that have been chatting about OB/OS levels. Keep in mind that looking at these is a form of countertrend trading. If you go back and look, you will likely see that quite a bit of our H4 3T, H1 BO and D1 MT trades are shorts when in OS territory and longs in OB territory. These systems (in particular the MT system) shine during big moves, and in these scenarios trading off of OS &amp; OB levels can get you into trouble. I totally think it's valid to use OB/OS levels for TP levels, and I believe LG has left quite a bit of slack in regards to how each trader wishes to take their pips off the table Just my 2 cents

--- 帖子 #16035 ---
Hi Kan, Do not reload the indicator...when you change the x and/or y setting in the user dialog...these settings "stay" with the chart the indicator is attached to. When you reload the indicator it changes back to the default settings. Just change the values in the x and/or y and click the "ok" to save the new settings for the chart that you are working on. "If" the indicator has not moved then just change the time frame for that chart. ie., if your chart is a H4 change it to a H1 and back to the H4. This will refresh all the indicators on your chart and you should be good to go. Right click anywhere on screen and left click on Indicator list. Double left click on the indicator name...or single click and pick edit. Change the DisplayStarts_X value to 500. Make sure that the IndicatorRSIWindow is set to false. Click ok to exit user setting dialog. Click close to exit indicator list dialog. Poooofffffhh...you indicator should now be somewhere around mid screen. When this looks the way you want it, create a template so you can reproduce it on any new charts without having to mess with the indicator again. If you use a very large number the indicator will plot but will be offscreen where you can't see it so use small number changes to start so you get an idea of how far an increase of 10 moves it.

--- 帖子 #16084 ---
Hi guys, I'm going to show you a prime example of why you should wait for the trend to be established before taking any of these trades (especially MT trades). I waited last night until 3:00am for London open and took all my trades within the first 15 minutes when everything exploded upwards and all RSI indicators were up mostly for D1 and W1 (this would have been 3 hours into my new day candle, so good according to MT rules). A lot of the trades I had entered even had some good price action signals (bullish inside bars, bullish engulfing bars on the H1 and M15). However, because I traded during an open of such a high volatility market, you can see what happened in my attachment. They swung low, hit my 30 pip SL before finding a trend for the day. If I had waited, I would have been left out of some very bad MT trades and still made some good pips on the ones with an established direction. From now on, I will be trying out MT trades around 8pm EST (CrucialCraig's time) even though my new daily candle doesn't start until 12am EST. I think LG was right saying it's more about the market and trend than about when the candle starts.

--- 帖子 #16170 ---
This method will carry itself once positions are established, but there will be lots of losses before getting to established positions, that is very true. Most positions will be stopped out. One needs to be able to handle 20+ losses before hitting a real move, like the 3000 move down on EURUSD from Nov. 2009 to May 2010. What if we had 10 or more branches on that move?..I'd be out of here! But would we care if we took 100+ losses to get there? I would not even give it a thought. That's the endgame. Remember that all the trading books seem to agree that 60% of long term trades end in losses or BE. Thus, the 40% are the big return trades...what we are looking for here. The ability to withstand multiple losses is what pushes trend followers to look for very high Reward:Risk ratios. It requires true mental toughness and most traders don't have it and instead look for Risk:Reward rations. There is nothing wrong with that, but we must give up that way of thinking to be successful with these long term trades. I am still testing myself to see which group I fit into. But I am hoping it is the Reward:Risk group.

I had that same problem with 3 taps. Lost three weeks work during couple of days. Its not very inspiring to lose 3 weeks work, but dont give up. I analysed the problem a while ago and found that if weekly trend changes (or if the price is ranging, but thats not as bad as trend change) in the middle of the week, thats bad for 3 taps as well as other longer tf trades. If you check last two weeks, there has been a change in the trend in the middle of the week on many currencies. If the trend continues the whole week as it started on monday, there is no prob, but to ride with it. LG said before that weekly trend is more reliable later in the week. This might have something to do with that also. I havent been able to solve this problem so far, but I think that it could be worthwhile to secure your potential profits by trailing tp in the middle of the week as well as check out trend confirmation on open trades during the week by eg. highs/lows, higher highs/higher lows on 1h or 4h. --- 帖子 #16209 ---
Thanks for your input Ben. To answer your question, I have never suggested a TP or SL for 3 Taps other than reasonable R/S levels. The reason is that I never considered these methods beginning trader methods, although they are deceptively simple and many newbies have embraced them. But I always assumed traders could determine their own levels, based on individual tolerance, comfort, and accounts. I have tried hard to avoid getting into long discussions about MM, how to draw trendlines, support and Resistance levels, etc..again because I assumed every trader was intimately familiar with these things. I now see that with MoneyTree, MM issues have cropped up...and that's certainly ok.

--- 帖子 #16210 ---
What I would like traders here to understand and I don't believe I have done a great job at it so far, is that I have tried to systematically take you through a method of trading.. starting with H1 charts (H1 4C BO)...then H4 charts (3 Tap) and now daily charts (MoneyTree)...that is extremely interrelated . These systems can be traded separately, or all together. By that I mean a H1 BO can be used to enter a MoneyTree trade, as can a 3 Tap or a H1 BO can become a 3 Tap and both can become a MoneyTree trade. Or a trader can stick with only H1 trades or only 3 Tap trades. But, in my opinion, MoneyTree is the endgame. And with Moneytree, my work on the thread is almost done.

SL with 30 pips is OK, for the majors, if entry is well on the lower timeframes. But not enough for volatil pairs like geppy or exotic currency pairs. 2. LG, you try to catch the big trend. I will focus in my demo on the opposite way with near targets plus the big trend. Lets say I splitt a trade in 3 parts, with first target 1 daily candle length (or the average daily range). In a down market it means, price is testing a resistance and resume downdtrend in the direction of the RSI. BUT what happens if it taps 3 times and breaks through it, opposite to the direction of the RSI ? This means the resistance is broken and price will reverse. So if I have a 3 tap 4 h entry short, how about to put a buy limit order a bit above my SL ? Just in case price will reverse ? I will not trade this in my demo, but I will watch behaviour of price after my SL is hit, if it reverse. See example in the second chart. green pips to all.

--- 帖子 #16284 ---
Number 1 is correct. Number 2 not exactly. This is a pure price action trade. There does not need to be confirmation of the daily and weekly for this trade...only for the 3 Tap and MoneyTree setups. Just follow PA and it is likely the H1 and maybe the H4 RSIs will be in confirmation. but it is not necessary for the H1 BO. Number 3 is correct, in that SL and TP are discretionary with the trader. I have recommended reasonable S/R levels, but the other side of the H/L would work too.

--- 帖子 #16292 ---
With the Daily Money Tree Method: 1-We confirm Daily and Weekly Rsi direction. 2-We switch to H1 charts, draw H and L of the first 4 candles of the day. 3-We enter the trade on a breakout of these H or L's, depending of the Daily and Weekly Rsi direction. 4- We use a SL of 30 pips, let the trade run till next day.. Before ordering a Ferrari, I wanted to confirm this, thanks

--- 帖子 #16365 ---
This is what we are looking for...3 and more branches all making pips. Let's say the first branch is up 500 pips, the second is up 300 pips and the third is at 200 pips. But the price of getting there has been 300 pips. We let the first branch continue, but we decide to replenish our capital by "cashing in" 200 pips from branch two, and 100 pips from branch three. We have restored our capital and still have 500 + 100 +100 pips from the continuing branches and thus have 700 pips of unrealized gain. If that is profit one wants to take off the tables, by all means do it. It is totally up to the invidivual, but if there is really a 2000 or 3000 pip run like we have seen, we would want to be in on it. Think what it would be like if we had 10 or more positive branches on such a run! It is very doable...we just need that trend.

--- 帖子 #16366 ---

--- 帖子 #16436 ---
One of my brokers is Oanda and they, unlike many of the other brokers, do not close over the weekend. Therefore the charts will not reflect any gaps since they are continuous. FXDD, IBFX, FXCM and most of the other brokers close on Friday and open again Sunday night. The gaps are reflected in those brokers charts.

--- 帖子 #16556 ---
I think we all are battling that mind set. I used to stop live trading for the week after banking 100 pips. It was almost like a false humility, looking back on my reasoning...I think I was thinking along the lines of 100 pips was my fair share or something like that. But now I realize that 100 pips was nothing, kind of like picking some of the fruit and letting the rest rot on the tree...it made no sense. If you are getting to 600+ pip accumulations, it won't be too large a leap to 800, then even larger. Try to get use to taking good profits and setting BEs. Then if PA still moves in your favor, take more off the table and move to BE again. FXDD allows traders to close from a full contract to .50, then to .25. I have not tried going lower than that, but I think the .25 can be taken to .10. I am assuming all brokers are the same. The point is that once profit is taken down to .25 at BE...there is not much loss left there and the potential gain is tremendous.

--- 帖子 #16608 ---
josch, I agree about the RSI. It's less reliable at the beginning of a time frame. However, when looking at the RSI, I also look at the ongoing trend, and not only the last print. I don't the know the RSI-formula by heart, but using the same formula can give different results, depending upon the parameters. What I mean is that there are several ways to calculate the RSI, using closing/median/high-low/etcetera... When using the closing price, and the time frame has just begun, then the result is less reliable. The real problem is that when entering a trade, you're always in the middle of some time frame. The decision needs to be made at that point in time, with the information available at that point in time, while knowing that this information is outdated once the price moves. Having said that, the price has indeed moved, and it has breached the yellow 3 tap line and I was already short. Seeing the price struggling at the 0.83 level, and seeing the double top, I was too eager to enter a short trade. Instead of waiting for the right price action, I anticipated the move. Anticipating a move, instead of reacting on it, is tricky. No harm done this time, since I turned it into a long AUDNZD position by buying AUDUSD. So I keep this one open, for a long term Money Tree

--- 帖子 #16647 ---
Well spotted, chartlovers ! Why two ? It takes two to tango It's just an old habbit of this rabbit to look at the RSI(14) to have a visual check on the strength of ongoing trend. RSI(3) is in red and is used the same way as suggested by lawgirl, including the coloured arrows. RSI(14) is in green and is less hectic, it shows me the strength of the trend on a longer time horizon. It smooths out the hectic changes in the coloured arrows. What I mean is that if the coloured arrows turn against me, it's okay as long as the green RSI(14) is trending in the good direction. Because I think the arrows will change into the right colour and direction again after some candles. So that could even be a good time to accumulate the position, add another branch to the moneytree. Basically it's looking at the same thing, the trend

--- 帖子 #16701 ---
The attached indicator is an attempt to overcome the current bar repaint of the RSI slope. The main change is that you can input a Percent factor such that the RSI will be based on the current bar if it is x percent elapsed. If less than that, the RSI figures will be based on the previous bar. In other words, if you put in a factor of (say) 20, the RSI figures will be based on the previous bar until the current bar is 20% elapsed. Indicator icons change from outline to solid at the switchover to the current bar. I hope this is useful to someone.

--- 帖子 #16716 ---
I have attached other hourly charts for comparison. USDCHF showed BO's up and down during this period. During the 4CH1 range on thursday, the bodies of the heiken ashi have a better match with the trading range. The bodies of traditional candlesticks showed some fake moves during this period of range trading. On friday there was another upside BO on the 4CH1. This BO was followed by a rally, a top and a sell-off and a downside break. The last candles just before the sell-off confuse me a bit. At the top, traditional candlestick show some red candles and the formation looks toppish to me, especially the second (small) red candle before the sell-off. At that point, the heiken ashi chart produces another white candle to confirm the ongoing uptrend. This candle will probably make you stay longer in the trade, is that what you mean ? Another difference that I see is the following. During the downside break, the body of the first red candle did not break the 4CH1 line. The second red candle confirms the downside break, but at that time the price was trading well below the BO level. In case of a long position, because the body of the first red candle is still above support level, this could probably be a reason to stay longer in the trade. But the closing price is already below the 4CH1 of the day before. It's very interesting but at this moment it's a bit confusing to me, so I'll have to take a look at it again and again and again

--- 帖子 #16717 ---
I have attached another pair of charts for comparison. USDJPY showing two upside BO's on H1 4C (thursday and friday). Observe the last candle before the sell-off, at the end of the magenta line (see arrow) . If I understand it correctly, Heiken Ashi produces a white candle, thereby confirming the uptrend and making you stay longer in the trade. Traditional candlesticks produces a red candle, making me cautious to enter a long trade here at the double top. At the start of the sell-off, the body of the first red candle also breached the support level, which is good because it's an extra confirmation that the trend is indeed reversing. The same sell-off in USDCHF (see previous post) needs a second candle to confirm the downside break, which is not so good, well at least if you are looking at the bodies only.

Hello LG, I have been using HA bars for some years and find them to be very useful. Two ways to use them for exits are: 1) Conservative, wait for a tail to appear from the opposite end of the candle to the direction of price movement. I.E. if price is going up close either all or part of your position when a tail shows from the bottom of the candle. 2) Aggressive, wait until a candle closes in a different colour and then close your position. You must first decide which time frame you are TRADING though, no point in using this exit strategy on an M15 chart if you are following an H4 trend.

--- 帖子 #16767 ---
Thanks Merlyn, I am really liking them too. I like both both your suggestions conservative and aggressive. I am using them mostly on upper time frames...although I like them for H1 charts.

That could be a reason to be careful with pending orders.

First to 6th too..it really doesn't matter. I know what you are going through. Every single trader has/is going through the same thing. This is the hardest thing I have every done and I am including all of law school and studying for the bar. I try to explain it to people sometimes and just can't get them to understand..especially when there are only 3 ways the market can go--up, down, or sideways. All I can say is don't give up, if you really enjoy it. It doesn't matter how many demo accounts you blow through, just keep using them until you get your routine and pace going and are seeing success. Then do that same routine over and over again. Also..and excuse me, but I think this is guy thing...don't set arbitrary deadlines for yourself. By that I mean, things like "If I haven't doubled my account in 2 weeks, I'm out of here." So what if the deadline is not met. Just have progress as a goal. I use weekly "accounting" not daily. Did my week end with pips? A lot less pressure that way. The market has the jitters this year. More so than I have ever seen, probably because the world is the same. So much chaos and uncertainty, this is a much harder time to be trading, in my opinion. Don't over trade and don't chase trades. Two things I have to constantly remind myself of...still. There will always be more trades coming up. Right now you are frustrated and still working on a system. But once you work out your own way of trading and become successful, you will have another problem to deal with....boredom. Successful trading is very dull and lonely. That is why I think FF is so successful. It has brought together thousands of traders who sit at a computer away from their families, who are going through the same things and somehow we feel a little less isolated in this endeavor. Hope this helps.

We were talking about pending orders a few days ago. Here is an example of setting one that all indications show would be successful. I would set my pending order at the top of the wick, marked with the dotted line. Remember that wicks are probes that tell us where the market has tried to go, but did not have the steam at that time. If the order is hit. Zoom out for placing a reasonable TP area. SL, depending on how tight you would want it, could be one are the other of the blue R/S lines.

Hi, I have a question. I see that several chart, the H1 4C BO, the horizontal lines are not from the first four candles. You will be looking at the bodies of the first four H1 candles of a new trading day...disregard the tails (wicks)....whenever that is for you. That is one reason period seperators need to be placed on the chart. C. Place horizontal lines at the highest high of these four candles' bodies (not including the tails, if any) and the lowest low of these four candles' bodies , again, disregard the tails.

--- 帖子 #17000 ---
I think it is just a matter of personal preference whether you draw lines using only the bodies or using the wicks. Apart from that, I think the chart you are referring to is a Heiken Ashi chart, showing other bodies than regular candlesticks. The same with the starting time of the H1 4C BO, some use their broker starting day, some use Tokyo opening, some use London opening. It is flexible and adjustable to your own liking, choose one that matches best with your trading day. Once a nice BO happens, and the price moves, the RSI's will eventually point in the same direction. For me personally, I rarely catch those BO's, because they almost always happen when I am not sitting behind my screen Hope that helps

--- 帖子 #17031 ---
The channel is a 5 period Smoothed Average, using the high, the low and the median. I got this from a video posted here on this thread. You are probably right, I think it was Dean Malone on the video. I use this to see if the ongoing trend is still intact or in some kind of consolidation or maybe even reversing. Right now a new white candle appears on the H4 Heiken Ashi chart, it is still in the lower part of the channel, no trend reversal yet, but also no immediate continuation of the downtrend. The channel still has a downward slope, so I consider this a temporary pause in the downtrend. The pause before the selloff, the silence before the storm. Patience will be rewarded

--- 帖子 #17038 ---
When our trades lose money, whatever our logic, we can be sure we were not alone. But we can equally be sure that we were in the minority. Had we been in the majority the market would have performed as anticipated. The market decision process is that simple. It is a matter of putting our behavior in line with the majority as often as we can. The most effective tool to achieve that is our own empirically tested market psychology. We are the market, if only we can let ourselves mimic the mind of the market and not permit individuality to rule our decisions.

--- 帖子 #17040 ---
We will never mimic the mind of the market, in my opinion. I believe the best thing that we can do is give ourselves an edge. That is what I believe we are doing here..giving ourselves an edge. The next step is to be consistent with that edge, as is pointed out in "Trading in the Zone". Consistency is also what makes trading so boring...the rote, day in, day out process of "if the market does this, then I will do that." The consistency part of trading is incredibly powerful because it takes the emotional aspects away from trading. Trading should be a very "cold" venture...devoid of emotions...we know how lonely it is. It is consistency in how we trade that makes us "cold" and thus fairly immune to the emotional beatings that can occur with losses. This in turn gives us another edge. This boring rote process devoid of emotion is what 95% of traders will never understand and why 95% of traders are not successful. We are, or will, be successful because we understand.

--- 帖子 #17061 ---
Once a H4 3T is spotted, I check if the RSI's are in agreement. It certainly helps if the tap candle has the right colour, else wait for the next candle. Depending upon the price action, I do not wait for the close of the next H4 candle. Because waiting another 4 hours can mean that you will be missing a large part of the move. When entering a trade I normally switch to a lower timeframe (H1/M30/M15), so I can have a closer look at the price action. In this specific example with NZDUSD, I would probably enter the trade at the moment the line is tapped and the price bounces back. Because the uptrend is very strong, I do not wait for the next candle or a break out for confirmation. I just assume that a BO will follow and a continuation of the trend will follow after the tap. Observe the Heiken Ashi candles at the time of the tap, just before the breakout. The candle turns into the wrong colour and drops to the lower part of the channel. Hunting for stops and limits and trying to shake out the longs before the rally begins. I call this the katapult, the perfect entry for a long trade

--- 帖子 #17062 ---
AUDUSD shows an example of a perfect katapult. On the M30 candlesticks chart the katapult is clearly visible. On the H1 Heiken Ashi it drops to the other side of the channel for a shake out before the rally takes off. It usually happens in nervous fast moving markets (news events etc..). I consider this one a perfect katapult

--- 帖子 #17078 ---
How to determine where to draw trendlines is a matter of trial and error. Drawing a line requires 2 points, starting point and ending point. Drawing a trendline requires at least 3 points, according to the purists of technical analysis. When drawing trendlines, I search for tops and bottoms and try to connect those points. The magenta line in the upper part of the previous USDCAD H4 chart is drawn from a daily/weekly/monthly chart. That's the long term trendline, and the trend is down. The magenta line on the H4 chart connects the bottoms, the weekly lows, and also the fresh yearly lows, traded this month. A closer look at what happened: Last week price fell through this supportline and traded at new yearly lows again. The price recovered and attempted to get back above this line, but with no success. It failed to breach the line, and according to theory, former support now becomes resistance. Right now we are seeing a similar move, another attempt to get back above the resistance line. So far no success in breaking this line around the 0.95 level. As long as price does not break this resistance level, the (short term) trend is not broken. Because the long term trend is down, I am looking for a bearish setup in this one. That's where the H4 3T comes in I think that right now a bearish setup is in place. Have a close look at the H4 chart and observe the price action.

--- 帖子 #17123 ---
Yes, I do recommend that you stick with the H1 4C BO in this market, Walad. I am using it almost exclusively. I have banked around 200 pips already this week just with BOs. Rules are as simple as it gets: 1. Mark the first 4 hours of the new trading day. Those are your support/Resistance levels upon wish you will determine everything; 2. Check them when you can and make note of any directional movement toward one or the other of these levels; 3. Any pair's PA approaching the S/R levels? Note them and the directions of the RSIs. These go on your watch list; 4. Mark with a horizontal line any wick bottoms/tops that penetrate the S/R levels, remembering that wicks are price probes...soldiers sent out to explore the area. Look for those wick areas to be penetrated with a candle close on either an M15 chart or a M5 chart. 5. Mark your TP at the next support/Resistance level. There are probably hundreds of charts posted that show the above. Just look back a few pages and you will see them to study, Once you are comfortable with this, you will find variations such as consolidation BOs to trade. And you are right, they are puny variations, but they make pips. The GBPUSD chart below shows the entire setup.

--- 帖子 #17124 ---
Here is a pair heading for a BO that we can walk through together. I have marked the bottom of the wick on the first full BO candle with an arrow.

--- 帖子 #17125 ---

--- 帖子 #17186 ---
If I may add to LG's resent statement: “H1 BOs are PA trades and not necessarily trend trades" Something that might make this a bit easy regarding PA trading.. Yes, the H1 BOs are not always a trend trade but if you concentrate on the ones that are such as AUDUSD and AUDCAD post # 17172... As you will see, looking at the LG indicator, 90% of the arrows are red... trend is definitely down. Both trades taken short. Having said that.. Look left...see the price congestion that took place on Aug 3... Now look at the preceding price action from the beginning of Aug... See how the market/price has been in a downward trend. Odds are good ( not that it is certain ) that the break will be with the trend. AUDUSD... See the area 1.0800 around July 24/25... This became a resistance for the upper part of the congestion prior to the break down for this trade short. Yes this is a macro view but it illustrates how looking at PA can help you with LG’s trades. Add this to the LG indicator..odds a little more in your favor.. Again, not every trade is a trend trade but staying with the obvious trend trades (getting a macro view / larger view, may help you over the hurdle that you are having) This is an excellent method, very consistent but your ability to read PA is critical. One last thing. LG uses a method of determining support and resistance on the H1 BO that is different than the conventional thinking. That of drawing her S/R lines based on the bodies of the candles (opens and closes) not the top and bottom of the wicks. The wicks are probes... Ropes hanging from the ledge ( the ledge is the real support ). If you begin to see S/R in this manner throughout you charts, this will take you to a new level of understanding of PA and S/R. LG.. Feel free to add if I stated something incorrectly.. TSD

Price breaks short , retraces back up to the support now resistance.. The purple line is support drawn in the traditional way. price broke through as well but retrace back through the purple line.. I have also found that taking the most recent S/R vs. a S/R farther way in the same area tends to be the nmore accurate of the 2. My point in all this .. Look from were you came.. look left .. get a good macro view. Helps to see the trend. Use LG inidactor.. Learn to see and draw S/R lines.. They will become your road maps in PA trading. As you begining to see the S/R levels you will notice whether you are trading trend , or counter trend. Hope this helps TSD

I forgot to add one other item that will ( I think ) speak very directly to degournay's having some difficulty. If you look at the first chart I posted.. The one with all the arrows on it. Notice how price trends.. Then ranges... Then trends.. Nothing new here right.... But when you apply it to the contex of LG's statement “H1 BOs are PA trades and not necessarily trend trades" 1)Trading within range bound PA as shown, there may be little follow through.. A high degree of trade management is in order here.. Else you might get chopped up... or ... maybe just stay out. 2) Is the trade at the top or bottom of the range? Do you take the trade back into the range or hope for the break out? I prefer to take the trade back into the range ( if that's the set up ) as there is no conformation of a break out. Think of it this way.. I know I'm in range therefore I trade range.. 3) I will not hesitate to take a trade in the direction of the trend. How do we know? Look back/Look left.. It becomes easier to see when looking at the macro view.. PA is ranging.. PA is trending.. Especially when looking a H1 TF. The market moves slower, easier to see. I know I'm in trend, therefore I trade trend If you do not know if you are trending or ranging.. Please dont take the trade. This is not the perfect way, but hopefully it will help. Hey LG.. --- 帖子 #17210 ---
I don't think it will make much difference at all, 7. The BOs seldom happen immediately after the first four hours in any case. I miss plenty of BOs that occur from around midnight my time to 5 or 6 am when I wake up, yet there are still plenty of pips to be made. The marking of the R/S lines on the first 4 hours is a guide by which we "judge" our BOs, but those lines could just as easily mark most any 4-6 hour period within the trading day by which to "judge" or use as a guide for BOs. We use these two high/low lines to mark range consolidations anticipating BOs also.

--- 帖子 #17226 ---
I still lose money, pete, and always will. But I keep more than I lose and that is the key. Becoming almost machine-like in trading is the key, I believe. But human nature being what it is, machine-like is very boring so, we look around for things to make trading more interesting, maybe a new indicator or an ea. That is how I start losing money. As soon as I stray from watching PA, S/R areas, longer TF directions, etc, I generally start losing money. Yet I still from time to time want to try something new, start losing money, then go back to the tried and true. For me, BOs are the best way I have found to consistently make money. I always come back to them, no matter how far I stray. Finding your "zone" will happen, just keep doing what you are doing. I believe you have a natural talent for trading, and I can't say that about most of the traders I have seen. It is just a matter of finding your own pace, your own way of doing things, your own timing, etc. But accept that you will lose trades and you will have losing streaks, it just comes with the territory.

--- 帖子 #17233 ---
Gaps are traded at the open of the Asian market for the week..Sunday afternoon at 2:00 pm for me, but whenever your particular broker goes live. They are very simple: if price gaps up/down over 40 or more (an arbitrary number) pips from close on Friday, take a trade in the opposite direction. For example: gaps up 40+ pips = short trade gaps down 40+ pips = long trade The reason we take these trades is that almost all gaps fill sooner or later . These trades seem to be as much a "sure thing" as we have in forex trading. We don't discuss here the philosophy of how or why this happens, but there is much written here on FF about them, if you want more information.

--- 帖子 #17316 ---
I modified the original dashboard so that the current bar will kick in after whatever "percent elapsed" I want. That is, the RSI will calculate from the current bar only after it is x% old. Until then, it calculates as at the previous bar. To use this, set up an extra chart, do a "Window, Tile Vertically", make it EURUSD or any high frequency tick pair, apply the blank template, attach the dashboard indicator and re-size the windows to suit. Hey LawGirl - thanks again for the thread and feel free to put the attached on page one if you want.

--- 帖子 #17335 ---
My preference on the higher timeframes is for traditional candles - once I get down to H4 and lower I'll switch to HA or APB. For price action I will click on the candlestick or bar chart buttons so that they are overlayed on the HA/APB. As with any indicator, HA/APB adds in an averaging algorithm - depnds on how well you can read traditional candles and their associated patterns. Pros - HA/APB takes out the noise and shows the trend moves - but then so do MA Cons - Additional averaging, so real time Price Action is lost within the HA/APB but is easilly overlayed

--- 帖子 #17336 ---

--- 帖子 #17337 ---

--- 帖子 #17400 ---
Thats a lot of questions, dude! A few pointers: 1. BOs can happen any time of the day, the lines are drawn however at the first 4H candles of YOUR broker's day. Like today, lots of BOs happened US am session and not really during Asian. 2. Lots have been said on TP and SL, LG and most of us use S/R levels, LG doesn't use SLs, most others do, usually at your discretion and your MM style, but reasonable R:R ratio 3. Channel size doesn't matter, in my experience, the tighter the better the BO will be (like a sqeezed spring ready to pop) I trade all size channels. 4. For this method we don't include the wicks, but you could be more conservative and include them. I view wicks as probes and try to enter when price clears wicks/scouts. You can search the thread for "scout" and you'll see a lot of discussion about them 5. Retrace trades - see previous post and again, search for "retrace" and you shall find tons of good info here on this thread. There, now I messed up my lunch break. Back to work, many pips to all of you out there. Pete

I will agree with both Squaretrader's and Britpip7 assessments. I may added that the set ups for R/R using the 1H BO can be different for each pair as it relates to your equity. What I mean is the upper and lower lines drawn can be wide or very narrow. Please review previous posts as you will see that. A very simple method to be sure. I personally do not trade the 3 Taps as the 1H BO has plenty of set ups. Most (not all) fit my personal R/R Now for you to scream NO ANSWER!!!!!!!!!! Indicates a very high level of frustration. A common theme throughout many threads on FF. If you are looking to trade this or any other method you must be able to have strong discipline and self control. If by reading this your level of anxiety escalates you have a long road ahead of you. A great percentage of trading is about emotional control (took me a many years and a few $1000.00 to get that concept) Why??? Because I thought “I " was not the problem... Wrong ... I was precisely the problem. This is why so many fail... They do not believe (as you may not) that their emotional make up, at this point) is what is hurting their chances of becoming a successful trader. It is a very 'HARD LESSON " to learn and accept. Some never get it. Most likely you will write back something like ... "I do not have a problem you do"... "Why can’t I just get a straight answer" or something that really does not get you moving in the right direction. I hope you do not. This not meant to be an attack but more an observation that may help your trading going forward. Do not be in a hurry. This is an excellent method. LG and others bring a great deal to this thread. You will learn a lot if you just slow down, take a breath... re read the thread. Become an active, positive participant with this method and you will give yourself the best chance of being successful....Patience and time on the screen...You will soon learn if this method will fit your trading style. relax, learn... it will save you lots on $$$$ TSD

--- 帖子 #17487 ---
I'm not a pro, but let me try to answer this. I think everybody has their own style of managing trades, so you'll probably get different answers from every trader. I personally have a set TP of 20-30pips for night BOs when I can't monitor them. During the day I do go back and forth between the H1 and M15 to see if price is stalling or not. if it's not happening on M15 or reversing, I often move SL to BE or exit if it's a real reversal.

--- 帖子 #17597 ---
The 4C 1H BO method is beautifully spelled out on page 1. Read that over and over again until you understand what she's talking about, especially the M15 entry. Trading is a business and it has to be handled like that. You have to read, read, and read a ton to get your education, just like with any job. I'm a doctor and took me a zillion yrs of studying to get here, trading is just another kind of business that requires A LOT of studying. READ THE FIRST 50 pages of the thread at least to get familiar with the methods, then jump to maybe page 800 and you'll find tons of examples and explanations of the BO method from LG and others. But you really should read most of the thread if you wanna be a good trader. I and LG dont use limit orders anymore as the market has been very volatile lately and pending orders get us whipsawed way too often. Orders are put in whenever you see the BO happening. Could be at night or in the am. I had 2 trades last night at 10pm EST and 3 trades this am at 8am EST. That's when the BOs happened. They could happen anytime. Avoid NY pm though and low volatility times. If you're just getting started with this method, I suggest you don't do the MT yet. Understand the BOs fully and you wont need much of anything else. I don't even do the 3taps anymore (LG doesn't do them either as there are tons of 1H BOs out there to make a killing) Read, read, read, and screen time is the key to success!!!! Peace, Pete

Hello ... For my own purposes I made an indicator to draw the 4C box, project forward, and add bands to show scale. The indicator looks at the 4 H1 candles before the TradeStartHour. --- 帖子 #17703 ---
Sure, but please note that this EA does not correspond to the strategy of LG, H1 BO. Actually there are 2 EAs, which are used for any entry, one is for buying and the other for selling. This EAs send one order to the current price (Here is where you use the LG H1 BO strategy). Parameters are given as follows: MagicNumber StopLoss (SL in points) FiboBreakEven (fibo level, example: 161.8. 0 is SL, 100 is open price) BECLosePer (Order Percent to close at BE, ex: 50.0) FiboProfit1 (fibo level, example: 261.8) TP1ClosePer (Order Percent to close at TP1, ex: 30.0) FiboProfit2 (fibo level, example: 423.6) TP2ClosePer (Order Percent to close at TP2, ex: 20.0) Risk (Percent of Risk calculated on the free margin, ex: 1.0) Lots (Volume. If 0, then calculate the volume on the Risk) MinLots (Minimum Lots to execute or 0) MaxLots (Maximum Lots to execute or 0) TrailingStop (0 or TrailingStop calculate on the TP2 - Tp1. TrailingStop works when TP1 is reached) Please note that when you close an order, you must close the EA!!! Please, help me to test it's. Your comments are welcome. I want to help in some way to make the most of these marvelous LG strategies.

--- 帖子 #17752 ---
Buy and Sell EAS using Fibonacci levels SellFibo, and BuyFibo are two Expert Advisors that allow you to open an order to sell or buy respectively. you need to select entry point using some strategy, for example H1 4C BO or any other. In these EAs you need select the points for the Stop Loss (SL) from the open price, you can define a Fibonacci level to Break Even (BE), one Fibonacci level for a first Profit (TP1), and a Fibonacci level for a second Profit (TP2). Additionally, you can set a closing percents of the order when levels reach BE, TP1 and TP2. When the price reache TP1, you can set the execution of Trailing Stop (TS) as a percentage of the distance between TP1 and TP2. If you wanted, you can leave a percentage of the order open one it reaches TP2, in which case you must manually close this part of the order when you consider it better. You can also set the volume of the order corresponds to a fixed lot size or a percentage of calculated risk on the free margin of the account. The EA starts its execution immediately opening an order, when it reaches the level of BE, play an alert sound, partially close the order in the percentage that you define, and move the SL at the open price. Subsequently, if it reaches TP1, closes the percentage of the order you entered and active TS based on the percentage you entered. Reaching TP2, closes the percentage to be defined. At this point you must manually close the EA . When starting the execution of the EA, under the tab "Expert" line is displayed with relevant information of the order, ie OpenPrice, stoploss, BreakEven, TakeProfit1 and TakeProfit2. You may want to manually insert the graphic object Fibonacci starting from the OpenPrice and ending at the stoploss. Before you need to define the properties of Fibonacci levels to be used, where 0 is the SL, OpenPrice is 1, and the values ​​you entered as level parameters, BE, TP1 and TP2, such as 2.618 (to 261.8 level). The parameters of these EAs are: MagicNumber Stoploss (SL points) FiboBreakEven (Level fibo for BE, eg: 161.8) BECLosePer (Percentage of the order to close the BE, ie: 50.0) FiboProfit1 (fibo level for TP1, eg: 261.8) TP1ClosePer (Percentage of the Order to close at TP1, eg: 30.0) FiboProfit2 (Level fibo for TP2, eg: 423.6) TP2ClosePer (Percentage of the Order to close at TP2, eg: 20.0) Risk (Risk Percentage calculated on the free margin, eg: 1.0) Lots (Volumen. If 0, then the volume is calculated from the percentage of admitted Risk) MinLots (Minimum volume to run or 0) MaxLots (Maximum volume to be executed or 0) TrailingStop (0 or TrailingStop calculated on TP2 - TP1. TrailingStop brother works TP1 is reached. Pe: 50.0, indicating that corresponds to 50% of TP2-TP1) Any comments will be gladly answered.

--- 帖子 #17783 ---
lwiharjo, In the image attached you can see the Fibo object. First, you decide the open price 1.45000 and that SL will be at 100 pips, ie 1.44900. You select which Fibonacci level will correspond to the TP1 and TP2 and also to something I call BreakEven, which is the point at which the SL will move to BreakEven (Open Price). In this case, I selected BE at 200 Fibo Level, TP1 at 261.8 Fibo Level and Tp2 at 423.6 Fibo Level, but you can select these levels the value you want. In the second image, you can see the corresponding parameters to the Fibo levels, but you can modify as you want, for example, you can select FiboProfit2 to 600, 800, what you want, you're the one who decides this. The EAs does'nt draw the Fibo object, if you want, you need to draw it. This is handy to know at what time their objectives were achieved. I hope you have been more clear. I suggest you Try out the EA, for example, runs BuyFibo with default values​​, then immediately paint the Fibo with levels: 0 Stop Loss 1 Open Price 2 Break Even 2.618 Take Profit 1 4.236 Take Profit 2 Then follows the behavior of the EA and you can understand better.

--- 帖子 #17811 ---
cmena82, The idea is that you decide at what point to enter an order, Buy or Sell. At that time, you must run the EA, SellFibo or BuyFibo. The EA do not draw the object Fibo, if you want, you can insert the object Fibo. The EA internally calculated EA levels at which to close part of the order according to the parameters that you indicate as BreakEven level, and TakeProfit2 TakeProfit1. Please use version 1.20 of the EAs (post 17781) Spanish: La idea es que tu decides en que momento entrar a una orden, de compra o de venta. En ese momento, tu debes correr el EA BuyFibo o SellFibo. El EA no te dibuja el objeto Fibo, si tu quieres, puedes insertar el objeto Fibo. El EA internamente calcula los niveles a los cuales debe cerrar parte de la orden de acuerdo a los parámetros que tu le indiques como nivel de BreakEven, TakeProfit1 y TakeProfit2. Por favor utiliza la versón 1.20 de los EAs (post 17781)

--- 帖子 #17856 ---
Hi! Lawgirl &amp;Callisto, thanks for all you ave taught me in the past few months since I found this thread. --- 帖子 #17883 ---
Page 1 2. The H1 4 Candle Breakout Trade (H1 4C BO) I have added a new trade set-up to the 3 tap trade discussed above. It works hand and hand with the 3 tap trade. Often we can see PA going in one direction and want to get in, but need a logical way to do it. Certainly 3 tap is one way, but what if you do not see a good 3 tap set-up on the H4 chart? Then move to the H1 chart and take a look . The H1 4 candle breakout set-up: A. This is a price action (PA) trade and the weekly RSI direction does not need to match the direction of the trade. Because this is considered a "fast" trade...meaning over in a few hours at the longest...only the H4 and H1 candles need to confirm direction, but they will do that if PA moves in the desired direction. B. You will be looking at the bodies of the first four H1 candles of a new trading day...disregard the tails (wicks)....whenever that is for you. That is one reason period seperators need to be placed on the chart. C. Place horizontal lines at the highest high of these four candles' bodies (not including the tails, if any) and the lowest low of these four candles' bodies , again, disregard the tails. These lines are really just R/S lines. D. Wait for a breakout in the direction of the bias. I sometimes place a pending order below/above a R/S line before I go to bed. E. Enter from the M15 chart, when at least one candle has completely cleared the R/S line in the desired direction. The entry takes discretion, as the quality of the candles is important to observe. NOTE: You can set this up several hours after the fourth candle that you are observing. For example: My first four candles are from 2:00 pm - 6:00 pm. I may not get to the set-up until 8 or 9 p.m. That is ok, in fact, that gives time to observe PA. Do verify the directional bias again, however.

--- 帖子 #17891 ---
Hi, As we saw earlier, it is important to note the reasons for each entry as this can give us the discipline to execute our orders correctly. I present the following checklist that I hope to show to an entry. The idea is to show green every one of the items are met and which not in red. I think together we can keep improving this list, ie, changing some items, adding or eliminating other non-critical items. Long Reasons: - Price out of the channel (breakout bullish) - M15 bullish candle - RSI pointing up (H1, H4, D1) - STO pointing up (H1, H4, D1) - TDI, RSI Price Line (green) crossed Trade Signal Line (red) up - TDI angle 12-2 - First or second candle after TDI cross - TDI below 68 - Away resistance on D1 - Away a hundred level - No high-impact news soon Short Reasons: - Price out of the channel (breakout bearish) - M15 bearish candle - RSI pointing down (H1, H4, D1) - STO pointing down (H1, H4, D1) - TDI, RSI Price Line (green) crossed Trade Signal Line (red) down - TDI angle 4-6 - First or second candle after TDI cross - TDI above 32 - Away support on D1 - Away a hundred level - No high-impact news soon Obviously going to be impossible that all items are green, but at least the majority or the most important should be green to execute an order.

--- 帖子 #17932 ---
Hello Delite, LG's broker uses American EST which means that their day starts at 05:00 London time which just happens to be 3 hours before London open so the original 4 hour breakout strategy is based on the build-up to London open. If you adjusted your channel indicator to start at 05:00 London time you would be on the same strategy as LG who has confirmed, as have several others, that London open gives some very good moves. Having said that, any period of consolidation, such as a build up to a major news release, may be traded in exactly the same way; look for at least 4 hour bars stuck within a channel and confirm a break-out on a lower time frame, ideally in the direction of the dominant trend. Hope this helps.

I've been observing both threads pretty closely, and it's easy to glimpse the frequent rays of brilliance that are so apparent here. But, I suspect your success is due in larger part to the way you actually manage your trades, rather than just the logic and simplicity of your setups and entry rules. A number of folks have asked about what to do once they're in the trade, and while I know this is not a discussion about money management, I think that ' trade management ' of a specific type of trade once a specific setup is observed, is really a significant factor in helping traders to enjoy greater successes while following any specific method, yours included. I wonder if you would be so kind as to -- at least occasionally -- tell us how much drawdown you experienced in a particular trade, and how much you were willing to accept in that trade, when you first entered. Not to tell us what to do, of course, but to tell us what YOU did, and why your trade was successful (or not). You know, where you pulled out and why, how it really went before you turned a profit, that sort of thing. This pretty much transcends money management, which is really an issue of risking certain percentages of funds against certain percentages of possible gain, certainly not for discussion here, nor what I'm suggesting. If we knew how your trades actually ran, we would then have a much better idea of what to expect in our own trades, and I think the majority of students here (we are ALL students, no?), would learn more and would be be most appreciative. I could be wrong, of course; I often am Be well, trade well, and thanks again for all your great efforts.
