--- 帖子 #17963 ---
Hi gang, it's been a while since I've posted here but I've been working LG's BO method for quite a few months now and thought I'd put my 2 cents worth in hoping that my experience with this method may help others ... First of all, this method is awesome and has allowed me to ramp up my trading like no other method I've tried so far (and I've tried quite a few). However I did have to make some "refinements" to LG's method because, quite frankly, my particular broker's start time did not work well with this method at all. But I could see the channels forming and the breakouts happening, they just weren't timed right with my broker's start of day which seems to be a recurring question from what I've seen asked here about that particular point of this method. So being hard headed and obstinate, and knowing that LG's BO method obviously works even though I wasn't having much success with it, I did some major research by going back through my charts. After some experimentation with different time sets, I finally came up with 2 different 4H timeframes that have bumped my win ratio from about 50% to a whopping 80%-90% by utilizing both an Asian breakout session and a European breakout session. Basically I trade the AUD, JPY and NZD major pairs during the Asian session, and the EUR, GBP, USD and CHF major pairs during the European session. I also took it a step further by paying a professional to improve on the daily line boxes indicator because the one referenced here will only work based on your broker's start of day. In other words, if you want your time frame to begin several hours before your broker's start of day, the lines will not appear on your chart until it hits your 00:00 mark, even though the inputs suggest that you can change this (at least that was my experience with this particular indicator). So I had it changed to allow me complete freedom to start the line boxes at whatever time on my chart that I choose. In addition, it gives me a pop up alert as well as an audible alert that I can customize when a qualifying entry candle appears on the 15 minute chart. For me this was money well spent as it's certainly helped me grab a lot more pips. Of course there's more to it than what I've written here, such as the size and quality of the qualifying candle, time of day when/if one appears, managing the trade appropriately, etc. and so forth. Personally, I'm more of a scalping type trader so I use the 15 minute chart to enter and manage my trades exclusively and don't even look at the H1 chart anymore (although the indicator does use the H1 chart to form the proper time frame for the breakouts). In other words, while we would like something to be "one size fits all," that's usually not the case ... at least that's what my own experiences have taught me, and this method is no exception. The base method is sound and works great, but for your particular needs and schedule, you may find that you have to make some tweaks and modifications to make it work for your particular situation and circumstances, especially given all the different variables involved for each individual trader. That's my 2 cents worth anyway ... take what you like from it and leave the rest ... hope this is helpful in some way ...

--- 帖子 #17974 ---
For stops, it's entirely up to you. SLs should generally be placed at the point where the market will have proven your analysis to be wrong. So for example, if you are trading a BO, place your stop at the place where your BO becomes invalid. For me, I tend to use nearby SR around the BO area. As for the price breaking in one direction and then the other.....well spotted It's something I've noticed too. As far as I understand it, big limit orders are often placed on either side of a consolidation range/low volume range, so when PA breaks off in one direction it triggers one set of limit orders, pushing the price in that direction. However, the PA can soon run out of steam, retrace and then trigger the limit orders on the other side of the range. Please bear in mind that what I've just written could be a load of complete rubbish though

In fact you don't really need to watch for any RSI. There is a simple logic, to make a trend line you need at least two points, where do you think the third touch will go? --- 帖子 #18268 ---
“SCHADENFREUDE" Winning traders are not the only ones who should fear the wrath of the market gods. Since trading occurs in a highly competitive environment, you’ll find that if you are doing well, sometimes other traders will be resentful of your success and root for you to fail. I’ll never forget one particularly rough stretch, when two other traders who I thought were my friends were unable to contain their glee at my recent losing streak. Prior to this lapse, I had been “tearing it up” and I guess my good fortune had rubbed them the wrong way. Did I get carried away while I was winning, and was I therefore “asking for it” when things went awry? Did I offend the market gods? Perhaps, but now I was paying the price. Now that the shoe was on the other foot, these two were smiling in my face like five-year-old children on Christmas morning. The Germans have a word for this—schadenfreude, which loosely translates to “pleasure taken from someone else’s misfortune.” Just as the market gods will deflate an egotistical trader, they also have disdain for those who revel in the losses of others. Don’t indulge in schadenfreude, or you may find yourself working in a restaurant or teaching high school—the fates that befell my two so called friends. If you root for the guy next to you to fail, you are likely to fail as well.” Forex patterns and probabilities – Ed Ponsi

Hi Hercs, sorry for my late reaction to your answer, I must have missed the forex factory email, telling me there had been a reaction to my question here. In the meantime, I've developed my own little system (without the Law Girl's Indicator, actually completely without the RSI) and was busy testing it the last couple of days. It seems that no system works for everyone and I guess that has to do with both trader - and 'system' confidence (if there was an absolute mathematical way to trade forex profitably, it would have long been found by now, with all these intelligent people searching for it...). The thing with indicators is, at best, they can only give a 'heads up', because of the lagging issue (they all repaint on the current candle, 'till it closes - and some repaint even after that, which is a nightmare for 'back testers'). What seems to work best for me is watching price to break through a moving average on the higher time frames (preferably D1) and then look for entries on the lower time frames (H4, H1 - I don't like moving lower than that, because that raises the 'gambling' factor). Of course, most indicators are based on moving averages, so in the end it all boils down to the same thing. Your answer was very thorough, not something one writes down in 5 seconds, so I really thank you for that. Good luck with your future trading! Ronald

Hi Nat1173, Here are 7 Steps basic to incorporate LG21's RSI 3 day period into your chart, but you can use for our Indicators or Expert EA as well: 1. Double-Click on the MetaEditor as shown: Attached Image (click to enlarge) 2. The MetaEditor comes up. Go to the Folder Icon, Double-Click, to find your LG 21 Indicator: Attached Image (click to enlarge) 3. Double-Click making the LG21 RSI 3 Day Indicator Folder: Attached Image (click to enlarge) 4. The Double-Cick the Compile Icon:: Attached Image (click to enlarge) 5. The under the Files Menu, Double-Click on SAVE AS making sure that you are taken to the Indicator Folder of your MQL 4 - Double Click and Close-Out of your MQL 4: Attached Image (click to enlarge) 6. Bring your MQL 4 back-up, pick the Navigator from the VIEW Menu and new LG21 Indicator should show up on the Right-Upper corner of your Chart: Attached Image (click to enlarge) 7. Then, note pick RSI's Charts that look hopeful based on LG21's Instructions found on Post #1: Attached Image (click to enlarge) Also note, that instead of having all the Currency Pairs on Charts, which can take a lot of RAM, slowing up your Computer CPU and using up too much RAM, you may want to do the following: 1. place a separate RSI chart setting from a Period from the default of 14 days to 3 days 2. Open the Indicator List, Edit your LG21 Indicator to "true" for having only one LG RSI 3 day which will pace your single RSI Indicator on the Right Upper Corner. 3. Or, you can also Chose "true" for placing the RSI into your RSI sub-window, found on lower portion of your Edited RSI Menu, then you are done. Finally, the early thread replies here also use a 200 Day Mean Average in the Functions Menu and have fun practicing to customizing your MQL Charts to gain further expertise by just doing. I hope that helps. Feel free to ask any other questions if you still are having problems setting-up LG21's Indicator. Happy Trading and Cheers !

--- 帖子 #18860 ---
Hi Andre, First of all, I am a relative Newbie also...just experimenting as I go and trying to find the best trades across all TF when the TDI-RSI(13) and RSI(3) point in a downward or upward direction - in general. The rest has to do with using your gut feeling, like an art, to make a final decision to stay in, get in or stay out of a trade that comes with experience. Also, during my experimentation, I try to keep the TFs separated with the use of separate Broker MT4 platforms. For example, for Daily and H4, I will use LGs to see that H4, D1 and W1 point in the same direction with the same happening with TDI-RSI(13). Here is FXCM using H4 TF with many signs of a Bearish trend: Attached Image (click to enlarge) After seeing the direction changing, especially reversing at the extremes of Fibonacci end zones (Fib 0 to 24% or 100% to 74%), I look for PA setups like IBs and PBs as noted above. When the Blue outer lines or the yellow star appears, there is a good chance that something will be happening soon like a Breakout (BO) with the trend or contra-trend, again best when the Trend is leaving the Sellers or Buyers Fibonacci Zones. Then, with the H4 or Daily Chart I take SL between 30 to 40 Pips and TP 60 to 80 Pips respectively to have a RR 2:1. The B is to Buy and S is Sell...but again, I think that you have to look at the whole picture first to take any trade, namely: 1) Trend or Direction 2) Key Levels or Zone like the Upper Sellers' Zone or Buyer's or the Fib 50% were their is a higher risk of New reversals 3) Price Action with H4 and D1, less powerful with H1 or lesser TFs. With my Oanda Demo account, I am trying scalping using only 5 Pips with or without a SL of 150 Pips or higher wth TFs 5min, 15 min, 30 min and H1, especially at the NY Open !!!!! My main interests are using only the H4 using my FxChoice account which has an ECN so that you are paying a set commission fee and avoiding trading with the MM account as with Oanda and FXCM, where the MM use your money to trade against you. Andre and others, please also study the TDI-RSI , PVSRA and Sonic R System Threads here to learn even more where I have studied, as well as looking at and downloading every "Forex Price Action" free Youtube videos i.e. especially from the authors "Forex4Noobs by Nick Bencino", "Nial Fuller", "Timon Wells" and "Walter Peters" with his "Naked Forex Trading" and his Book on the subject !

OK...Thank you Andre and others who get something out of my work on trying to become a real professional F/T trader ;-) I am going through last weeks H4 Charts to see which Pairs show excellent volatility with great trades even if I missed them. Currently, I realize that I have been over-trading - but, only to see which Charts and Pairs are more predictable. Also, I noticed that FXCM seems to have the best smallest spreads from my other Demo Brokers. Also, it seems that the best or safest trades seem when the Trending Candle crosses into or out of the Resistance-Seller Fibonacci Zones and the Support-Buyers Supportive Zone, and also after bouncing off or Reversing after the Fib 0%, Fib 50% and Fib 100% zone. However, major News like Conferences, will likely, break through the Fibonacci !00% and 0%, will likely Stop you out...so, best to sty out. In general, with the H4, the 2:1 RR, the best for me has been TP-80 SL-40 or TP-60 SL-30. The SL is the most important and should be below the previous lowest Candle with Long-Bullish trades and above the Highest Candle with a Short-Bearish Trades. In alphabetical order, here are my review of Charts from last week: Attached Image (click to enlarge)

If this is correct is basically saying that for an uptrend, the Daily candle has to be Up (close &gt; open or blue candle or green or whatever you want to call an up candle) and the Weekly candle has to be Up as well (close &gt; open or blue candle).
